items.title: As the Colorado River shrinks, calls to drain Lake Powell grow
items.summary_raw: The 27-year-long drought in the Southwestern U.S. — the longest dry period in the last 1,200 years — is taking a serious toll on the flow of the Colorado River. Climate change is shrinking the snowpack in Colorado’s Rocky Mountains, the source of roughly 80 percent of the river’s annual flow, and higher temperatures are melting the snowpack earlier in the year, which saps runoff in late summer and fall. Warmer weather is also increasing evaporation from the river’s 40 reservoirs, including its two largest — lakes Powell and Mead. Last month, Lake Powell, on the Utah-Arizona border, reached a record low, at less than 150 feet above dead pool, the point at which water can no longer flow through the Glen Canyon Dam’s bypass tubes to reach Lake Mead, behind Hoover Dam, 300 miles downstream. The low water levels reduced the generation of hydropower from both reservoirs, complicated how riverine ecosystems are managed, and slashed deliveries of water to the Lower Basin states of Arizona, California, and Nevada. Farmers are fallowing fields. Developers in some areas have paused housing construction for lack of guaranteed water supplies. And the Bureau of Reclamation has curtailed its “environmental flows” — releases of cold water from Powell — which is threatening protected fish and preventing the buildup of sandbars that provide habitat for wildlife in the Grand Canyon. No matter how the river is managed going forward, observers say, ecosystems both downstream and up will see…

items.title: These cranberry bogs come with a side of solar
items.summary_raw: It’s cranberry season in southeastern Massachusetts. At bogs throughout the region, growers are collecting the ruby-red berries destined for holiday cakes, juice bottles, and cans of jellied sauce. At two farms, however, the harvesting process looks a little different: Pickers are navigating equipment around metal poles in the shade of solar panels. The two bogs are the first in the country — perhaps the world — to grow cranberries beneath an operating solar installation. This fall marks the second season cranberries have been harvested from beneath the panels. “We are literally proving it can be done,” said Prateek Tare, co-founder and executive vice president of Distributed Energy Infrastructure. His company constructed the two projects — a 4.4-megawatt array paired with a 13.5-megawatt-hour battery in the town of Kingston, and a 1-MW solar array in neighboring Plymouth. Solar development is a major part of Massachusetts’ plan to reach net-zero carbon emissions by 2050. The state has offered solar incentives since 2001, evolving and expanding them over the decades to drive even more development. However, the question of where to site solar projects has become a major point of contention in the densely populated and heavily wooded state. Building on rooftops and parking lots in developed areas can increase costs and limit generation capacity. But proposals for arrays on previously undeveloped land often spark protests from locals worried about the character of their…

items.title: Příliš rychlé svlékání jako zkáza cudnosti: Vynález praktického zipu se stal nepřítelem počestných mravů
items.summary_raw: Whitcomb Judson si sice nechal v roce 1891 patentovat předchůdce moderního zipu na boty, jeho nespolehlivý systém háčků a oček se však nesetkal s úspěchem a sám vynálezce z něj nikdy nezbohatl. Skutečně funkční a spolehlivý systém protilehlých zoubků navrhl až švédsko-americký inženýr Gideon Sundbäck, jehož patent z roku 1917 položil základ moderního zdrhovadla. Zavedení zipu do běžného oděvního průmyslu zpočátku bránily morální předsudky z příliš rychlého svlékání, definitivní průlom však přinesly armádní zakázky a pařížská móda v meziválečném období.

Energysheds and the Urban Energy Transition: A Method for Assessing Spatial Imbalances in Energy Flow
items.summary_raw: Abstract Urban areas are facing the challenges of transitioning toward a low-carbon society as a response to climate change. However, the benefits and burdens of this energy transition are not evenly distributed across cities. To address this disparity, the concept of energy justice has emerged. The issue of urban energy justice can be understood as a manifestation of geographical energy disparities where energy-consuming regions enjoy significant benefits, while energy producing regions suffer from externalities. In this paper, we propose a method that utilizes the notion of “energyshed” to align city energy consumption with power plant energy generation, addressing geographical energy (im)balances. The proposed method maps the spatial supply–demand relationships between regions and power plants without relying on proprietary algorithms or territory-specific cutoff distances. Although spatial imbalance alone does not establish energy injustice, the resulting energysheds provide a diagnostic basis for identifying energy-generating regions that bear disproportionate burdens and for informing a fairer allocation of resources during the energy transition.

items.title: Mussels possess distinct vanadium and iron storage systems for fabricating metal-reinforced adhesive fibers
items.summary_raw: Mussels fashion a protein-based fibrous adhesive holdfast known as a byssus to tether themselves in marine habitats against crashing waves. The capacity of mussels to anchor securely is dependent on load-bearing protein-metal cross-links mediated by 3,4-dihydroxyphenylalanine (DOPA) residues coordinated to metal ions, which significantly enhance byssus mechanical properties (e.g., adhesive strength, abrasion resistance, toughness, self-healing capacity). However, the natural metal incorporation process during byssus formation remains poorly understood—a knowledge gap that limits the decades-old field of mussel-inspired materials from fulfilling its potential. Here, we investigate the natural byssus biofabrication system, the mussel foot, focusing specifically on iron and vanadium storage using a multilength scale ensemble of spectroscopic methods. Confocal Raman spectroscopy, synchrotron µ-X-ray fluorescence and µ-X-ray absorption spectroscopy, and scanning transmission electron microscopy with energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy studies indicate that these two metals occupy separate coordination environments: vanadium storage is DOPA-based, while iron is stored in ferritin-like structures. Lacking precedence, these findings indicate that mussels evolved a catechol-based metal storage system to specifically acquire and store what is typically considered a trace metal ion in biology, which they employ subsequently to mechanically reinforce protein-based glues and coatings…

items.title: Intuitive knowledge of object acoustics enables perceptual separation of physical variables from impact sounds
items.summary_raw: Upon hearing objects collide, humans can estimate physical attributes such as material and mass. Although the physics of sound generation is well established, the inverse problem that listeners solve—of inferring physical parameters from sound—remains poorly understood. Classical accounts posit the use of acoustic cues that correlate with physical variables but do not explain how humans might distinguish multiple concurrent physical causes. To study this problem, we measured impulse responses from hundreds of everyday objects, extracted their resonances, and used statistics of the resonances to build a probabilistic generative model of impact sounds. We then used the model to synthesize and manipulate stimuli for experiments measuring judgments of physical variables. Humans accurately judged object properties from collision sounds. However, when both of the colliding objects varied, performance was impaired if the distribution of object resonances deviated from those measured in real-world objects. The results suggest that humans have internalized the statistical regularities of real-world object acoustics, and use this knowledge to separate the acoustic contributions of the distinct objects in the world that give rise to sounds.

items.title: Simply aging
items.summary_raw: Biological aging is complex and resists any single mechanistic narrative. This article develops a conceptual framework for aging biology through a series of brief statements on central topics in the field, with the goal of discussing aging simply, directly and accessibly. The organizing principle is that aging is a default outcome of living: because biological processes are inherently imperfect, deleterious changes (the deleteriome) accumulate over time and progressively erode functional reserve. The deleteriome provides a unifying framework for molecular damage, regulatory drift, maladaptive remodeling, and system-level failure, without reducing aging to individual genes, pathways, compartments, hallmarks, or pathologies. Evolution does not program aging; it shapes maintenance and renewal systems that oppose this trajectory with limited fidelity and unavoidable trade-offs. Aging begins during development, following an early embryonic phase of rejuvenation. Modern biomarkers make biological age imperfectly but increasingly measurable. Biological age is heterogeneous across cells, organs, and systems, modifiable by interventions and environment, and in some contexts partially reversible or resettable, although aging itself is irreversible. This model links first principles of aging to measurement, intervention, and longer-term strategies, with the goal of clarifying how substantial longevity gains might be achieved, both within and beyond existing species-level constraints.

items.title: Correction for Pande et al., A lipid cue drives the subcellular localization of a self-inserting bacterial transmembrane protein
Bayesian knockoff filter for controlling false discovery rate
items.summary_raw: In many scientific fields, researchers are interested in discovering features with substantial effects on the response from a large number of candidate features while controlling the proportion of false discoveries. By incorporating the knockoff procedure in a Bayesian framework, we develop the Bayesian knockoff filter (BKF) for selecting important features. The BKF is built upon a tight upper bound for the posterior probability of the null hypothesis, which is derived under the Bayesian “flip-sign” property implied by our procedure. In contrast to the standard knockoff methods in the frequentist paradigm, we allow the knockoff variables to be generated in every iteration of the Markov chain Monte Carlo procedure, which removes the unwanted variability of the single-knockoff generation (knockoff is typically generated only once before the model fitting). Compared with multi-knockoffs, the BKF is more principled and natural in incorporating side information through prior distributions under a fully Bayesian framework. We further develop an e-value BKF approach to theoretically guarantee the frequentist false discovery rate (FDR) control. Numerical experiments on both synthetic and real data demonstrate the advantages of the BKF over existing knockoff methods and Bayesian variable selection approaches, i.e., the BKF possesses comparable power, yields a lower FDR and more stable selection sets.

items.title: Predicting key viral mutations from within-host deep sequencing data
items.summary_raw: Rapid SARS-CoV-2 evolution drives continuous epidemic waves, harming vaccine protection and exerting heavy burden to population health. Predicting virus evolution holds the key for current and future medical countermeasures against infectious diseases by allowing well-matching vaccines and timely epidemic response. However, due to its high genetic diversity, fast transmissibility and evolutionary rate, accurate and timely prediction of SARS-CoV-2 evolution remains a challenge. To address this, we developed a computational framework, Beth-2, to predict key mutations of SARS-CoV-2 through analyzing within-host viral genome deep sequencing data. We leveraged the early fitness signals of variants exhibited within-host and their fitness pattern between-host to infer the emerging mutations with fitness potential. In retrospective data validation, 98.6% of the key SARS-CoV-2 mutations on receptor binding domain could be detected by our model with a median lead time of 9 mo before they reached predominance at population level. Among the 26 prospectively predicted mutations, 69% of them exhibited significantly enhanced transmissibility and five showed significant immune escape from plasma of subjects who received COVID-19 mRNA vaccine collected 6 mo after the prediction time. The mutations predicted by Beth-2 that are functionally enhanced include F456L, the defining mutation of multiple current circulating lineages, including KP.3, NB.1.8.1, and XFG. items.title: Coupling of structural preordering and density fluctuation: A unified picture of nucleation in metallic glasses
items.summary_raw: Crystallization is ubiquitous in nature and technology, occurring in pharmaceuticals, biomacromolecules, polymers, metallurgy and glass formation. Yet how crystallization proceeds, particularly at its earliest stage, remains elusive. Studies on glass-forming liquids increasingly suggest that crystallization initiates in structurally preordered regions, with density fluctuations playing a secondary role, a view widely generalized from hard-sphere colloids. Here we show, across disordered metallic systems from pure elements and intermetallic compounds to glass-forming alloys, that density fluctuations and structural preordering emerge simultaneously during nucleation. This coupling reflects local atomic rearrangements in which free-volume reduction, denser packing, and bond-orientational order develop together. Our findings provide a physical basis for a unified nucleation framework for disordered materials.

items.title: Gastruloids reveal alternative morphogenetic routes for body-axis elongation with distinct cytoskeletal dependencies
items.summary_raw: Morphogenesis requires cells to integrate genetic and environmental information to pattern and shape tissues. Recent studies in vivo and in vitro have shown how alterations in environmental cues can induce alternative morphogenetic programs. However, what determines which morphogenetic strategy cells deploy in different environments remains unknown. Using gastruloids, a model for mammalian posterior body-axis elongation where environmental cues can be controlled in vitro, we show that substrate availability determines which force-generation strategy cells employ to build the body axis. In free-floating conditions, gastruloids self-assemble a single posterior body axis, presumably through cell–cell interactions. When plated on laminin, gastruloids acquire a flat morphology, break symmetry multiple times, and produce several independently elongating cell streams with anterior–posterior polarity through collective cell migration. On laminin, formin activity and focal adhesion-mediated traction are required for tissue elongation, yet both are functionally dispensable in free-floating conditions. Transcriptomic analysis shows that formin inhibition blocks elongation on laminin without any detectable transcriptional changes, indicating that these cytoskeletal components play primarily a mechanical role that is only required when cells engage a substrate. Furthermore, laminin biases cells toward posterior migratory fates while preserving similar Hox expression. Together, these…

items.title: Methionine restriction inhibits EZH2-mediated GSDMD methylation to promote pyroptosis in prostate cancer
items.summary_raw: EZH2 is frequently overexpressed in solid tumors, yet the clinical efficacy of its inhibitors remains limited, highlighting an urgent need to elucidate their cytotoxic mechanisms. Here, we identify EZH2 as a posttranslational suppressor of pyroptosis through direct methylation of GSDMD. We revealed that EZH2 inhibition triggered GSDMD-dependent pyroptosis in prostate cancer cells. Clinical specimens showed an inverse correlation between EZH2 levels and cleaved GSDMD (GSDMD N-terminal, GSDMD-N) levels, reinforcing its role as a negative regulator of GSDMD activation. Mechanistically, EZH2 methylated GSDMD at lysine 168, thereby blocking caspase-1-mediated cleavage and suppressing its activation. Notably, methionine deprivation overcame this blockade and combined with the EZH2 inhibitor GSK126 to enhance pyroptosis and suppress tumor growth in vivo. These findings establish the methionine–EZH2–GSDMD axis as an epigenetic-metabolic hub controlling pyroptosis via posttranslational regulation, providing a mechanistic rationale for co-targeting methionine metabolism and EZH2 in prostate cancer therapy.

items.title: Evolutionary dynamics of collective behavior across the tree of ray-finned fishes
items.summary_raw: Trait evolution and lineage diversification are thought to be driven by selection on the phenotypes of individuals. However, many important phenotypes are only manifested when individuals interact. Collective behavior is one such phenotype. During collective behavior, interactions among individuals lead to emergent group-level phenotypes that can govern individual fitness. Yet, whether collective behaviors exhibit similar patterns of trait evolution to individual traits and whether these group phenotypes have influenced macroevolutionary diversification is unknown. In ray-finned fishes, the most species-rich of all vertebrate classes, many species exhibit striking displays of collective behavior in the form of collective movement. Here, we use state-of-the-art machine learning methods for text and image analysis to quantify collective movement phenotypes for 2,839 Actinopterygian fishes, comprising nearly 10% of all extant species. We find that collective movement is highly evolutionarily stable in some clades and extremely labile in others, exhibiting over 300 evolutionary transitions. Consistent with theoretical predictions, collective movement is associated with more patchy diets and higher predation pressure. Finally, we find that the evolution of collective movement coincides with an increase in net macroevolutionary diversification rate. Our analyses reveal that collective behavior is deeply intertwined with ecological and evolutionary dynamics across a vast…

items.title: Respiratory phase orchestrates human olfactory cortical dynamics
items.summary_raw: Olfaction is fundamental to perception, memory, and emotion, yet the neural basis of human odor processing remains poorly understood. We demonstrate that odor-evoked brain activity is organized by respiratory phase—not absolute time—revealing that natural breathing structures olfactory cortical dynamics. Using simultaneous nasal respiration and electroencephalography recordings in 17 participants, we delivered naturalistic odors (peppermint, oregano, and grapefruit) synchronized to individual breathing cycles. Odor presentation elicited respiratory phase-locked event-related spectral perturbations (RPL-ERSPs) in frontal and temporal regions, emerging during the first breath after stimulus onset. The most discriminative neural signatures were theta-band activity during inhalation and alpha-band activity during exhalation, patterns that were obscured in traditional time-locked analyses due to natural variability in breath duration. Leave-one-subject-out cross-validation of RPL-ERSPs achieved reliable odor detection (peppermint: AUC = 0.79; oregano: AUC = 0.67; grapefruit: AUC = 0.62), establishing that phase-locked features generalize across individuals. To connect neural responses to perceptual experience without relying on odor naming-which can be disproportionately impaired in some populations-we quantified odor recognition using free-response descriptions scored with a semantic-similarity approach. Behavioral recognition strength paralleled the neural decoding hierarchy…

items.title: Diffusion in a d -dimensional rough potential
items.summary_raw: The prediction of diffusion in solids is necessary to understand the microstructure evolution in materials out of equilibrium. Although one can reasonably predict diffusive transport coefficients using atomistic methods, these approaches can be very computationally expensive. In this work, we develop an analytical model for the diffusivity in a noisy solid solution in an arbitrary number of dimensions ( d ) using a mean first passage time analysis. We observe that roughness always decreases the diffusivity, aligning with sluggish diffusion theories in concentrated alloys, finding that an increase in diffusivity induced by alloying elements must be due to a decrease in the average activation energy, not to the noise. These analytical results are then compared with kinetic Monte Carlo simulations, which are in good quantitative agreement with the simulation data for d ≤ 5, and excellent quantitative agreement for d ≤ 3. This generalization to arbitrary dimensions has been elusive to the community since Zwanzig [R. Zwanzig, Proc. Natl. Acad. Sci. U.S.A. 85 , 2029–2030 (1988)] published his seminal work on one-dimensional systems.

items.title: Ochrana ozonové vrstvy je věcí mezinárodní spolupráce, kde ČR hraje důležitou roli
items.summary_raw: Dne 5. listopadu 2026 se v Kigali ve Rwandě v rámci 38. zasedání smluvních stran Montrealského protokolu (MOP38) uskutečnil kulatý stůl segmentu na vysoké úrovni věnovaný desátému výročí přijetí Kigalského dodatku. Diskuse pod názvem „Ten Years of the Kigali Amendment: Political Leadership, Achievements and Ways Forward“ se zaměřila na zhodnocení dosavadních výsledků při snižování spotřeby částečně fluorovaných uhlovodíků (HFC), sdílení národních zkušeností a stanovení priorit pro další období. Účastníci zdůraznili, že úspěšná implementace Kigalského dodatku vyžaduje propojení klimatických politik s energetickou účinností, podporu inovací, rozvoj odborných kapacit a intenzivní mezinárodní spolupráci. Za Českou republiku vystoupil náměstek ministra životního prostředí Ivo Marcin, který představil zkušenosti České republiky a Evropské unie s postupným omezováním HFC a upozornil na význam odborného vzdělávání, certifikace techniků, boje proti nelegálnímu obchodu s regulovanými látkami, mezinárodní spolupráce, výzkumu, prosazování opatření a výměny zkušeností jako klíčových předpokladů pro dosažení klimatických cílů Kigalského dodatku v nadcházejícím desetiletí.

items.title: Glaciers around the world are endangered — but no two are alike
items.summary_raw: Part of my work as a geographer and glacier scientist involves traveling around the world. Literally. Several times a year, I join expeditions, traversing continents and oceans, sometimes half the planet, in mere days. I’ve visited glaciers in some startling places — like Uganda’s Stanley Glacier, where ice retreat influences human health and malaria outbreaks. Or Iceland’s Breiðamerkurjökull, where glacier change is exacerbating the ice-breaking pressures of global tourism . Or South Georgia’s Heaney Glacier, where ice retreat has provided expansive real estate for one of the largest King penguin colonies on Earth. My job is to translate the landscape: how oceans move nutrients pole to pole; why one mountain might support snow but another does not; how glaciers shape societies. I’ll own it’s a peculiar way to experience the world. From 30,000 feet, borders fall away. Trees become forests become systems become a living planet. I see connections everywhere. But that view from 30,000 feet, while striking, can miss much of what’s unfolding below at the individual level — the people, the lives, the histories. Glaciers, I think, suffer from this same problem of perspective. We tend to see them from a great distance, as a single global story. They’re tallied together: Some 275,000 individual glaciers remain worldwide . They’re measured together: how quickly they are shrinking, how much they impact sea level change, how long before they are gone. How many of them already are. But…

items.title: Plastic pollution is putting an old legal doctrine to a new test
items.summary_raw: Plastic pollution blights the streets, beaches, parks, and lawns of Baltimore. A significant amount of that litter bears the circular red-and-blue Pepsi logo or the flowing white script of Coca-Cola’s branding. But, legally speaking, none of that rubbish is Pepsi’s fault. Or Coke’s. That’s what a Baltimore city circuit court judge ruled this summer following a legal battle in which the city and county of Baltimore sought money from PepsiCo, Coca-Cola , and others to clean up plastic pollution. Companies “conducting lawful activities,” wrote Judge Audrey J.S. Carrión, referring to the sale of single-use plastics, “should not be held liable under public nuisance claims because others are misusing the products in an unlawful manner.” In other words, plastic pollution is a problem of consumer behavior, not corporate irresponsibility. As far as the state’s public nuisance law is concerned, a company’s liability ends at the point of sale. Similar reasoning scuttled a public nuisance lawsuit the state of New York filed against PepsiCo and Frito-Lay and has arisen in similar litigation from Missouri to California . As environmental advocates and governments continue to develop this legal theory, those setbacks raise a fundamental question: When does a company’s responsibility for its products end? And can public nuisance laws succeed in making polluters pay? The notion of public nuisance dates to 13th-century English common law and traditionally applied to violations of rights…

items.title: School Climate and Opportunities for Physics Learning in Resource-Constrained Schools
items.source_name: International Journal on Research in STEM Education
items.summary_raw: This descriptive mixed-methods case study examined how school-climate conditions were perceived and observed to shape opportunities for learning Physics in a Community Day Secondary School in Area 25, Lilongwe, Malawi. The study involved 43 participants: 40 students, two Physics teachers and one head teacher. Student questionnaire responses were summarised using frequencies and percentages (n = 40), while the research report also drew on school observations and focus-group discussions. A 25-item, four-response-option questionnaire covered infrastructure, learning resources, safety, rules and regulations, and interpersonal relationships. In the four reported quantitative figures, disagreement response categories comprised the plotted totals for infrastructure (22/40, 55%), learning resources (25/40, 62.5%) and safety (30/40, 75%), whereas agreement categories comprised the plotted total for interpersonal relationships (27/40, 67.5%). For school rules and regulations, the reported distribution comprised 28 agreement-category responses (70%) and 12 disagreement-category responses (30%). These results describe respondents' perceptions of school conditions and do not demonstrate a statistically significant effect on Physics achievement. The qualitative account described constraints on practical work, independent study and classroom interaction, and identified school rules and management as relevant contextual conditions. The study did not report analysed individual Physics test…

items.title: Decomposition of carbon emission drivers and urban typology in the Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area: implications for regional environmental management
items.summary_raw: The Guangdong–Hong Kong–Macao Greater Bay Area is marked by pronounced urban heterogeneity, so that a uniform account of its carbon emission drivers is unlikely to hold. Using panel data for 11 cities from 2015 to 2023, this study applies the Generalized Divisia Index Method to decompose eight drivers of emission change and to classify the cities by their factor contribution structures. Economic growth (G) and output carbon intensity (CI) are the largest positive and negative contributors in ten of the eleven cities (mean G = +19.18%, mean CI = −9.94%), the exception being Macao. An exploratory Ward clustering of the four most variable factors, cross-validated against k-means, distinguishes four types of driving structure—carbon-intensity suppression, economic-scale driven, energy-scale expansion, and a specialized service-structure type (Macao); an innovation index combining research and development (R&D) intensity and patent density varies independently of these types. Decoupling is likewise uneven, ranging from strong decoupling in three cities (Foshan, Zhongshan and Hong Kong; Tapio elasticity t = −0.152 to −0.437) to weak decoupling in six (0.133 ≤ t ≤ 0.462) and expansive coupling in Huizhou and Macao. Per-capita emissions and energy-structure carbon intensity show marked dispersion. These findings inform a three-tiered policy discussion—differentiated measures, collaborative governance, and data support—for coordinated low-carbon governance in urban agglomerations.

items.title: Climate justice, fossil fuel lock-ins and opportunities
items.source_name: International Environmental Agreements Politics Law and Economics
items.summary_raw: Abstract More than thirty years after the adoption of the UN Convention on Climate Change, fossil fuel still provides 80% of the world’s total energy consumption. The escalation in renewables makes a dent in fossil fuel use, but cannot, in itself, address the climate problem. Hence, this paper asks: What blocks the transition away from fossil fuel and what opportunities are there to phase out fossil fuel? This paper integrates the results of a five-year project discussed and debated during the Climate Change and Fossil Fuels (CLIFF) Conference in Amsterdam in November 2025. It argues that the focus on politically feasible, efficient, short-term win–win solutions has exacerbated the global ability to manage climate change; and that without a just approach the climate problem cannot be addressed. Using the frame of climate system justice and lock-in, the paper identifies ten overlapping systemic lock-ins (profitability, discursive, legal, investment, economic/fiscal, infrastructural, labour, behavioural, political, professional) that operate at multiple levels of governance and across different domains. The paper identifies different strategies to unlock these different lock-ins across the different domains. Unlocking the lock-ins requires scientists, social movements and large-scale social and political mobilization to support these ideas as they clearly go against the business-as-usual and incremental policy processes. These ideas can be supported by the judiciary which…

items.title: Proč mohou ranní mrazíky v těchto dnech ohrozit některé rostliny?

items.title: The Use, Environmental Knowledge and Climate Change Attitudes of Australian Nurses and Midwives Regarding Nitrous Oxide
items.summary_raw: ABSTRACT Aim The aim of this research was to investigate the clinical use of nitrous oxide among Australian nurses and midwives, assess their pharmacological knowledge of the gas, determine their awareness of its environmental effects and evaluate their broader attitudes toward climate change. Background Balancing clinical efficacy with environmental sustainability is an emerging priority in acute pain management. While nitrous oxide offers rapid, reversible analgesia, its substantial ecological footprint as a greenhouse gas cannot be ignored. Nurses and midwives are well‐positioned to drive sustainable analgesic practices, yet their current utilisation and awareness of these environmental impacts require further investigation. Design A cross‐sectional survey of nurses and midwives practising in Australia. Method Australian nurses and midwives who have administered nitrous oxide as part of patient management were invited to complete a 62‐item survey. Quantitative data were analysed using descriptive statistics and qualitative responses were thematically analysed. Results Responses from 446 respondents were analysed. Pharmacological knowledge of nitrous oxide was low (median 28.6%), as was awareness of its environmental impact (median 28.6%). Respondents aged 40 and under had lower awareness of nitrous oxide's impact on climate (28.6% vs. 42.9%). Climate change beliefs and intentions were high (both 80.0%). Awareness of nitrous oxide's environmental impact explained 79% of…

items.title: Assessment of the knowledge, attitude, and practices of the people on dengue fever and malaria in the central Nepal
items.summary_raw: Dengue and malaria remain critical, resurgent public health challenges in Nepal. This study assessed the knowledge, attitudes, and practices (KAP) regarding these mosquito-borne diseases among 130 households in Hetauda Sub-Metropolitan City, Makawanpur. Utilizing a questionnaire-based survey, the study found that 28% of respondents self-reported a household history of dengue within the past year often cluster-infecting multiple family members while only 1% self-reported history of malaria. Participants demonstrated high knowledge regarding dengue vectors (87%) and prevention (72%), alongside strong confidence (97%) in their chosen treatment strategies. Conversely, knowledge regarding malaria transmission was remarkably low (13%). While community attitudes and knowledge favor dengue prevention, critical gaps persist regarding malaria. These findings underscore the need for targeted, community-level educational interventions and intensified vector control programs to mitigate transmission risks and strengthen regional public health resilience.

items.title: Public attitudes and actions towards renewable energy in the EU countries: A micro-level analysis during the energy crisis
items.summary_raw: Background: Despite ambitious EU decarbonization targets, household adoption of renewable energy (RE) remains uneven, particularly during systemic energy price shocks.Methods: Using Flash Eurobarometer microdata ($N \approx 23,000$) spanning 27 EU countries linked with regional macro indicators, we combine binary logistic regression with machine learning classifiers (random forests and decision trees) to evaluate adoption drivers and behavioural discrepancies.Results: We identify both a significant attitude–behaviour gap and an inverse attitude–behaviour gap in specific demographic segments. Machine learning feature importance confirms that structural factors (homeownership, regional climate requirements) and capital constraints strongly dominate psychological readiness in determining realized RE investments.Conclusions & Policy: Rising energy prices heighten adoption interest but exacerbate disparities. Effective decarbonization policy requires tenure-specific incentives (targeting renters), targeted upfront subsidies for low-income and elderly households, and place-based financial support for regions facing disproportionate energy burdens.

items.title: Challenges and opportunities in ensuring clean and affordable energy in Sub-Saharan Africa
items.summary_raw: Over the past decade, Sub-Saharan Africa (SSA) has made notable progress in advancing Sustainable Development Goal 7 (SDG 7); yet, achieving universal access to clean and affordable energy remains a pressing challenge. The existing literature treats SSA as a homogeneous region, and the implementation challenges and opportunities unique to sub-regions are underexplored. This study explores both the challenges and opportunities for advancing SDG 7 across sub-regions of SSA using World Bank datasets. It employs Pareto chart analysis to identify priorities from sub-regions, country levels, and core components of SDG 7. Pareto chart analysis is a powerful quality analysis tool that provides pathways for strategic interventions. Importantly, conventional indicators of electricity or clean cooking fail to capture adequacy and sustainability. This study uses final energy consumption per person as an energy poverty index. Findings highlight the strategic importance of expanding electricity access in Central Africa and accelerating clean cooking adoption in all sub-regions, with urgent interventions required in Nigeria (3.1 kWh/person/year), Ethiopia (4.5 kWh/person/year), and the Democratic Republic of Congo (4.6 kWh/person/year). Nigeria and Ethiopia account for 30% and 29.4% of the regional electricity and clean cooking energy deficits, respectively, underscoring their pivotal role in shaping progress. Therefore, prioritized and targeted interventions are essential for accelerating…

items.title: Life aspirations, risk-benefit perceptions, and public acceptance of candidate gerotherapeutic medications: a preregistered national survey in Singapore
items.summary_raw: Background Despite growing interest in gerotherapeutic medications, research on public acceptance has relied predominantly on Western convenience samples and has not tested integrated models linking motivational goals to risk-benefit perceptions. Drawing on intrinsic and extrinsic life goals and secondary risk theory, this study addresses these gaps by examining willingness among Singapore residents to take drugs like metformin for health optimization. Methods Data came from a preregistered, nationally representative survey of 2,003 Singapore adults. Structural equation modeling tested relationships among life aspirations, desired lifespan, risk-benefit perceptions, and willingness to take health optimization medications. Results Most respondents expressed a preference for living 60–90 years in optimal health, and about one-third indicated willingness to use health optimization medications. Life aspirations were positively associated with desired lifespan ( R 2 = 0.04), but desired lifespan was unrelated to medication willingness. In contrast, willingness was positively related to worry about chronic disease, perceived efficacy, and perceived societal costs and negatively related to perceived health risks and perceived ethical costs ( R 2 = 0.39). Conclusion These findings suggest that motivational goals and risk-benefit perceptions are independent pathways to medication willingness. They highlight the need for communicating efficacy evidence while addressing safety and…

items.title: Eco-Hype or Eco-Hope?
items.source_name: The International Journal of Social Sustainability in Economic Social and Cultural Context
items.summary_raw: The Olympic Games claim to be exemplars of sustainability, aiming to inspire sustainable futures around the world. The organizers positioned Paris 2024 as the most sustainable Games ever, promising a 50% reduction in carbon emissions compared to prior editions. The issue of greenwashing—projecting a picture of environmental responsibility without taking significant action—becomes pertinent and pressing in this situation. Because of the Games’ enormous popularity, any sustainability narrative that is adopted has a worldwide audience and can either support or contradict public views of environmental responsibility. Therefore, it is necessary to consider if the Paris Olympics indeed signify a radical change in the way that these kinds of events are planned and carried out, or if they are just an example of a more advanced kind of greenwashing. In light of this, a crucial research question arises: Was Paris’ goal to create a new standard truly intended, or was it just excellent advertising covering up unpleasant facts? This study pursued its objective by conducting a two-round Delphi survey that included a diverse range of professional expertise from the field of sports and sponsorship, among others in order to enhance the multi-faceted examination of sustainability and public opinion. In addition to shedding light on the veracity of Paris 2024’s sustainability claims, the present study advances our knowledge of how environmental narratives are created, disseminated, and…

items.title: МОВНІ СТРАТЕГІЇ ВПЛИВУ В СУЧАСНОМУ АНГЛОМОВНОМУ МЕДІАДИСКУРСІ
items.summary_raw: Статтю присвячено дослідженню мовних стратегій впливу в сучасному англомовному медіадискурсі. Актуальність дослідження зумовлена посиленням ролі засобів масової інформації та цифрових медіа у формуванні громадської думки, інтерпретації суспільно значущих подій і впливі на сприйняття інформації аудиторією. Метою статті є вивчення особливостей реалізації мовних стратегій впливу в сучасному англомоному медіадискурсі та визначення мовних засобів, за допомогою яких здійснюється переконувальний вплив на реципієнта. Теоретичну основу дослідження становлять положення критичного дискурс-аналізу, прагмалінгвістики, медіалінгвістики, теорії фреймування та сучасних досліджень мовного впливу. Емпіричний матеріал представлено англомовними медіатекстами провідних міжнародних інформаційних видань Reuters та The Guardian, опублікованими у 2024–2025 роках. У дослідженні застосовано метод суцільної вибірки, дискурс-аналіз, описовий, контекстуально-інтерпретаційний та прагмалінгвістичний методи аналізу. У результаті аналізу запропоновано класифікацію найбільш репрезентативних мовних стратегій впливу, що функціонують у сучасному англомовному медіадискурсі. Виокремлено сім стратегій: звернення до авторитетного джерела, емоційне фреймування, статистичне переконання, метафоричне фреймування, вираження впевненості та обов’язковості, залучення аудиторії та протиставлення. Встановлено, що їх реалізація забезпечується комплексом лексичних, граматичних, стилістичних і прагматичних засобів, які…

items.title: The impact of the Swiss CO2 levy on residential heating emissions and energy demand
items.summary_raw: This paper assesses the impact of the Swiss CO 2 levy on residential heating energy demand and the associated CO 2 emissions. Using the synthetic control method, the results show that the levy led to an average annual reduction in CO 2 emissions of 6.5% during the post-treatment period (2008–2021), corresponding to a decrease of 0.1 metric tons of CO 2 per capita per year. Furthermore, the empirically estimated price elasticities for heating oil indicate that the short-run elasticity for the retail price is − 0.044 , while the elasticity for the CO 2 levy is − 0.997 , demonstrating that consumers respond more strongly to policy-induced price changes than to market-driven price changes. In the long run, these elasticities increase to − 0.054 (retail price) and − 1.215 (levy), highlighting that over time, households adjust their demand more significantly in response to sustained price changes. A similar pattern is observed for natural gas, with short-run elasticities of − 0.216 (retail) and − 0.547 (levy), increasing to − 0.552 and − 1.396 , respectively, in the long run. These findings are consistent with the Swiss CO 2 levy contributing to lower fossil-fuel demand and building-sector emissions, although the SCM inference does not reach conventional levels of statistical significance. The results underline the importance of policy-induced price instruments and highlight the necessity of high levy rates to ensure a measurable impact on consumption behavior.

items.title: Climate change adaptation practices in fruit-irrigated agriculture: the role of nudging in farmers’ adoption decisions
items.summary_raw: Purpose This study analyses farmers’ responses to economic incentives and behavioural nudges for promoting adoption of water and soil conservation practices, identifying which are most effective. Design/methodology/approach A discrete choice experiment was conducted with irrigated fruit farmers, focusing on three climate change adaptation agricultural practices (subsurface irrigation, regulated deficit irrigation and cover crops) combined with a monetary incentive (framed as subsidy or discount) and additional services replicating the most common characteristics of nudges. Four categories of nudges are evaluated: facilitators (advisory mobile apps), confrontational (apps showcasing the negative effects of not adopting the water-saving practices), social norms (apps benchmarking individual performance against peers) and reinforcement (public recognition and certifications). The analysis incorporates preference heterogeneity based on farmers’ attitudes to nudging. Findings Results show that both monetary incentives and nudges increase farmers’ willingness to adopt subsurface irrigation, regulated deficit irrigation and cover crops. Apps tackling behavioural biases can reduce the need for compensation. Confrontational nudges are most effective; facilitation nudges show heterogeneous response and social influence and signalling nudges generate undefined responses. Therefore, there is potential to reduce the overall cost of promoting biodiversity and water-saving technology…

items.title: Public Priorities Between Worker Protection and Renewable Power in the AI Transition: Evidence From a Novel Randomized Survey Experiment
items.summary_raw: ABSTRACT The development of artificial intelligence (AI) creates simultaneous fiscal pressures on welfare provision and energy infrastructure, requiring governments to support workers exposed to technological displacement while also financing the low‐carbon energy generation needed by expanding data‐centre systems. This article investigates how citizens allocate priority between the social policy and energy demands generated by AI, and the political conflicts that may arise around it, using a survey experiment fielded in 2025 in six European countries (France, Germany, Italy, Poland, Spain and the United Kingdom). Findings show that European public opinion favours an equal allocation of resources between social protection for workers negatively affected by AI and investments in renewable energy for data centres. Although economic insecurity raises support for welfare spending, partisan identity drives the greatest divide: Voters of all mainstream parties favour investment in renewable energy, whereas only radical left and radical right voters prefer an even allocation of resources between the two policy domains. Variation in the type of social policy proposed—income support or training—yields only a weak and blurred effect on public preferences.

items.title: A Value–Belief–Norm (VBN) Approach to Visitor Attitudes Toward Carbon Offsetting in Protected Areas
items.summary_raw: The tourism industry is recognized as a major contributor to greenhouse gas emissions, significantly advancing climate change. Carbon offsetting is often suggested as an ancillary approach to alleviate or counterbalance inevitable emissions generated by tourism activities; nevertheless, what is the public impression of this measure? When are they expected to engage in it? This study employing the Value–Belief–Norm theory (VBN) mainly aims to investigate the influence of visitors’ value orientations on their overall perceptions regarding carbon offsetting within the leisure context of protected-area visitation—a realm where leisure pursuits represent a considerable contributor to carbon emissions. A total of 517 protected-area visitors in Spain and 383 in the Netherlands participated in the study. Results indicate that individuals who prioritize biospheric and altruistic values are more likely to exhibit robust support for carbon offsetting initiatives in protected areas, demonstrating the importance of fundamental value orientations in shaping pro-environmental attitudes. In addition, the findings stress human accountability for climate repercussions and reveal offsetting alternatives as ethically justifiable and effectively gratifying. The study offers governance-related implications, indicating that harmonizing carbon offsetting programs with fundamental societal principles may bolster the perceived legitimacy of offsetting initiatives, foster visitor involvement, and lead…

items.title: Adoption and Impact of Climate-Smart Technologies on Agrifood Systems in Vihiga County, Kenya
items.source_name: African Journal of Climate Change and Resource Sustainability
items.summary_raw: Agrifood systems in sub-Saharan Africa face significant challenges from climate change, threatening food security and rural livelihoods. Climate-smart technologies (CSTs) offer a viable way to strengthen resilience, productivity, and sustainability in smallholder farming systems. This study examines the adoption and impact of CSTs in Vihiga County, a high-potential agricultural region in western Kenya with small landholdings and high vulnerability to climate variability. Using a mixed-methods approach, the study assesses the extent of CST adoption, key drivers and barriers, and socio-economic benefits among smallholder farmers. Primary data were collected through household surveys (n=383), focus group discussions (n=5), and key informant interviews (n=15) with farmers, extension officers, and policymakers. Findings indicate that practices such as conservation agriculture (25%), agroforestry (15%), drought-resistant crop varieties (60%), and integrated soil fertility management have contributed to improved yields, reduced greenhouse gas emissions, and enhanced climate adaptation. However, adoption remains constrained by limited access to finance, inadequate extension services, and fragmented land ownership. The study highlights the role of policy support, capacity building, and public-private partnerships in scaling up CSTs for sustainable agrifood transformation. By aligning local practices with Kenya's Climate-Smart Agriculture Strategy, Vihiga County can serve as a model…

items.title: Investigating a Two-Dimensional Carbon Cost Control Method Based on “Carbon Flow–Value Flow”
items.summary_raw: Achieving carbon peaking and carbon neutrality requires coordinated action across macro, meso, and micro levels. For Chinese firms, reducing carbon emissions and controlling carbon costs are important challenges. Using Nanjing Iron and Steel Co., Ltd. (NJ Steel) as a case, this study proposes a two-dimensional “carbon flow–value flow” cost control method that traces carbon-containing material and energy inputs, transformation, and emissions through steel production, maps these flows to internal resource transfer costs and external environmental damage costs, and identifies process-level control points and optimization measures. Carbon flow analysis indicated that coking, ironmaking, and steelmaking are high-emission processes. Value flow analysis showed that these processes also incur high carbon costs and are therefore key control points. Within the process-level quantitative boundary and simulated optimization scenarios, internal resource transfer costs and external environmental damage costs were RMB 1,176 million and RMB 1,442 million lower than baseline, respectively. After accounting for technical retrofit investment and key parameter uncertainty, carbon cost reductions ranged from approximately RMB 1,879 million to RMB 3,941 million across the sensitivity scenarios. The findings provide practical guidance for enterprises seeking to strengthen carbon emissions management, optimize carbon cost control, and advance their low-carbon transition.

items.title: Atypical phenylalanine ammonia-lyases that enhance phenylpropanoid production in plants
items.summary_raw: Plants synthesize diverse phenylpropanoids, which provide us essential medicine, nutrients, and biomaterials while also acting as a major global carbon sink. Phenylpropanoids are primarily derived from L-phenylalanine (Phe) via Phe ammonia-lyase (PAL), a highly regulated enzymatic activity that limits phenylpropanoid production. However, it remains poorly understood how different plant species regulate PAL enzymes. Phylogeny-guided biochemical screening uncovered complex and diverse feedback regulation of PAL enzymes from 14 different plant species. This screening found a previously uncharacterized PAL clade, namely PALnc (from noncanonical), with some members exhibiting feedback activation by p -coumaric acid, caffeic acid, and 4-hydroxyphenylpyruvic acid in vitro. Transient expression of two PALnc genes, from Elaeis guineensis ( EgPALnc ) and Piper methysticum ( PmPALnc2 ), in Nicotiana benthamiana leaves elevated phenylpropanoid content, supported by the high in planta stability of PALnc proteins compared to canonical PALs. Whereas overexpression of Arabidopsis thaliana PAL1 ( AtPAL1 ) in stable Arabidopsis transgenic lines resulted in very low accumulation of AtPAL1 protein and minor metabolic effects, introduction of EgPALnc rendered high content of EgPALnc protein and hyperaccumulation of hydroxycinnamates derivatives. Our findings uncover a previously overlooked diversity in the regulation of the entry step of phenylpropanoid biosynthesis across various plants and…

items.title: Dysregulation of mechanosensing signaling in monocytes of patients with systemic sclerosis is associated with skin inflammation
items.summary_raw: Systemic sclerosis (SSc) is a severe autoimmune connective tissue disease characterized by immune dysregulation and progressive fibrosis of the skin and internal organs, resulting in substantial organ dysfunction and increased mortality. Fibrosis is driven in part by infiltration of immune cells, including monocytes that become activated within fibrotic tissue. However, how the mechanical properties of fibrotic skin regulate their function remains poorly understood. Here, we demonstrate that increased stiffness activates human monocytes through mechanosensing. Reanalysis of single cell RNA sequencing datasets revealed that skin infiltrating monocytes exhibit heightened inflammatory signatures as compared to circulating counterparts, with further amplification in SSc. Using collagen-coated hydrogels modeling physiological and fibrotic stiffness, we show that increased stiffness enhances CD86 expression, and broadly upregulates inflammatory transcriptional programs in human monocytes. Mechanistically, stiffness-driven activation was associated with chromatin remodeling and epigenetic reprogramming, identifying the transcription factor Specificity Protein 1 (SP1) as a central regulator. CRISPR–Cas9-mediated disruption or pharmacologic inhibition of SP1 significantly attenuated stiffness- induced inflammatory gene expression, whereas we found no evidence for involvement of the canonical YAP/TAZ–TEAD axis, and pharmacological modulation of PIEZO1 neither reproduced nor blocked…

items.title: Polarized twin walls in a halide perovskite
items.summary_raw: Halide perovskites have emerged as promising materials for next-generation photovoltaics, laser sources, and X-ray detectors. There is intense debate as to whether some photoactive halide perovskites exhibit ferroelectric behavior and whether it might be possible to utilize the bulk photovoltaic effect to enhance the performance of halide perovskite solar cells. Here, using low-dose scanning transmission electron microscopy, we identify ferroelastic twin walls in vapor-deposited CsPbI 3 thin films, parallel to {110} and {112}. Remarkably, despite CsPbI 3 being centrosymmetric and nonpolar, we observe directly that Pb atoms shift at {110} twin walls driving a local ferroelectric-like polarization. These polar twin walls form an intrinsic array of nanoscale interfaces, spaced ~30 to 50 nm apart, embedded within the nonpolar perovskite lattice. In contrast, {112} twin walls do not show a polar displacement of Pb but strongly suppress octahedral tilt and off-center Cs atom displacements, revealing a different untapped structural degree of freedom. These findings reveal previously hidden nanoscale polarization in halide perovskite semiconductors, opening opportunities for enhanced conductivity and photovoltaic behavior through domain wall engineering.

items.title: Trust as a hidden driver of epidemic-relevant behavior: Institution- and behavior-specific associations across 20 national survey waves
items.summary_raw: Compartmental models of infectious disease transmission make assumptions about human behaviors. Specifically, they parameterize interactions across population groups, assumed to have distinct epidemiologically relevant behavioral patterns, primarily through contact matrices stratified by demographic variables such as age, gender, or socioeconomic status. Although such demographic characteristics are readily measurable, they may inadequately capture the social and psychological forces that govern protective behaviors. Drawing on 20 waves of a national survey conducted throughout the COVID-19 pandemic in the United States, we show that institutional trust—particularly trust in public health agencies, physicians, and hospitals—is a dominant predictor of protective behavior adoption. For mask wearing during periods of strongest pandemic activity, institutional trust explains more behavioral difference across population groups than age, income, education, and partisan affiliation combined. In unadjusted analyses, the difference in protective behavior adoption between individuals with the highest and lowest trust in the US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) was four- to six-fold larger than the corresponding differences by age, income, or education, and exceeded the difference between Democratic and Republican respondents. items.title: In-group neural alignment serves as a biomarker of social identity
items.summary_raw: In this study, we propose a perspective on neural synchronization. Beyond reflecting shared understanding between individuals, we suggest it serves as a biological marker of social homogeneity. We examined fMRI neural responses of 42 participants (21 religious, 21 secular) watching neutral and religion-relevant video narratives. While explicit measures of emotional response, agreement, and engagement showed no significant differences in within-group variance, religious participants—representing a tighter social structure—exhibited significantly higher in-group neural synchrony across all content types and brain networks. Remarkably, synchrony values predicted religious orientation with an accuracy of up to 92%. We conclude that a community’s homogeneous social structure drives pervasive neural alignment, positioning neural synchrony as a potential signature of group cohesion beyond explicit behavioral measures.

items.title: Intermittent gas–liquid rearrangement controls the mixing of gases in porous media
items.summary_raw: Gas mixing in porous media governs important environmental and industrial applications in which multiple gas components share the available pore space with liquid water, simultaneously undergoing gas mixing and gas–liquid redistribution. Currently, this process is represented by macroscopic models that ignore pore scale dynamics. We demonstrate that this is not generally valid, and can lead to large errors in the mixing rate. We use 4D X-ray imaging to investigate nitrogen injection into a porous sandstone saturated with krypton and water, jointly imaging the gas mixture composition evolution and multiphase flow of gas and water. In contrast to the smooth, continuous representation of the conventional advection–diffusion model, our results show that gas mixing evolves through a sequence of distinct regimes controlled by gas connectivity. Initially, immiscible gas–water displacement generates gas composition variance as the different gases occupy neighboring pores separated by water. As gas connectivity increases, intermittent gas–liquid interfacial rearrangements rapidly connect regions of contrasting gas composition, driving a fast decay in composition variance. Once connectivity stabilizes, mixing is controlled by a confined diffusion process within the quasi-static gas network. At later times, further mixing is driven slowly by multicomponent Ostwald ripening, whereby trapped gas ganglia exchange solutes through the surrounding liquid phase. These findings provide…

items.title: Majorana edge reconstruction and the ν = 5/2 non-Abelian thermal Hall puzzle
items.summary_raw: Pioneering thermal transport measurements on two-dimensional electron gases in high magnetic fields have demonstrated that the quantized Hall state at filling factor ν = 5/2 has a thermal Hall conductance κ quantized in half-integer multiples of κ 0 = π 2 k B 2 T / 3 h . Half-integer κ / κ 0 is a signature of neutral Majorana edge modes, in turn linked to the presence of non-Abelian anyon excitations in the bulk. However, the experimentally observed value of κ corresponds to the “PH-Pfaffian” state, in tension with numerical studies which instead favor either the Pfaffian or the AntiPfaffian. A variety of mechanisms have been invoked to explain this discrepancy, but have been either ruled out by further experiments or else involve fine-tuning. Building on density-matrix-renormalization group studies of physically realistic edges and analytic calculations of edge structure, we propose an alternative resolution of this puzzle involving an “edge reconstruction” solely involving the neutral Majorana sector of the theory. Such a Majorana edge reconstruction can “screen” a Pfaffian or AntiPfaffian bulk, so that transport signatures become indistinguishable from those of the PH-Pfaffian. We argue that this physically natural scenario is consistent with experiment.

items.title: Normalized Raman imaging for studies of tissue physiology of the kidney
items.summary_raw: Conventional histology relies on fixation, embedding, sectioning, and staining methods that distort cellular architecture, extract lipids, and introduce variability, limiting reproducibility. We present a pipeline for automated histopathology in the mouse kidney using normalized stimulated Raman imaging (NoRI) that enables quantitative, label-free protein and lipid measurements at high spatial resolution. NoRI computationally corrects protein, lipid, and water Raman signals, allowing quantitative biomass measurements while preserving tissue architecture, facilitating analysis by convolutional neural networks (CNN) for quantitative, morphological feature extraction. Applied to mouse kidney, CNN analysis of NoRI images was able to accurately classify tubule types (F1=0.93; harmonic mean of precision and recall against immunofluorescence-defined labels), anatomical regions (F1 = 0.91), and biological sex (F1 = 0.97), revealing greater cytoplasmic lipid (+6.5 to 7.3 mg/mL; P ≤ 0.028) and nuclear protein (+26.3 mg/mL; P ≤ 0.001) in female tubules. Using acute kidney injury (AKI) in mice as a disease model to test our histopathology pipeline combining NoRI and CNNs, we captured dynamic lipid and protein organization and quantified brush border remodeling and lipid droplet changes over 25 d postinjury. Spatial lipid quantification was central for feature classification in AKI (F1 = 0.99). Quantitative NoRI images also significantly outperformed equivalent raw stimulated Raman…

items.title: Some theoretical limitations of t-SNE
items.summary_raw: t-distributed Stochastic Neighborhood Embedding (t-SNE) has gained popularity as a dimension reduction technique, especially for visualizing data. It is well-known that dimension reduction may lose important data features. We provide a mathematical framework for understanding this loss for t-SNE, establishing several quantitative results across different scenarios that demonstrate how important structural information is lost.

items.title: How the midterms could unleash a new era for clean energy in these 3 states

That’s the thesis of the “ America Is All In ” coalition, which brings together cities and states that have vowed to uphold America’s “climate commitments … [i]n the absence of federal leadership.” The unspoken caveat in these claims is that the states leading the way on climate policy are concentrated in a few liberal parts of the country, like New England and the West Coast. The Democratic Party’s historic victory in this week’s midterm elections could change that. Democrats have secured control of both state legislative chambers and the governor’s mansion — also known as a “trifecta” — in Arizona, Pennsylvania, and Wisconsin, three states that have spent years or decades under Republican or divided control. The three states have also lagged in their support for clean energy. Democrats also restored trifectas in Minnesota, Michigan, and Nevada this week, but those are states where they last had unified control earlier this decade. “It is impossible to overstate how monumental these results are,” said David Weiskopf, the senior policy director at Climate Cabinet, a nonprofit that works to elect climate-focused candidates and pass state climate policy. items.title: Extreme flooding in the Southwest foreshadows a wild El Niño winter
items.summary_raw: The Southwest just got way too much of a good thing. Last weekend, a ferocious storm inundated communities and killed at least four people . Though precipitation is an essential component of Arizona’s desert climate, the state got two or three months’ worth of it in just a few days — far more than human infrastructure could handle all at once. Since September 20, an astonishing 28.84 inches of rain has fallen on Clovis, New Mexico, compared to its historical average of just 3.3 inches. “This weekend was just adding more on the rough times that those communities in Southwest Colorado and Arizona and Utah and New Mexico have been having recently,” said Russ Schumacher, director of the Colorado Climate Center at Colorado State University, who’s also the state climatologist. “I think the El Niño connection is pretty clear.” Indeed, that band of warm water in the Pacific could be priming much of the southern United States for a winter of increased precipitation, according to the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration’s seasonal outlook . “Could an event like this have happened in a non-El Niño year?” asked Michael A. Crimmins, a climatologist at the University of Arizona. “It could have, but it would have been a lot harder to pull all of the ingredients together at the same time, and would have been a lot less likely.” A wetter winter looks likely across the southern US Precipitation outlook through February 2027 Slightly favors wetter Favors wetter Slightly favors drier…

items.title: Governing Travel Through AI-Based Information: Passenger Well-being, Behavioural Change, and Green Choices
items.summary_raw: Abstract This paper investigates the transformative potential of AI-based real-time crowding information in shaping travel behaviour, passenger well-being, and environmentally sustainable choices in rail transport—addressing both technological innovation and its socio-economic impacts. Drawing on original stated-preference data from the capacity-constrained “Cinque Terre” railway corridor in Italy, we integrate behavioural indicators with a discrete choice experiment to examine how passengers respond to AI-generated predictions of crowding, delays, fares, and information sources. Our results demonstrate that exposure to such AI-driven information significantly increases passengers’ propensity to adjust departure times and opt for less crowded, lower-emission services. The analysis reveals a substantial willingness to incur delays or monetary costs to avoid severe crowding, highlighting the critical disutility of peak-period congestion. These findings suggest that AI-based information systems can serve as effective demand management tools, delivering well-being gains while supporting sustainable mobility and decarbonisation strategies.

INFLUENCE OF FAMILY SUPPORT ON ENTREPRENEURIAL ATTITUDES - A CASE FROM BULGARIA
items.summary_raw: This report examines the dynamics between the perceived support from one’s immediate social circle and the degree of personal autonomy in decision-making and the undertaking of new initiatives. Based on quantitative research (using a 5-point Likert scale among 645 respondents from Bulgaria in 2025 and 2026), the study analyzes attitudes regarding exclusive trust, emotional confidence, and the need for external approval. The results reveal a pattern of „supported autonomy“, wherein high levels of psychological security and acceptance do not lead to complete individual independence, but rather to a form of regulated social interdependence. The study’s design incorporates methodological controls to validate the reliability of the findings.

Methods A cross-sectional survey of 89 Architects in Lagos was carried out using questionnaires to assess the awareness, adoption, and barriers to the adoption of IoT technologies. Results The study results show that there’s a sufficient level of awareness of IoT technologies such as surveillance cameras, smart appliances, Biometric authentication systems, and solar energy monitoring systems; however, adoption remains moderate due to financial limitations, low client demand, limited professional training, and low policy support. Factors such as perceived usefulness, along with ease of use and social influences, were seen as major drivers of adoption. Discussion The findings indicate that awareness alone is not really sufficient to ensure the adoption of IoT technologies in smart housing. Widespread implementation of these technologies will require improved professional training, better client awareness, supportive policy frameworks, and financial incentives to reduce adoption barriers among architects in Lagos. This article examines the macroeconomic, institutional, and financial conditions associated with the adoption of carbon finance in emerging markets. Carbon finance is conceptualized broadly to include carbon pricing and crediting mechanisms, green and sustainability-linked debt, climate funds, blended finance, and other arrangements that connect capital allocation with emissions mitigation. Drawing on financial-development theory, institutional economics, the resource-mobilization perspective, and the political economy of energy transitions, the article develops a framework linking macroeconomic stability, financial-market depth, institutional quality, trade exposure, energy structure, and international climate-finance access to carbon finance adoption. It proposes a comparative panel-data research design for emerging and developing economies, with adoption measured through instrument presence, market activity, capital mobilized, and the sectoral allocation of proceeds. Integrating local ecological knowledge from professional fishers with environmental observations can improve the understanding, forecasting, and management of climate-sensitive jellyfish hazards
items.summary_raw: Abstract Climate variability is increasing the frequency and impacts of marine hazards, yet early warning systems often lack mechanisms to translate environmental signals into timely governance responses. Here, we examine how local ecological knowledge can be operationalized within a national hazard monitoring framework using jellyfish blooms as a model marine hazard. We analyzed 15 years (2010–2024) of weekly, fisher-reported observations from Korean coastal waters, focusing on Aurelia coerulea and Nemopilema nomurai. From these weekly reports, we calculated occurrence rate, defined as the percentage of respondents reporting jellyfish presence, and aggregation frequency, defined as the percentage reporting jellyfish aggregations. These indices were interpreted as operational risk indicators rather than standardized abundance estimates. Their utility was evaluated by testing temporal alignment with official national jellyfish alerts and by quantifying species-specific lead–lag structures. Distinct bloom dynamics emerged: A. coerulea formed persistent aggregations peaking from late spring to summer, whereas N. nomurai exhibited low background occurrence punctuated by abrupt mass events in late summer to autumn. Monthly sea surface temperature (SST) showed positive associations with fisher-reported occurrence and aggregation frequencies for both species (p < 0.05). This study develops a decision‐support framework aligned with the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) to prioritize strategies integrating cultural heritage preservation, renewable energy, and sustainable urban development under uncertainty. The Fuzzy Analytical Hierarchy Process (AHP) was applied to determine the relative importance of the criteria and sub‐criteria, while Technique for Order Preference by Similarity to Ideal Solution (TOPSIS)‐Grey analysis was used to rank the proposed strategies based on expert judgments. The findings of Fuzzy AHP identified Urban Aesthetics as the most important main criterion, followed by Renewable Energy Integration and Preservation of Historic Sites. items.title: (In)consistency on the route to Paris: EU and Swedish climate and forest-related policy mixes towards the fulfilment of the Paris Agreement
items.summary_raw: In response to the Paris Agreement and the EU’s climate emergency declaration, the EU has enacted policies strengthening forests’ role in climate mitigation. This paper analyses the climate-forest policy mix at EU and national levels, using Sweden as critical case. We examine the horizontal and vertical consistency of these policy mixes, focusing on problem framings, goals, targets, roles assigned to forests, and procedural – and substantive policy instruments. Combining these aspects into a single analysis adds to previous research by creating more comprehensive understanding of challenges and (in)consistencies in the policy mix, both regarding potential goal trade-offs, approaches towards goal achievement, and (lacking) connections between objectives and policy instruments. We identify four major inconsistencies: (1) differing views on the appropriate balance of EU and Member State influence over forests; (2) numerous policy objectives but few specific targets and concrete instruments; (3) EU’s focus on regulations and market-based instruments versus Sweden’s focus on voluntary actions and ownership rights; and (4) contrasting preferences regarding forest management practices. To bridge these gaps, policymakers need to clearly delineate the EU’s and Member States’ roles, establish measurable and timebound objectives linked to tailored policy instruments, and implement mechanisms for adaptive, multifunctional, and just forest management.

items.title: Boosting Climate Justice by Boosting Economic Growth
items.source_name: Erasmus Journal for Philosophy and Economics
items.summary_raw: Many considerations speak against economic growth. Climate justice is not among them—on the contrary. We argue that climate justice speaks for promoting GDP growth in the coming decades, even in rich countries. Growth strengthens adaptive capacity, can make up for a sizable fraction of climate impacts, and, above all, is a powerful tool for liberation from poverty. On mitigation, our claim is weaker: radical emission cuts require going all-in on clean technology, and clean technology progress shrinks the leverage of forgoing growth. Whether growth accelerates clean technology enough to outweigh its direct effect on emissions is uncertain—but this uncertainty is insufficient to undermine the overall case. We aim to serve both sides of the debate: growth proponents, as the politically dominant camp, rarely flesh out the arguments for their stance, let alone in terms of justice; growth sceptics often stop short of a clearly delineated conclusion. We supply both.

items.title: Knowledge, attitudes, and practices of farmers towards sustainable agriculture in the Barind Tract of Bangladesh
items.summary_raw: Abstract The global imperative to transition towards sustainable agricultural systems is particularly acute in vulnerable, resource-scarce regions such as the Barind Tract of Bangladesh, an area characterized by a semi-arid climate, soil infertility, and acute water scarcity. Understanding the drivers and barriers to adoption is critical, with the Knowledge, Attitude, and Practice (KAP) framework serving as a vital analytical tool. This study provides a comprehensive assessment of farmers' KAP towards sustainable agriculture and examines the socio-economic and institutional factors that influence them. Data were collected through structured, face-to-face interviews with 273 smallholder farmers, selected via a multi-stage random sampling technique across the Rajshahi district. The data were analyzed using descriptive statistics and multiple regression models. The findings reveal a critical paradox: while farmers possess moderate to high levels of knowledge (Mean = 19.27) and overwhelmingly favorable attitudes (Mean = 56.34) regarding the benefits of sustainable practices, their actual adoption remains only moderate (Mean = 16.16), exposing a significant knowledge-practice gap. Regression analyses identified Annual Farm Income (AFI) as the single most significant positive determinant across all three KAP domains, underscoring economic capacity as the fundamental gatekeeper to adoption.
