items.title: The Imperative of Economic Growth Is Arbitrarily Constraining
items.source_name: Erasmus Journal for Philosophy and Economics
items.summary_raw: Governments routinely treat continual growth in per capita consumption as a standing imperative. I argue that doing so arbitrarily constrains our policy choices. Descriptively, I use the case of growth in climate change policy to show that despite the common emphasis on the ways growth expands our capabilities and consumption opportunities, the pursuit of growth also limits us. Normatively, I argue that these constraints are arbitrary. A justified constraint must identify the interests it serves, so that we can ask whether they are weighty enough to warrant the limitations it would impose. A principle requiring each generation to exceed the consumption of the last cannot supply that information. At best, growth can serve as a proxy for our underlying intergenerational obligations, and only under conditions that may no longer hold in wealthy societies.

items.title: Mehr als Klimaschutz? Ein systematisches Review zu psychosozialen Co-Benefits von Klimapolitik
items.source_name: Publication server of the Robert Koch Institute (Robert Kock Institute)
items.summary_raw: Hintergrund: Der Klimawandel birgt erhebliche Risiken für die psychosoziale Gesundheit, doch über mögliche psychosoziale Co-Benefits klimapolitischer Maßnahmen ist bislang wenig bekannt. Dieses systematische Review untersucht (A) psychosoziale Co-Benefits, die mit klimapolitischen Maßnahmen einhergehen, und (B) moderierende Faktoren, die diese Effekte beeinflussen. Methode: Gemäß den PRISMA-Leitlinien wurden k = 21 Studien identifiziert und anhand des PICOS-Schemas sowie einer narrativen Synthese ausgewertet. Ergebnisse: Klimapolitische Maßnahmen – insbesondere Reduktion der Luftverschmutzung, Umweltsteuern und naturbasierte Interventionen im städtischen Raum – gingen mit Verbesserungen des subjektiven Wohlbefindens, der psychischen Gesundheit und des sozialen Zusammenhalts einher. Die Effekte wurden durch Umweltverbesserungen und Gewinne an körperlicher Gesundheit moderiert und variierten nach sozioökonomischem Status, Alter und Kontext, etwa Schulen oder ländlichen vs. städtischen Standorten. Der Zugang zu Interventionen und deren tatsächliche Nutzung erwiesen sich als relevante, aber wenig untersuchte Mechanismen. Einige Studien wiesen auf Zielkonflikte hin, darunter eine ungleiche Verteilung des Nutzens und unbeabsichtigte soziale Effekte. Schlussfolgerungen: Insgesamt können klimapolitische Maßnahmen psychosoziale Co-Benefits erzeugen, die Evidenz ist jedoch heterogen und methodisch begrenzt. Künftige Forschung sollte kausale Schlussfolgerungen stärken, Outcome-Maße…

items.title: Climate Change Reporting in Pakistani Media: Framing, Editorial Priorities, and Public Awareness
items.summary_raw: Pakistan contributes roughly 0.4 percent of global greenhouse gas emissions yet ranks among the countries most severely affected by extreme weather, a disparity that places unusual demands on its news media. This study examines how Pakistani media report climate change, what editorial logics govern that reporting, and how the resulting coverage relates to public awareness. Using a critical synthesis design, it integrates peer reviewed content and framing analyses, a doctoral framing study, national and cross national audience surveys, think tank and donor research, and official climate data published between 2019 and 2026. Three findings emerge. First, coverage has grown substantially in volume but remains event driven and politically framed, with responsibility and disaster frames dominant, attribution to anthropogenic climate change rare, and mitigation, agriculture, displacement and mental health persistently underreported. Second, these patterns are produced less by editorial hostility than by newsroom structure: the environment beat remains an afterthought, reporters are generalists covering several beats, editors frequently lack subject command, and ratings driven news judgement favours live disaster imagery over explanatory work. Third, public awareness is high in the abstract but shallow in causal terms, and audience engagement has plateaued into what has been termed climate perception inertia, with a large majority of Pakistanis reporting that the issue has been…

items.title: Moderní energetiku v Evropě brzdí cena. V Česku ale nejsou odpovědí jen dotace
Sodium-Ion Batteries, Direct Lithium Extraction, Bidirectional Grid Integration, and Advanced Nuclear Power: A Review of Their Transition to Commercial Deployment, 2020–2026
items.source_name: Journal of Emerging and Innovative Technologies
items.summary_raw: Objectives: This review examines the technical foundations, deployment status, and economic drivers of four technologies reaching commercial inflection points in 2025 and 2026: sodium ion batteries, direct lithium extraction, bidirectional grid integration, and advanced nuclear power. The aim is to assess how storage chemistry, raw material extraction, grid integration, and firm low carbon generation are advancing together, and to identify the barriers each field still faces. Material and Methods: The review draws on peer reviewed literature, agency reports (including the International Energy Agency and the International Atomic Energy Agency), and recent industry disclosures from manufacturers, utilities, and technology companies. For each technology the review covers technical principles, performance and deployment status, and open barriers, then considers how the four fields interact. Results: Sodium ion batteries have moved into mass production and now offer a credible lower cost, more abundant alternative to lithium chemistry for grid storage and entry level electric vehicles, though energy density still lags mainstream lithium iron phosphate cells. Direct lithium extraction recovers lithium from brines with less land and water use and in hours rather than months, opening new resources such as geothermal and oilfield brines. Bidirectional charging is turning millions of idle vehicle and home batteries into distributed grid assets through a four layer architecture…

items.title: A text-mining analysis of climate risk disclosure and corporate energy efficiency in Chinese listed firms
items.summary_raw: This study examines the association between climate risk disclosure and corporate energy efficiency using Chinese A-share data from 2012 to 2024. A firm-level disclosure index is constructed via text mining based on the TCFD framework. Two-way fixed effects models show a positive association, with a one-standard-deviation increase in disclosure corresponding to approximately a 3.6% increase in energy efficiency, robust to endogeneity tests. Transition risk disclosure has a stronger association with energy efficiency than physical risk; the difference widens further when standardized by each dimension’s dispersion. Mediation analysis indicates green innovation and eased financing constraints are partial channels whose separately estimated indirect effects sum to approximately 20% of the total effect, though the direct effect dominates. Heterogeneity analysis reveals stronger effects in state-owned, heavily polluting, and carbon pilot region firms, with insignificant effects outside pilot regions; the association also strengthens significantly after the launch of the national carbon market in 2021. The study contributes to the literature by shifting the focus from capital market reactions to real operational outcomes, distinguishing between physical and transition risk disclosure, and highlighting the role of institutional context in determining whether climate disclosure produces substantive effects on energy performance.

items.title: The purinergic receptor P2Y 13 controls the activation and mode of division of adult ventricular–subventricular zone neural stem cells
items.summary_raw: The ventricular–subventricular zone (V-SVZ) is the most active germinal area in the mammalian brain and it continues to generate newborn neurons throughout life. This area harbors a population of neural stem cells (NSCs) that exist in different states of activation: quiescent NSCs, primed NSCs, and activated NSCs. There are currently few specific markers to effectively discern each state. Likewise, the molecular signals that control the transition from quiescence to activation remain largely unexplored, and the factors that controls whether dividing NSCs differentiate or self-renew are poorly understood. Here, we present evidence that the metabotropic P2Y 13 purinergic receptor plays a critical role in regulating adult neurogenesis. We found that P2Y 13 is specifically expressed in NSCs within the adult V-SVZ and that its levels can be used to distinguish quiescent from activated NSCs. P2Y 13 signaling promotes NSC activation, enhancing lineage progression as opposed to their self-renewal. Conversely, pharmacological blockade or genetic silencing of P2Y 13 receptors favors NSC quiescence. Thus, we consider the metabotropic P2Y 13 purinergic receptor a pivotal modulator of NSC dynamics.

items.title: An aggregation-prone region in talin controls talin self-interactions and regulates integrin adhesion complex dynamics
items.summary_raw: Talin is a mechanosensitive scaffold that couples integrins to the actin cytoskeleton and coordinates signaling at integrin adhesion complexes. A second integrin-binding site (IBS2) has been proposed within the R11–R12 region of the talin rod, although the molecular basis of this interaction has remained unclear. Here, we show that talin R11 contains a cryptic aggregation-prone region (APR) embedded within Helix50. Mechanical unfolding of R11 exposes this motif, enabling high-affinity talin–talin interactions and force-dependent self-association. The isolated APR forms amyloid-like fibers in vitro, and APR-disrupting gatekeeper mutations suppress fiber formation, talin self-association, and cellular recruitment. We therefore designate this motif Aggregation-Prone Region 1 (APR1). Mitochondrial-targeting experiments demonstrate that APR1-dependent recruitment occurs in cells independently of focal adhesions and integrins. APR1 overlaps the vinculin-binding site in Helix50, and vinculin disrupts preexisting talin assemblies, revealing a mechano-chaperone function for vinculin. Disruption of APR1-mediated self-association does not impair adhesion formation but instead generates larger, more talin-rich adhesions with altered assembly dynamics and signaling properties, indicating a role for APR1 in regulating adhesion remodeling. Together, these findings identify force-dependent talin self-association as a mechanism in mechanotransduction and suggest that the region previously…

items.title: Lead impairs long-term memory by disrupting mitochondrial redox homeostasis in Drosophila
items.summary_raw: Lead (Pb) exposure remains a major environmental risk factor for cognitive dysfunction, yet the cellular mechanisms underlying Pb-induced memory impairment are poorly understood. Here, we show that both developmental and adult-onset Pb exposure selectively disrupts protein-synthesis-dependent long-term memory (LTM) in Drosophila melanogaster while sparing other memory forms. Using a mitochondria-targeted redox biosensor (mito-roGFP2-Orp1), we found that Pb elevates mitochondrial oxidative stress and disrupts redox homeostasis in cholinergic neurons and in dorsal-anterior-lateral (DAL) neurons, a critical locus for LTM consolidation. Pb-induced redox imbalance suppresses training-induced de novo protein synthesis in DAL neurons, thereby impairing memory consolidation. Antioxidant treatment with epigallocatechin gallate restores mitochondrial redox balance and rescues LTM by reinstating activity-dependent protein synthesis in DAL neurons. These findings identify mitochondrial redox dysregulation as a key mechanism linking environmental Pb exposure to impaired memory consolidation. Our results further establish a genetically tractable platform for dissecting neurotoxic mechanisms and for evaluating antioxidant-based strategies to mitigate Pb-induced cognitive dysfunction.

items.title: Comprehensive classification of HCN1 variants linked to neurodevelopmental disorders with and without epilepsy
items.summary_raw: Hyperpolarization-activated cyclic nucleotide-gated 1 (HCN1) channels mediate the cationic I h current, a fundamental regulator of neuronal excitability and synaptic integration, and are predominantly expressed in the cortex and hippocampus. Although HCN1 variants have been increasingly identified in patients with epilepsy, from milder forms to developmental and epileptic encephalopathies (DEE), genotype–phenotype correlations remain poorly defined. Here, we used patch-clamp electrophysiology and confocal imaging in HEK293 cells to functionally characterize 43 HCN1 variants identified in patients with neurodevelopmental disorders, with or without epilepsy. Based on biophysical properties, we established a classification system comprising four distinct functional classes: I) low or no current; II) hyperpolarizing shift in voltage dependence; III) depolarizing shift in voltage dependence; and IV) generation of an instantaneous current. The molecular basis for this classification was further interpreted using available cryo-EM structures of HCN1. Integration with clinical data from 50 patients revealed a striking correlation between functional class and clinical presentation. Loss-of-function variants prevailed among individuals with milder phenotypes or without epilepsy, with the latter distinctively clustering within the channel selectivity filter. In contrast, gain-of-function and mixed variants were predominantly associated with DEE. Finally, we demonstrate that allosteric…

items.title: USP46 restrains K63-linked polyubiquitination–dependent aggregation and activation of the NLRP3 inflammasome in lupus nephritis
items.summary_raw: The activation of the NLRP3 inflammasome necessitates its aggregation within the dispersed trans-Golgi network (dTGN) and subsequent transport from the dTGN to the microtubule organizing center (MTOC), a process facilitated by HDAC6. However, the regulatory mechanisms governing the formation of NLRP3 aggregates remain insufficiently understood. In this study, we demonstrate that proteasome impairment induces polyubiquitination and aggregation of NLRP3 at the MTOC. We demonstrate ubiquitin-specific protease 46 (USP46) as a key factor that recognizes NLRP3 as a substrate and restricts nondegradative K63-linked polyubiquitination at lysine residue K930, thereby preventing excessive aggregation, transport to the MTOC, and inflammasome activation. Furthermore, myeloid-specific knockout of USP46 exacerbates renal injury and inflammation in both lipopolysaccharide-induced-induced endotoxic shock and pristane-induced lupus nephritis models. Our findings provide insights into the regulatory mechanisms underlying the aggresomal activation of the NLRP3 inflammasome.

items.title: Codfishes survived essential gene loss by functionally co-opting freshwater ovulatory pathways to marine egg hydration
items.summary_raw: Adaptive evolution associated with dispensable gene loss is widespread in the animal kingdom. However, loss of genes essential for embryonic survival and the mechanisms that evolved to bypass negative selection and extinction are less well known. Here, we show that all Gadiformes, an ecologically dominant order of codfishes, lost the aqp1ab -type genes that are essential for the formation of hydrated pelagic eggs and embryonic survival of marine teleosts in oceanic environments. Despite such gene loss, codfishes produce some of the most highly hydrated pelagic eggs of all marine teleosts. To resolve this apparent paradox, we initially confirmed that the mechanisms of osmotic drive are conserved with other pelagic-egg-producing marine teleosts, and then conducted comparative transcript analyses of aquaporin water channels in distantly-related freshwater and marine teleosts. This uncovered Aqp4-type channels that have been chromosomally linked to the Aqp1-type channels in jawed vertebrate genomes for >450 million years as the primary candidates. Using immunolocalization, functional assays, and inhibition experiments with zebrafish and Atlantic cod as model organisms, we show that short isoforms of Aqp4 are required for egg ovulation in more ancestral lineages of freshwater teleosts and were recruited to the oocyte hydration pathway of codfishes. By contrast, the oldest and most modern lineages of marine teleosts producing pelagic eggs still utilize the aqp1ab genes for egg…

items.title: A DPY19L2/FAM209-associated protein–Arp complex–CAPZA3 scaffold is essential for perinuclear theca assembly and fertilization
items.summary_raw: Fertilization is a fundamental biological process that enables the fusion of a spermatozoon with an oocyte to initiate embryonic development. However, the underlying mechanisms leading to fertilization failure remain poorly understood. Here, we demonstrated that the actin-related protein (Arp) family members ACTRT2 and ACTRT3 are essential for fertilization in both humans and mice, whereas ACTL10 is dispensable for fertility and the human-specific ACTL8 may play a role in early spermatogenesis. Ultrastructural and immunofluorescence analyses revealed that, during spermatogenesis, ACTRT2 or ACTRT3 deficiency disrupts the assembly of subacrosomal layer of the perinuclear theca (SAL-PT), leading to acrosome detachment and subsequent manchette abnormalities, which in turn impairs the formation of the postacrosomal sheath of the PT. These structural defects were accompanied by reduced abundance of the candidate sperm-borne oocyte-activating factors PAWP and PLCζ. Moreover, knockout of Actrt2 or Actrt3 severely impaired spermatozoa’s ability to penetrate the zona pellucida during in vitro fertilization. Mechanistically, ACTRT2, ACTRT3, ACTL7A, ACTL7B, and ACTL9 form a testis-enriched Arp complex in the SAL-PT and maintain the stability of one another. This complex interacts with the PT protein CAPZA3, which subsequently binds and stabilizes PLCζ. Additionally, the Arp complex interacts with DPY19L2/FAM209-associated proteins to mediate acrosome anchoring to the nuclear envelope…

items.title: A tetravalent bispecific protein enables targeted degradation of VCAM-1 and VEGFR for treatment of choroidal neovascularization
items.summary_raw: Wet age-related macular degeneration (AMD), a leading cause of irreversible vision loss, is driven by pathological choroidal neovascularization (CNV). Although anti-vascular endothelial growth factor (anti-VEGF) therapies remain the clinical standard, their utility is constrained by incomplete responses in nearly 50% of patients and off-target risks—such as geographic atrophy—stemming from non-specific VEGF blockade. Here, we identify a robust correlation between vascular cell adhesion molecule-1 (VCAM-1) and VEGF/VEGF receptor (VEGFR) expression in aqueous humor from AMD patients and in murine CNV models. Thus, we engineered a tetravalent bispecific protein, RHV, by functionalizing an L-rhamnulose-1-phosphate aldolase scaffold with peptides that selectively bind VCAM-1 and the VEGFR on neovessels. The tetravalent design confers high apparent affinity, enhancing pathological endothelial targeting while sparing healthy retinal vasculature. RHV induces concurrent internalization and lysosomal degradation of both VCAM-1 and VEGFR via a head-to-tail binding mode, leading to sustained inhibition of the VEGF/VEGFR, PI3K/AKT and Apelin/APJ signaling pathways. In murine CNV models, a single intravitreal injection of RHV exhibits superior ocular retention and lesion penetration, achieving therapeutic efficacy comparable to aflibercept [a ligand-trap fusion protein for VEGF-A, VEGF-B and placental growth factor (PIGF)] at one-quarter of the molar dose. items.title: QnAs with Alison Gopnik
Modified Newtonian Dynamics and galaxy clusters
items.summary_raw: First proposed by Milgrom in 1983 as an alternative to the standard Cold Dark Matter (CDM) paradigm, Modified Newtonian Dynamics (MOND) has gained renewed momentum in light of persistent nondetections of exotic dark matter particles and growing tensions facing CDM on galactic scales. While MOND perfectly reproduces galactic rotation curves, it encounters notable challenges in explaining the equilibrium of galaxy clusters. Although it reduces the overall dark matter budget in these massive systems, an unidentified mass component remains required. This paper investigates the hypothesis that this missing mass is baryonic: composed of nonradiating ordinary matter such as stellar remnants, gas too diffuse to initiate star formation, or compact, ultra-dense clouds of cold molecular gas with low volume filling factors. Using a sample of 106 clusters mapped in X-rays, emitted by the hot intracluster medium composing most of the visible mass, we derive first the total mass within the Newtonian dynamics, assuming hydrostatic equilibrium and spherical symmetry. Then, with the modified Poisson equation, we reconstruct the spatial distribution of the invisible missing matter within the MOND framework. In the sample, the relaxed systems harboring cooling flows, known as cool-core clusters, have the highest peaks of dark missing mass. Its density profile reveals a pronounced central concentration bounded by a steep truncation immediately beyond a core radius of 20 to 30 kpc, confirming…

items.title: Multifunctional multiphysics metamaterials via decomposition-based multiobjective optimization design
items.summary_raw: Metamaterials offer unprecedented control over physical fields through their microstructure, but current design methods cannot meet the demands of scenarios involving active sources, multiphysics field coupling, and multifunctional requirements. Moreover, existing approaches are generally developed for specific functions, making it difficult to integrate different functionalities and select the functional priorities within a single structure. To overcome these limitations, this study presents a systematic inverse design framework for multifunctional multiphysics metamaterials via multiobjective optimization. To uniformly explore the Pareto front, which clearly exhibits trade-offs among functionalities and facilitates the selection of functional priorities, we employ dynamic normalization into the decomposition-based multiobjective evolutionary algorithm. A robust anisotropic unit-cell database is constructed and used for generating metamaterials with optimized microstructures for multifunctionality. Three complex cases are studied that can simultaneously achieve mechanical cloaking plus stress minimization, thermal cloaking plus stress minimization, and direct current cloaking plus thermal stress minimization. Furthermore, the proposed framework is employed in potential engineering problems, for example, to realize mechanical cloaking by embedding functional components in structural materials, while minimizing the surrounding stress on functional components for mechanical…

items.title: Profile of Françoise Combes
items.summary_raw: Françoise Combes’s childhood curiosity motivated her to pursue a career in science. Her studies in physics at the École Normale Supérieure in Paris eventually led her to focus on astrophysics. With help from mentors, such as astrophysicists Evry Schatzman and Pierre Encrenaz, Combes has had a distinguished career in astrophysics. She is renowned for her work studying the formation and evolution of galaxies and their dynamics and her research on dark matter. In her Inaugural Article, she describes her latest work exploring alternatives to dark matter.

items.title: Maize genetic diversity is largely unstructured by human ethnolinguistic diversity in its center of origin
items.summary_raw: Population structure and environmental features often capture major axes of genetic variation in many species. Yet the impacts of human activity often remain unquantified. For domesticated species that rely on human activity for survival and dispersal, human movements and cultural differences may play key roles patterning genetic diversity. Maize is a staple crop of enormous cultural importance to indigenous peoples of the Americas, but cannot survive or disperse without farmers. Using publicly available genotyping and passport data from approximately 2,000 traditional maize varieties, more than 500 whole genome sequences of humans from Mexico, and indigenous linguistic maps, we quantify anthropogenic effects on maize genetic diversity in the Americas. Maize shows very little overall structure, highlighting the effectiveness of indigenous farmers in moving and mixing maize populations. While principal components of maize diversity show meaningful correlations to human genetic diversity, our linear modeling suggests little additional impact of human population structure beyond shared geography. Though differences in maize diversity are often patterned by language locally, we find only weak genome-wide effects at larger spatial scales. Despite the relatively weak global signal of anthropogenic effects, linguistic Genome-wide association, outlier F ST analyses, and selection scans identified loci associated with specific languages. Leveraging landscape-level sequencing data, we…

items.title: Intrinsically motivated humans and agents in open-world exploration
items.summary_raw: What drives exploration? Understanding the intrinsic motivation to explore is a long-standing challenge in both cognitive science and AI. In this study, we directly compare adults, children aged 8 to 12 y, and AI agents exploring a complex, open-ended environment called Crafter ( 1 ). We study how three common information-theoretic intrinsic objectives—entropy, information gain, and empowerment—relate to their behavior. We find that all three are positively correlated with human exploration progress for both children and adults, although entropy and empowerment are more strongly related to exploration progress in children than information gain. Furthermore, across agents and humans we observe that entropy initially increases rapidly, then plateaus, while empowerment increases continuously, suggesting that in early exploration they look for novel states, while in advanced exploration they look for states they can control. Finally, we find preliminary evidence that private speech about goals may aid exploration in children. Our data are available at https://github.com/alyd/humans_in_crafter_data .

items.title: Dynamic virulence decomposition disentangles host and pathogen contributions over the course of infection
items.summary_raw: Decomposing virulence into host and pathogen effects is key to understanding how virulence is generated during infection, and how host and pathogen contributions evolve over time. Conventional virulence decomposition is, however, not designed to quantify how these contributions vary throughout an infection. Building on conventional virulence decomposition, we developed a dynamic framework that integrates disease space analysis to quantify these changing contributions. We applied this framework to existing data from house finches ( Haemorhous mexicanus ) experimentally infected with the emerging bacterial pathogen, Mycoplasma gallisepticum , examining two biologically meaningful infection phases: an early phase dominated by innate immune responses and a later phase in which the adaptive immune response is fully activated. Our analyses revealed that virulence components evolved differently across infection phases, with pathogen exploitation, per-parasite-pathogenicity (PPP), and host resistance each exhibiting distinct trajectories. These findings corroborated several known evolutionary patterns, while also revealing the evolution of increased PPP in this system. In contrast, the apparent evolution of host tolerance inferred from aggregated peak measurements was not supported by phase-specific analyses, demonstrating that aggregated and phase-specific measures can provide different mechanistic insights into virulence. By linking conventional virulence decomposition with…

items.title: Entropic tightening of knots in granular chains under vibration
items.summary_raw: Knots are common in long chains, from DNA and proteins to everyday strings, yet direct observation of knot dynamics is difficult. Using granular chains on vibrating platforms, we directly visualize knot dynamics and find that knot cores spontaneously tighten, a behavior observed across different knot types. We quantitatively explain spontaneous knot tightening using knot-tube theory: segments confined within the knot core experience entropic loss and tend to escape the core to gain conformational entropy. Although driven granular chains are not in thermodynamic equilibrium, their steady-state knot-size statistics are approximately captured by equilibrium statistical mechanics and Monte Carlo simulations. Analyses of state-transition probabilities and time-reversal asymmetry suggest a weak violation of detailed balance when the granular dynamics are projected onto the knot-size coordinate. Finally, we discuss the possible relevance of knot tightening to topoisomerase-mediated DNA unknotting.

items.title: Municipal sludge disposal emerges as a major, hidden, and rapidly growing atmospheric mercury source
items.summary_raw: Wastewater treatment greatly reduces mercury pollution in aquatic ecosystems but does not eliminate it. Here, we identify municipal sludge disposal as a major, long-overlooked atmospheric mercury source. In China, sludge disposal emitted 42 - 10 + 18 Mg in 2024, exceeding 10% of national anthropogenic emissions and ranking third after cement production and nonferrous metal smelting. These emissions have increased by nearly a thousandfold since the 1970s and are concentrated in densely populated urban areas, driven by the rapid expansion of sludge incineration, codisposal, and composting. Our findings reveal a cross-media pollution transfer embedded in sustainability transitions and call for sludge disposal to be incorporated into UNEP mercury budget and Minamata Convention assessments.

items.title: Progressive shifts in soil respiration response to long-term nitrogen enrichment across global forests and grasslands
items.summary_raw: Soil stores the largest pool of actively cycling carbon (C) on land, and its dynamics under global changes are critical for projecting climate feedbacks. Global nitrogen (N) deposition has more than doubled since the 1860s; however, the temporal dynamics of soil C emissions under prolonged N deposition are poorly understood. Here, using a global time-series dataset compiled from 38 long-term experiments in forests and grasslands, we find that the response of soil respiration (Rs) to N addition systematically shifts from a transient increase persisting for approximately 2 y to a sustained suppression over time (mean effect = −6%; 95% CI = [−10%, −3%]). Rs in forests and grasslands followed consistent nonlinear trajectories, characterized by a rapid initial decline in the magnitude of the response, which progressively leveled off. Notably, suppression of Rs emerged when cumulative N inputs exceeded a threshold of ~100 kg N ha −1 . Consequently, the suppression was both stronger and occurred more rapidly under high-level N additions (>50 kg N ha −1 y −1 ). These temporal dynamics were associated with N-induced soil acidification and related changes in microbial properties. Overall, these findings indicate that accurate prediction of land–atmosphere C fluxes under global change requires models to capture the reported temporal dynamics.

items.title: Amphipathic helices repurpose a Patched/NPC1-like cholesterol transporter to function at Plasmodium –erythrocyte membrane contact sites
items.summary_raw: The interface between the malaria parasite Plasmodium spp. and its host erythrocyte critically mediates nutrient uptake, lipid exchange, and protein export required for parasite replication and thus pathogenesis. Approximately half of this interface consists of narrow membrane contact sites, a region defined by only 3 to 4 nm of aqueous space between the parasite plasma membrane and the parasitophorous vacuole membrane. Despite its extent, the region remains largely uncharacterized and inaccessible, not least due to its narrowness. The sole identified resident is the Plasmodium falciparum Niemann-Pick Type C1-Related protein, PfNCR1, an essential Patched/NPC1-like cholesterol transporter, suggesting this conserved transporter family has evolved an unconventional adaptation for localizing to membrane contact sites that can reveal a mechanism to access the region. Here, using live-cell microscopy and assessment of cholesterol homeostasis, we identify a helix–linker–helix (HLH) domain as the necessary modification for efficient PfNCR1 localization. We find that correct localization is required for the parasite to maintain low cholesterol levels, connecting targeting to function. Using a glycosylphosphatidylinositol-anchored fluorescent reporter as a minimal membrane-associated protein, we show that the HLH domain is sufficient to drive localization to the narrow membrane contact site region. items.title: As Nebraska seeks to grow, Omaha’s energy capacity is a major hurdle

In addition to facing transmission constraints, utilities couldn’t generate enough power due to issues with fuel supply and equipment malfunctions. In Nebraska, in an effort to preserve the grid and prevent a system-wide failure, the Omaha Public Power District, or OPPD, conducted rolling blackouts . Afterward, the Southwest Power Pool, which manages the region’s grid reliability, required its members to keep more power capacity in reserve in case of future emergency situations. In the following years, the data center boom, electrification, and growth from other industries have brought utilities around the country the promise of new customers and the challenge of a huge spike in demand. As a result, OPPD, which serves about 419,000 customers across eastern Nebraska, is running low on the amount of energy capacity it can promise to new and expanding economic development projects. The shortage is threatening the region’s ability to develop economically, attract companies, add jobs, and grow. What’s more, OPPD is facing the same challenges that are plaguing utilities and electric grids across the country: Power plants and other electric grid infrastructure are aging. items.title: What a historic ‘blue wave’ midterm means for climate action
items.summary_raw: The Democratic Party won a commanding victory in Tuesday’s midterm elections. As of Wednesday morning, the party had secured control of both the Senate and the House of Representatives, as well as several state governments. The party’s strong performance, driven in part by voters’ anger over inflation and the war in Iran, reached into traditional Republican strongholds like Ohio and South Carolina. The sweep will have profound consequences for climate action in the United States, even with President Donald Trump still in the White House. Flipping control of Congress will allow the Democrats to hinder Trump’s numerous attempts to roll back federal climate policy. In the first two years of Trump’s term, party leaders could do little more than write strongly worded statements to administration officials. They were powerless to stop the suspension of clean energy funding , the elimination of climate rules for power plants and motor vehicles , and the hollowing out of agencies like the U.S. Forest Service and the Federal Emergency Management Agency . Now, the party will have a lot more leverage. Democratic senators and members of Congress can issue subpoenas to force administration officials to testify before Congress, and could even impeach Trump administration figures over funding clawbacks and staff reductions that Democrats have called unlawful . items.title: Does hope help? Climate emotions and the chances for change
items.summary_raw: Abstract Hope is sometimes dismissed as a feel‐good attitude that discourages people from taking meaningful action. In climate debates, many activists and scholars frame fear as a more effective motivator than hope. Yet in rural Namibia and Kenya, as well as in several recent social movements, hope is experienced as a vital force that sustains people in their efforts to create change. Drawing on these experiences and on phenomenology, we examine whether hope can productively address the climate crisis. We show that practical hope can transform situations by warding off despair, enabling achievement, and drawing others into collective action. We also describe how our interlocutors understand their heart as growing stronger when they confront hardship with hope, indicating an ontological shift toward a more resilient and hopeful self. We conclude that practical hope is effective, and that anthropology should communicate more hope‐filled narratives that contribute to an atmosphere in which transformative change becomes possible.

items.title: What shapes public support for mangrove restoration? The role of perceptions of ecosystem services and disservices
items.summary_raw: Mangroves offer a wide range of ecosystem services, yet have historically attracted negative perceptions, often tied to real or perceived disservices. While global interest in mangrove restoration is increasing, success remains uneven, partially due to persistent social barriers, including limited stakeholder engagement. Understanding how public perceptions of mangroves influence restoration support could inform more effective strategies. However, the extent to which multiple disservices shape support across different social groups remains unclear. In this study, we examine the case of Australia's Great Barrier Reef catchments, surveying 869 residents across 21 Local Government Areas. Using a 5-point Likert scale, we assessed perceptions of mangrove ecosystem services and disservices. Binomial logistic regression was used to model restoration support as a function of these perceptions and sociodemographic variables. Overall, 87.6% of residents supported mangrove restoration. Support remained high across the catchments, and perceptions of ecosystem services and disservices were associated with variation in support. Biodiversity showed the strongest positive association, with each one-point increase in perceived importance corresponding to 2.37 times higher odds of supporting restoration (Odds Ratio (OR) = 2.37, 95% CI = 1.61–3.54). In contrast, each one-point increase in perceived loss of land productivity was associated with 38% lower odds of support (OR = 0.62, 95% CI =…

items.title: Moral Distress Among Hospice Nurses in China: A Mixed‐Methods Study Informed by an Ecological Systems Perspective
items.summary_raw: AIM: To examine moral distress and associated factors among nurses involved in hospice care in China and explore how these experiences are shaped across individual, relational, organisational and sociocultural contexts. BACKGROUND: Hospice nurses frequently encounter ethically challenging situations. In China, moral distress may be further shaped by organisational constraints, family-centred decision-making and sociocultural expectations surrounding end-of-life care. METHODS: A convergent parallel mixed-methods design was used and reported in accordance with the Good Reporting of a Mixed-Methods Study (GRAMMS) guidelines. Quantitative data were collected from 295 nurses using measures of moral distress, moral resilience, work-family conflict and hospital ethical climate. Semi-structured interviews were conducted with 15 nurses purposively selected from the quantitative sample. The datasets were analysed separately and integrated during interpretation. FINDINGS: Moral distress was associated with factors across individual, relational and organisational contexts. Greater moral resilience and a more supportive ethical climate were associated with lower moral distress, whereas greater work-family conflict was associated with higher moral distress. Qualitative findings complemented these associations by highlighting how nurses described ethically challenging care in relation to sociocultural expectations surrounding life preservation and family-led decision-making. items.title: National Sentiment Towards Population Growth in Australian Towns and Cities
items.summary_raw: Accommodating future population growth is one of the biggest global challenges facing urban planning and design. The national population of Australia is projected to double by 2101, while community support for growth is far from unanimous. This paper reports on a national survey of sentiment towards population growth, specifically within respondents’ hometowns or cities. The survey reveals that most respondents supported population growth. However, quantitative and qualitative analyses lead to more nuanced findings, highlighting vital statistical differences in attitudes between geographic cohorts and concerns about future growth. The main drivers of resistance and factors that support population growth within urban and rural communities are highlighted with implications for more responsive urban planning and design strategies.

items.title: Green investments and urbanization in Sub-Saharan Africa: Do renewable energy investments also matter to SDG11?
items.summary_raw: The unprecedented rate of urbanization in Sub-Saharan Africa combined with extreme environmental and developmental pressures highlights the urgent need to comprehend how green investment influences the trajectories of urbanization and sustainability outcomes. This paper examines the twofold effect of green investment on urban agglomeration and sustainable cities and communities in 36 Sub-Saharan African countries from 2001 to 2024. Using two-stage least squares, feasible generalized least squares, panel Granger causality, and income-stratified robustness checks, the results show that green investment significantly restrains unplanned urban concentration and at the same time promotes sustainable urban development, reflecting its spatially redistributive nature. Access to electricity and GDP per capita become the leading drivers of structural urbanization, whereas the quality of regulations has income-contingent governance impacts. The mutually reinforcing nature of urbanization, green investment, and sustainable cities and communities is confirmed by bidirectional causality among key variables. Importantly, institutional capacity is found to be a consequence of sustainable urban development, but not a precondition, providing valuable sequencing information. To promote inclusive, sustainable urbanization in line with SDG11, policymakers should lower barriers to accessing green finance, enhance regulatory frameworks, and implement spatial planning reforms to direct green…

items.title: Evolving response of a community to offshore wind energy development – an evaluation of human adaptation to transition
items.source_name: Journal of Environmental Planning and Management
items.summary_raw: This paper explores responses of host communities to offshore wind energy infrastructure through a case study of the Aberdeen Offshore Wind Farm (OWF), situated 2.4 km off the coast of northeast Scotland. Adopting a longitudinal mixed-methods research approach, the nearby communities’ evolving responses are explored across four phases of OWF development: pre-consent, consent, construction, and early operation. Schlossberg’s theory of human adaptation to transition is adopted as an analytical framework to explore how the factors and variables that mediate between human transition and adaptation are manifest in the case study. The conclusions demonstrate that human adaptation was shaped by the externally imposed nature of the transition, historic land legacy issues and the presence of an already altered physical environment. This paper offers original insight to the wider elements that can influence the socio-technical dimensions of energy transitions and the importance of developing long-term understanding of what supports human adaptation.

items.title: Patterns of implicit and explicit attitudes V: Increases in bias from 2021 to 2025
items.summary_raw: Between 2007 and 2020, implicit and explicit intergroup attitudes declined in bias steadily and were forecasted to continue toward attitude neutrality. But, since 2020, 5 y of new data (2021–2025) from 2.8 million U.S. respondents reveal that past trends have stalled or, in some cases, even reversed. The largest reversals in bias emerged for sexuality, transgender, race, and skin-tone bias which increased by 12 to 22% on implicit measures and by 24% to more than tripling on explicit measures. Age, disability, and body weight bias also increased, but at relatively slower rates. Breakpoint analyses showed that implicit attitudes were early indicators of change, reversing trend ~1 y earlier than explicit reports. For most topics, reversals were widespread across demographic groups and even extended to an international sample of 274,884 non-U.S. respondents. However, younger respondents (<20-y-old)—who had previously shown the largest decreases in bias—now showed the largest increases in bias; these trends also interacted with politics and gender (e.g., young conservative men were the most likely to increase). Exploratory analyses ruled out various single-cause explanations. Instead, we suggest that the best explanation is that 2020–2021 marked a turning point in the sociopolitical climate, whereby co-occurring existential threats from the COVID-19 pandemic, amplified economic insecurity, political sectarianism, and online toxicity prompted increases in intergroup bias. These…

items.title: Regulatory Uncertainty: Asset Allocation and Asset Pricing
items.summary_raw: Abstract Regulatory uncertainty is a central channel through which policy affects financial decisions. We develop a programmatic conceptual framework for studying regulatory uncertainty in asset allocation and asset pricing. We define regulatory uncertainty as uncertainty about the design, timing, implementation, interpretation, and enforcement of regulations that directly shape cash flows, feasible actions, institutional constraints, and market expectations. This perspective distinguishes regulatory uncertainty from broader economic policy uncertainty by focusing on regulations, regulatory parameters, and enforcement practices rather than on policy uncertainty in general. The framework identifies four main entry points into financial models: cash-flow dynamics, beliefs and learning, regulatory constraints including tax constraints, and intermediary capital and liquidity constraints. It also clarifies when regulatory uncertainty is merely reflected in expected cash flows and when it commands a risk premium. We illustrate the framework in selected domains in which regulatory uncertainty is economically important: financial regulation, climate policy, taxation, and insurance. We thereby provide a common language for connecting theoretical modeling, measurement, and empirical analysis of regulatory uncertainty and for deriving implications for investors, firms, intermediaries, and regulators.

items.title: A three-stage roadmap and key issue outlook for China’s hydrogen energy industry toward 2060
items.summary_raw: Abstract China has recently elevated hydrogen energy to a strategic priority within its national energy security framework. As policy support, technology maturation, and regulatory integration advance, the sector is moving from preliminary demonstration toward more systematic deployment. This study develops a three-stage roadmap for China’s hydrogen energy industry toward 2060 by integrating techno-economic modeling, scenario analysis, and policy-target cross-checking. The results suggest a staged evolution within the broader energy system: scenario-specific enablement through 2030, system regulation and cross-sector integration during 2030−2040, and a possible foundational energy-carrier role by 2060. In the current phase, hydrogen deployment is constrained by high renewable-hydrogen costs, incomplete safety regulation, and system-compatibility barriers; its role therefore remains concentrated in selected industrial and mobility applications. In the mid-term phase, declining renewable-hydrogen costs and maturing storage and transportation networks could allow hydrogen to support long-duration energy storage, renewable-power integration, and industrial decarbonization. In the long term, hydrogen may form a dual-carrier energy architecture with electricity, provided that technology, safety governance, infrastructure, and standards continue to mature. The proposed roadmap offers a structured reference for hydrogen-related policy planning, infrastructure investment, and future…

items.title: Public lands and forest-based climate solutions: perceptions, policy support, and management preferences
items.source_name: Frontiers in Forests and Global Change
items.summary_raw: This study examines public support for forest-based climate solutions on U.S. public lands using data from a nonprobability Qualtrics panel of U.S. adults. We use a partial proportional-odds model to examine support for prioritizing carbon storage, and a multivariate ordered probit model to jointly evaluate support for six forest-carbon management strategies. Respondents expressed stronger support for restoration- and resilience-oriented strategies, particularly post-disturbance recovery and wildfire-risk reduction, than for limiting forest conversion. Climate-change awareness and support for immediate climate action were positively associated with carbon prioritization and all six management strategies. Carbon concern and familiarity were also positively associated with carbon prioritization, although their relationships with individual strategies varied. Among public-land values, ecological value was positively associated with most management strategies, while social value was particularly relevant to disturbance-risk reduction and several restoration-oriented strategies. We also found that trust in scientists and public agencies, public-land visitation, age, distance, and household income showed significant but varying associations with carbon prioritization and individual management strategies. These findings indicate that public acceptance of forest-carbon management is strategy-specific and reflects climate orientations, public-land values, familiarity, and…

items.title: Explosive price dynamics consistent with bubble-like behavior in clean and traditional energy investments: A GSADF approach amidst global events
items.summary_raw: This study examines explosive price dynamics consistent with bubble-like behavior in clean and renewable energy ETFs, index, and equities compared to traditional energy counterparts, using the Generalized Supremum Augmented Dickey-Fuller (GSADF) test across four subperiods: Pre-Paris Agreement, Paris Agreement, COVID-19, and Russia-Ukraine War. Using daily price data for clean energy assets (ICLN, QCLN, CELS, ENPH, AEIS) and traditional energy assets (VDE, IXC, XLE, USEG), the analysis reveals pronounced prevalence of explosive price episodes in clean energy markets, with 76.55% of explosive price episodes in the Pre-agreement period and 72.66% during COVID-19, consistent with speculative dynamics. Traditional energy assets exhibit greater resilience, with limited explosive episodes, notably only USEG during the Russia-Ukraine War. The novel segmented subperiod approach, combined with GSADF’s precise bubble date-stamping of explosive episodes, distinguishes this study by offering granular insights into sector-specific vulnerabilities, unlike prior broader analyses. The findings indicate that selected clean energy instruments exhibited more frequent explosive price episodes during crisis periods than their traditional energy counterparts, a pattern that may inform risk assessment and further research relevant to SDG 7 (Affordable and Clean Energy) and SDG 13 (Climate Action) but does not by itself warrant specific investment or policy recommendations.

items.title: Perceptions and Attitudes Toward Plant-Based Meat Alternatives: A Systematic Meta-Ethnography Review
items.summary_raw: CONTEXT: Plant-based meat alternatives (PBMAs) can support the transition toward healthier and more sustainable dietary patterns. However, PBMA adoption remains limited despite availability and awareness of health and environmental benefits, highlighting a gap between potential and practice. OBJECTIVE: This review sought to synthesize evidence on perceptions and attitudes toward PBMAs across populations and to examine how sociodemographic factors shape consumer perspectives. DATA SOURCES: A comprehensive search was conducted across MEDLINE, CINAHL, Web of Science, Greenfile, and Cochrane from inception to August 2025. DATA EXTRACTION: This systematic review was informed by meta-ethnographic principles (4 to 6), while qualitative data were synthesized using thematic synthesis. Qualitative data from eligible studies were analyzed using a thematic synthesis assisted by ATLAS.ti software and an inductive and iterative approach for coding. Quality assessment employed the Critical Appraisal Skills Programme (CASP) checklist, and confidence in findings was evaluated using the GRADE-CERQual (Confidence in Evidence from Reviews of Qualitative Research) approach. DATA ANALYSIS: This review included 31 studies with a total of 2425 participants (aged 9 to > 65 years) from the Asia-Pacific (n = 14), Europe (n = 14), the United States (n = 1), and the United Kingdom (n = 4). items.title: Effect of Adoption of Green Construction Practices on Sustainability of Public Infrastructure Projects in Rwanda: A Case of Kigali Green Complex, City of Kigali
items.source_name: International Journal of Innovative Science and Research Technology (IJISRT)
items.summary_raw: The study examines the effect of adopting green construction practices on the sustainability of public infrastructure projects in Rwanda, focusing on the Kigali Green Complex as a case study. The general objective was to assess how integrated green practices influence environmental sustainability, while specific objectives explored the contributions of energy-efficient building systems, renewable energy technologies, sustainable water management practices, and low-carbon construction materials. The research employed a mixed-methods approach using a descriptive and correlational research design. The study population was 212 stakeholders while sample size was 139 respondents. Stratified random sampling and purposive sampling were used. Data were collected using structured questionnaires. Quantitative data were analyzed using descriptive statistics (means and standard deviations), Pearson correlation, and multiple linear regression. Findings from descriptive statistics indicated high adoption levels of green construction practices, with mean scores above 4.0 across all variables.

items.title: Do Ads Persuade Voters in Direct Democratic Campaigns?
items.summary_raw: Abstract One of the primary goals of political campaigns is to shape voters' decisions. Despite elites spending money on advertising, its effectiveness in persuading voters remains a subject of debate. Based on theories of attitude change, I argue that increased exposure to advertising persuades voters to change their vote intention in the direction of the ads. Moreover, this study examines the moderating effect of sophistication on the relationship between ad exposure and vote choice. To test the effect of print and online advertisements on vote change, I link detailed campaign advertisement data to individual‐level rolling cross‐section panel data from the 2023 Climate Law referendum in Switzerland. The findings show that exposure to advertisements against the Climate Law significantly influences vote change, while exposure to ads in favor does not reach statistical significance. Evidence regarding sophistication's moderating role is limited.

items.title: The Creation and Legacy of “Have Americans’ Social Attitudes Become More Polarized”
items.summary_raw: Thirty years ago, Paul DiMaggio, Bethany Bryson and I published an article in the American Journal of Sociology titled “Have Americans’ Social Attitudes Become More Polarized?” In this article, I recount some of the social context and process of creating the article and describe how it exemplifies the DiMaggio academic style. The style is: (a) a focus on conceptualization of social processes that have previously been only vaguely described; (b) a push for innovation in measurement and estimation; (c) attention to social theory. I finish by showing the influence and legacy of this paper over the past 30 years. While the topical foci of scholars change, as do their measures and methods, the emphasis on conceptualization in the paper has guaranteed its enduring legacy.

items.title: China’s Energy Structure Transition Toward Carbon Neutrality: Carbon Emission Characteristics, Bottleneck Constraints and Prospects
items.source_name: Academic Journal of Science and Technology
items.summary_raw: Against the backdrop of escalating global climate change and energy security pressures, promoting a low-carbon transformation of the energy structure has become a crucial pathway to achieving sustainable development. China is currently at a critical stage of synergistically advancing economic development, energy security, and carbon emission reduction targets. This paper reviews the evolution of China's energy supply and demand structure in recent years and further explores the main constraints of energy structure, technological innovation, and grid absorption capacity on the low-carbon energy transition. Research shows that China's energy structure is gradually shifting towards a low-carbon direction, with the proportion of fossil fuel supply and consumption continuing to decline, carbon emissions from some key industrial sectors stabilizing or decreasing, and positive progress being made in energy electrification and new energy development. However, resource constraints, key technological bottlenecks, and insufficient grid absorption capacity for high proportions of new energy remain significant factors hindering the energy transition. In the future, China's energy system will further develop towards zero-carbon supply, electrified consumption, distributed energy storage, and intelligent dispatch. Accelerating breakthroughs in key technologies such as hydrogen energy, advanced energy storage, and carbon capture, utilization, and storage (CCUS) is essential to support the…

items.title: Elevating Indigenous Voices for a Just Energy Transition
items.summary_raw: In the face of an accelerating climate crisis and shifting geopolitical power balances, the world is pursuing a “green transition” in which electrification is central. Electrification demands critical raw materials, including rare earth elements, a large share of which lie beneath Indigenous lands. Although the UN affirms Indigenous peoples’ right to own, use, develop, and control their traditional lands, these rights are routinely overruled, including on “national security” grounds. The newly discovered Per Geijer deposit in Northern Sweden—Europe’s largest known rare earth elements find—sits at the centre of these tensions. Drawing upon a workshop, field visits, and a narrative review of academic, policy, and media sources, this article examines three competing narratives surrounding the proposed new mine: the “green transition,” “national security,” and “energy justice” narratives, which we read in relation to the “energy trilemma.” Focusing on cumulative threats to the Gabna reindeer-herding community from Kiruna’s century-old iron ore mine and the proposed Per Geijer project, we explore the power imbalances that determine which stories are heard in energy transition decision-making, and which are marginalised. We argue that recognition, restorative, and intergenerational justice principles need to be brought to the centre of transition planning. items.title: Navigating the nexus how climate change risk perception and economic dependence influence local support for sustainable tourism
items.source_name: Revista Rosa dos Ventos - Turismo e Hospitalidade
items.summary_raw: This study examines the mediating role of economic dependence in the influence of local people's climate change risk perception on their support for sustainable tourism development in a climate-sensitive and economically tourism-dependent region. Integrating Protection Motivation Theory and Social Exchange Theory the research analyzes how threat perceptions and economic interests shape sustainable tourism development attitudes. Structural Equation Modeling was used with data collected from 397 local residents in Rize, Türkiye. The findings show that climate change risk perception positively influences both economic dependence and support for sustainable tourism development, and economic dependence positively influences support for sustainable tourism development. Most importantly, economic dependence was found to play a significant partial mediating role in the relationship between climate change risk perception and sustainable tourism development support, i.e., the effect of climate change risk perception on sustainable tourism development is partially mediated by perceived economic security. The study contributes to theoretical understanding by identifying economic dependence as a key mechanism in the protection motivation theory -social exchange theory interaction and provides policy recommendations that balance climate risk communication with the economic benefits of sustainable tourism development. This is particularly important for regions facing dual pressures of…

items.title: Arrow's shadow over climate governance
items.summary_raw: For thirty years, climate negotiations have failed to produce a stable and widely accepted rule for distributing mitigation burdens, even as finance, technology, and loss and damage have advanced. Political will, free-riding, and domestic constraints explain part of that, but not why the deadlock persists. This paper contends that the challenge is structural. It uses Arrow's voting paradox to diagnose the burden-sharing track of the climate negotiations and to draw the institutional consequences. Burden-sharing constitutes a preference-aggregation problem involving incompatible fairness principles. Arrow's impossibility theorem elucidates both the nature and direction of this difficulty: no procedure can transform divergent rankings of historical responsibility, capability, and equal per capita claims into a single, stable, and broadly accepted formula. Although the theorem does not establish formal impossibility within a treaty context or explain any specific negotiation breakdown, it highlights a constraint that neither improved analysis nor increased commitment has overcome.Because the constraint is structural and unsolvable, agreement proceeds by working around the aggregation problem. Issue linkage relaxes Arrow’s independence condition, while the Paris Agreement shifts aggregation from an ex ante distribution to self-differentiation, focal points, and an ex post stocktake of collective progress. Sen’s comparative justice helps explain why this works: parties need not…

items.title: Fiscal responses to the European energy crisis: Trade-offs in targeting household relief measures
items.summary_raw: The 2021-2023 energy price shock compelled European governments to shield households while navigating four, often competing, objectives: delivering meaningful relief, containing fiscal costs and inflation, preserving energy conservation incentives, and maintaining public support. This study presents the first cross-national comparative analysis of how 18 EU member states managed these perceived trade-offs. By integrating Bruegel’s Fiscal Tracker with uprated Eurostat Household Budget Survey microdata, we model the allocation of fiscal support for 229 household-oriented interventions across four dimensions: benefit adequacy, targeting efficiency, environmental sustainability, and political salience. Initial responses favoured broad-based, highly visible measures that offered rapid but diffuse relief; over time, governments pivoted towards more targeted schemes, enhancing the distributive impact and environmental alignment of support. Nordic packages were sustainable yet largely inconspicuous, while Central and Eastern European schemes maximised visibility but were relatively regressive and blunted conservation signals. Western and Mediterranean European countries that combined tiered price caps with targeted transfers exemplified how ‘targeting within universalism’ can reconcile competing objectives. The four-dimensional evaluative framework developed herein underscores that the design of crisis relief is inherently political. It offers a transferable tool for assessing…
