items.title: How 20th-century immigrants did not have to change their last names in order to become American
items.summary_raw: Reports of parents’ names in Social Security Application records allow us to quantify at a population level the extent and nature of historical last name changes by immigrants. Our analysis of European, Middle Eastern, and Asian immigrants of the early to mid-20th-century finds that more than 80% kept their last names. Computational linguistic analysis shows that most of those who did change preserved their surname’s ethnic signal, leaving only about 5% of all immigrants trying to disguise their foreign origins. Of these, Jewish immigrants had the highest rate of ethnicity-concealing last name changes; Italian, Japanese, and Chinese immigrants all had the lowest. Our proposed framework helps understand the variation: name changes were rarest where ethnic community networks were densest and where passing as unmarked was least credible—as among visibly non-White immigrants. Our findings challenge the dominant assimilationist narrative that immigrants in this era had to shed their foreign identities to enter the American mainstream. “Becoming White” by adopting an English surname was not a large part of historical immigrant experience. Rather, the overwhelming majority of immigrants chose to openly preserve their ethnic origins. Our results also suggest that nominal record linkage of historical immigrant populations may be more feasible than previously assumed.

items.title: Forcing dataset updates impact regional but not global Earth radiation budget trends in the GFDL AM4 climate model
items.summary_raw: The availability of up-to-date forcing datasets is critical for reconciling Earth system model simulations with contemporary observations. With the newly released CMIP7 forcing dataset, which extends the historical record through 2021, this study provides a systematic evaluation of how using updated forcings over the “middle-of-the-road” SSP2-4.5 scenario forcings influences the simulated radiation budget in the GFDL AM4 climate model. The updated forcing dataset used in the atmosphere model does not improve the agreement between the simulated global-mean top-of-the-atmosphere radiation trends and the satellite-observed trends. Regionally, we identify pronounced shifts in radiative energy partitioning between atmosphere and surface. Specifically, during 2001–2021, accelerated reductions in sulfate and black carbon aerosols over East Asia drive a significant decline in atmospheric solar absorption that matches observations, while a substantial increase in organic aerosols at higher latitudes induces a localized increase in atmospheric absorption that does not match observations. The substantial influence of localized forcing changes on simulated regional climate underscores the necessity for routine updates of forcing datasets.

items.title: Engineered T cell–agonist chimera for logic-gated STING activation and augmented cancer immunotherapy
items.summary_raw: The efficacy of adoptive T cell therapy against solid tumors is markedly hindered by the immunosuppressive microenvironment. Here, we demonstrate that stimulator of interferon genes (STING) activation in tumor-associated macrophages (TAM) enhances the intratumoral infiltration and cytotoxicity of adoptive T cells. We next design a TAM-targeted nanoagonist and engineer a T cell – agonist chimera (SNTC) via covalent surface anchoring, to achieve synchronized biodistribution of STING agonist with adoptive T cells. The nanoagonist is locally released in tumor tissue in response to the elevated reduction potential on T cell surface, followed by intracellular glutathione-mediated restoration of STING agonist in TAM, thereby enabling AND logic-gated STING activation. SNTC not only reshapes tumor stroma and immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment to augment adoptive T cell function but also enhances the antigen presentation ability of TAM to activate endogenous T cells. SNTC elicits robust antitumor efficacy in melanoma tumor-bearing mice, resulting in over 40% survival beyond 60 d. Moreover, combining tumor-infiltrating T lymphocyte (TIL)-based SNTC with immune checkpoint blockade therapy leads to sustained tumor regression in mouse model of orthotopic pancreatic tumor. Collectively, SNTC holds translational potential to optimize STING activation for adoptive T cell therapy of cancer.

items.title: Rapid target engagement of KRAS G12C tricomplex inhibitor RO3903 overcomes resistance and drives durable tumor regression
items.summary_raw: The clinical durability of first-generation KRAS G12C inhibitors is constrained by resistance mechanisms, primarily the rapid, receptor tyrosine kinase (RTK)-mediated reactivation of KRAS to its drug-insensitive, guanosine triphosphate (GTP)-bound (ON) state. Here, we perform a systematic comparative characterization of clinical and investigational KRAS G12C inhibitors, including Sotorasib, Adagrasib, Divarasib, and Elironrasib, and our structurally optimized tricomplex ON inhibitor, RO7783903 (RO3903). We demonstrate that the covalent tricomplex inhibitors RO3903 and Elironrasib effectively outpace dynamic nucleotide cycling, conferring resilience to potent RTK stimulation and overcoming the secondary KRAS mutations that drive clinical resistance to guanosine diphosphate (GDP)-bound (OFF) state inhibitors. Notably, RO3903 potently inhibits tumor growth in a dose-dependent manner across multiple preclinical models, including an orthotopic intracranial model. Furthermore, RO3903 exhibits synergistic efficacy when combined with inhibitors targeting OFF-state KRAS G12C, YAP-TEAD, EGFR/MET, or FAK, as well as with anti-PD1 antibody and anti-PD1/VEGF bispecific antibody immunotherapies. The high potency, fast target engagement, and brain tumor inhibition of RO3903 position this molecule as a valuable tool reagent and a promising partner for combination strategies to achieve durable tumor regression.

items.title: Subcellular compartment determines signal dominance: Endosomal cAMP overrides concurrent plasma membrane RhoA activation from a single receptor
items.summary_raw: Cells convey information not only via the identity of activated signaling pathways but also through the subcellular location where those signals originate. Whether spatially distinct signals from a single activated receptor compete to determine net cellular output has remained unclear. Here, we demonstrate this principle for a G-protein-coupled receptor (GPCR), showing that endosomal and plasma membrane signals from a single activated receptor are not merely distinct but functionally opposed, with endosomal signaling predominating to reverse the net cellular output. Using the adhesion GPCR GPR64/ADGRG2 as a model system, we show that ligand activation engages two spatially distinct G-protein pathways that are not just additive but functionally opposed: plasma membrane G 13 /RhoA activation and Gs/cAMP production that persists from endosomes following receptor internalization. The endosomal cAMP pool actively overrides concurrent plasma membrane RhoA activation, resulting in net RhoA inactivation, an outcome that is completely reversed by pharmacological blockade of endocytosis or endosomal G s inactivation. In parathyroid cells, where GPR64 is highly expressed, this endosomal signal dominance suppresses parathyroid hormone secretion independently of extracellular Ca 2+ levels. These findings support a model in which the subcellular compartment, rather than pathway identity, determines the dominant signal and the overall cellular response of a single activated receptor, with…

items.title: Coacervate droplets as a liquefier for the solid-to-liquid transition of RNA aggregates
items.summary_raw: Biomolecular condensates are functionally gated by their material properties. While RNA is a primary structural scaffold, its sequence-specific interactions can aberrantly drive condensates into dysfunctional solid aggregates. Yet, actively reversing this solidification to restore function remains a fundamental challenge, impeding progress in synthetic biology and therapeutics interventions. Here, we establish that complex coacervates can be engineered as liquefiers to actively remodel solid RNA–peptide aggregates into functional liquid droplets. Integrating systematic experiments with all-atom simulations, we decode a multiscale mechanism: coacervate infiltration at the micrometer scale mediates molecular buffering at the nanometer scale, which fluidizes the crosslinked network to drive macroscopic liquefaction. This capability is governed by a design rule, where coacervates formed by small-molecular anions exhibit optimal efficacy. We deploy this principle to functionally rescue silenced RNA within a model of pathologically solidified ribonucleoprotein assemblies. Our work provides a general framework for the active, compositional control of biomolecular phase behavior, with direct implications for managing pathological aggregation and engineering functional condensates in synthetic and living systems.

items.title: Rising cell-free DNA level tracks cancer-associated methylation signal and improves multicancer detection
items.summary_raw: Cancer patients carry more circulating cell-free DNA (ccfDNA)—small DNA fragments shed into the blood—than healthy people. Most of this excess comes not from the tumor itself but from immune cells, suggesting that it would simply dilute the much smaller amount of tumor-derived DNA in a blood sample. Using a study of 1,480 previously untreated participants across 43 hospitals—including patients with 14 cancer types spanning all stages, patients with benign growths, and healthy volunteers—we show the opposite: as total ccfDNA rises, it becomes enriched, not diluted, in fragments carrying cancer-associated DNA methylation signatures, independent of cancer type, disease stage, and a broad panel of demographic, clinical, and technical covariates. In fact, total ccfDNA explains more variance in cancer-associated methylation signal than the disease stage itself. This basic biological finding suggests a coupling between immune cell activity and tumor methylation. It also has a practical implication: we show that rising ccfDNA concentration is associated with higher cancer detection sensitivity, even within disease stages and particularly in early-stage disease—stage I sensitivity varied from 0.55 in the lowest ccfDNA concentration tertile to 0.85 in the highest, and stage II from 0.59 to 0.86. This suggests that ccfDNA concentration should be considered as a stage-independent stratification variable for benchmarking cancer-detection tests. Interestingly, similar behavior was…

items.title: Spontaneous gas film expansion at an oil–water interface
items.summary_raw: Spontaneous interfacial separation of oil and water, by inserting a gas film between the two liquids, is thermodynamically unfavorable because the oil–water interface is replaced by oil–gas and water–gas interfaces with a higher combined interfacial energy. Here, we demonstrate that microstructural confinement enables this transition after bubble introduction through the coupling of wetting, capillarity, and gas transport. Spontaneous oil imbibition into a water-submerged micropillar array, together with local contact-line pinning, deforms the oil–water interface into a metastable meniscus and generates a local pressure deficit in the confined oil. This deficit, combined with the bubble’s interfacial configuration, lowers its air partial pressure and promotes dissolved-air uptake from the surrounding water. Geometric confinement, reduced oil pressure, and low oil–gas interfacial tension favor bubble lateral invasion of adjacent oil-filled cells over vertical extrusion. As the gas front advances, meniscus relaxation and oil redistribution promote further wetting, renewing the capillary conditions that support gas film propagation. We develop a coupled transport-capillarity framework that captures these morphological transitions and predicts a characteristic timescale for gas film evolution, determined by the interaction among geometry, capillarity, and gas-phase transport. Spatially varying the microstructure further controls the propagation pathway and morphology of the gas…

items.title: Senescent CD8 T effector memory cells are functionally impaired, enriched in aging and disease, and a barrier to immunotherapy
items.summary_raw: Senescent cells play important roles in various biological processes that promote fitness and health; however, their timely elimination by immune cells is critical to maintain tissue homeostasis and prevent disease. Despite this, senescent cells accumulate systemically with age, suggesting that certain immune cells also become senescent and dysfunctional during aging. In support of this, we previously demonstrated that CD8 T cells, immune cells capable of targeting senescent cells, increasingly develop characteristics of senescence with advancing age in humans. Here, we characterized the senescence state of human SA-βGal-expressing (SA-βGal high ) CD8 T effector memory (EM) cells, their functional capabilities, and their enrichment in aging and disease. Single-cell RNA sequencing revealed that SA-βGal high CD8 T cells with unique transcriptional signatures develop in all stages of T cell differentiation, including in CD8 T EM cells, which increased in abundance with human aging. SA-βGal high CD8 T EM cells expressed various classical markers of senescence and were significantly impaired in their ability to proliferate, produce cytokines, and eliminate senescent human stromal cells. Gene signatures of senescent SA-βGal high CD8 T EM cells were enriched in CD8 T cells from older human donors, patients with age-related disorders, cancer, and in smokers. Furthermore, we show that T cell senescence is distinct from and dominant over T cell exhaustion, limiting the response of CD8…

items.title: Core effectors of the Fusarium pan-effectome contribute to host specificity
items.summary_raw: Fusarium fungi cause economically important diseases of cereal crops, including Fusarium head blight, ear blight, and root rot. Central to these interactions are secreted effector proteins that manipulate host biology to promote infection. In turn, plants have evolved to recognize effector activity to activate immune responses and restrict disease. Despite their importance, the diversity, conservation, and evolution of Fusarium effectors remain poorly understood. Here, we present the Fusarium sambucinum Species complex Effector Compendium (FUSEC), a sequence-defined pan-effectome constructed from 188 high-quality genomes representing 27 species. FUSEC comprises 4,057 sequence-defined effector families, including a conserved soft-core repertoire of 235 families present in at least 95% of isolates. Structure-guided comparisons reorganized these conserved families into 184 structure-defined groups, revealing relationships that extend beyond sequence similarity and identifying similarities to numerous experimentally characterized fungal (a)virulence factors. Despite their broad conservation, soft-core families exhibited substantial within-family sequence diversity, and analyses of diversifying selection identified 44 candidate families undergoing adaptive evolution. Functional screening revealed that the majority of these candidates altered wheat immune responses, and CRISPR-Cas9-mediated gene deletions in Fusarium graminearum demonstrated that multiple conserved effectors…

items.title: Extracellular polymeric substances drive Curvibacter host adaptation and cospeciation with Hydra
items.summary_raw: The interactions between hosts and their microbial symbionts play a crucial role to host physiology. Bacteria can adapt to specific host environments over evolutionary timescales, leading to cospeciation and the formation of specialized host–microbe relationships. Understanding the molecular mechanisms underlying these adaptations provides key insights into the evolution of symbiosis and the stability of microbial communities. This study investigates the cospeciation and molecular adaptations of Curvibacter to its host Hydra , a well-established model for the study of host–microbe interactions. We provide strong evidence of cospeciation, as demonstrated by phylogenetic congruence between different Hydra species and their corresponding Curvibacter symbionts, along with preferential recolonization of germ-free Hydra by their native Curvibacter strains. Comparative genomic analyses reveal that host-associated Curvibacter strains exhibit distinct metabolic and biosynthetic adaptations compared to their free-living relatives. Specifically, the enrichment of proteins linked to host glycan interactions, extracellular polymeric substances (EPS), DNA metabolic processes, ABC transport, sugar metabolism, and bacterial chemotaxis highlights specialized adaptations of Curvibacter symbionts within the Hydra glycocalyx. Importantly, some of these signatures are only detectable within the Hydra vulgaris -associated Curvibacter subgroup, emphasizing the need to examine host-specific…

items.title: Coupled outward and inward oxide growth during metal oxidation
items.summary_raw: Metal oxidation is traditionally described as a dichotomy: oxide scales grow either outward via cation diffusion or inward via anion diffusion, with the dominant pathway determined by the prevailing point defects in the oxide lattice. Here, we demonstrate that these two modes are not mutually exclusive but intrinsically coupled within a single oxidation process. Using in situ environmental transmission electron microscopy to monitor the oxidation of copper—a canonical cationic system—we directly visualize simultaneous oxide propagation at both the O 2 /Cu 2 O surface interface and the buried Cu 2 O/Cu interface. Complementary simulations reveal the mechanistic origin of this behavior. Outward cation transport during surface oxide growth injects a sustained flux of vacancies into the underlying metal lattice, which facilitates inward oxygen incorporation and drives oxide growth at the buried interface. This vacancy-mediated feedback couples cationic and anionic transport process, providing a unified framework in which surface cationic growth directly enables inward anionic-driven growth. By identifying vacancy injection as a key mediator of interfacial mass transport, this work provides a mechanistic basis for predicting oxidation kinetics and defect-regulated solid-state transformation pathways in reactive environments.

items.title: Geochemical signatures of magnetite are conserved in diverse populations of environmental magnetotactic bacteria
items.summary_raw: Magnetotactic bacteria (MTB) synthesize intracellular magnetite nanoparticles in a genetically controlled manner. They may represent some of the earliest biomineralizing organisms on Earth, and a unique window into ancient life and the environments that hosted it. Yet, identification of their mineralogical remains in ancient rocks is highly challenging due to the lack of reliable and lasting proxies. Previous results obtained from laboratory cultures of single strains of MTB revealed trace element and Fe isotope patterns that are not shared by any other source of magnetite, which could be used as reliable proxies for the identification of ancient MTB. However, the environmental relevance of these previous findings for environmental and mixed population of MTB is unknown. We report the trace element and Fe isotope compositions of magnetite extracted from environmental MTB collected in the water column of Lake Pavin, France, and show that the most distinctive geochemical traits (enrichment in Mo, Se, Sn, and light Fe isotopes) of magnetite produced by MTB cultivated in the laboratory are conserved in environmental populations. They represent potential biological signatures that can be searched in ancient rocks and coupled with magnetic and mineralogical tracers to support the presence of MTB and reconstruct their emergence and evolution.

items.title: Hepatocyte-derived exosomal miR-122 mediates liver-to-brain crosstalk and neuroinflammation in alcohol-exposed Alzheimer’s disease mice
items.summary_raw: Neuroinflammation and microglial activation are common features in Alzheimer’s disease (AD) and excessive alcohol consumption. Alcohol induces liver damage and inflammation, and altered serum aminotransferases have been reported in patients with AD. Small extracellular vesicles (sEVs) and their cargo are emerging as mediators of intercellular communication in AD and alcohol-induced liver injury. However, the effects of alcohol use on AD progression remain to be elucidated. In this study, we evaluated the effects of repeated binge drinking on the liver and brain in the APP/PS1 mouse model of AD. Alcohol-exposed APP/PS1 mice showed elevated serum alanine aminotransferase levels, indicating liver injury absent in controls, along with increased pro-inflammatory cytokine expression in both liver and brain. Alcohol increased the biogenesis and release of sEVs in AD mice and in mouse hepatocytes. These sEVs were enriched in mature miR-122-5p that is predominant in hepatocytes. In vivo, miR-122-5p was detected in the brain of alcohol-exposed AD mice suggesting EV-mediated miR-122-5p transfer to the brain. Microglial uptake of hepatocyte-derived sEVs was confirmed in vitro. sEVs from alcohol-treated hepatocytes sensitized BV-2 microglia to LPS stimulation, significantly enhancing CCL2, CXCL2, CCL3, and TNF-α production. Transfection of microglia with a miR-122-5p mimic partially recapitulated the pro-inflammatory sensitization by sEVs from alcohol-exposed hepatocytes, which was…

items.title: Cooling fast and slow: Characterizing the effects of vitrification in cryo-EM and the subsequent recovery of equilibrium populations
items.summary_raw: Single-particle cryogenic electron microscopy (cryo-EM), a powerful class of techniques in structural biology with the potential to resolve molecular ensembles, requires that samples be vitrified to protect them from the high vacuum of the electron microscope. However, the effects of vitrification on biomolecular ensembles are unknown. To study them, we carried out extensive molecular dynamics simulations (over 50 ms) of the Trp-cage miniprotein at equilibrium and undergoing rapid cooling. We simulated seven cooling rates spanning three orders of magnitude, with the slowest coolings matching experimental rates. By inspecting molecular mobility and density-temperature trajectories for water with and without protein, we found that water vitrification is unaltered by the protein. To track protein conformation changes, and to relate them to kinetics, we made a Markov State Model (MSM) of Trp-cage from 5.4 ms of equilibrium sampling at 277 K. We observed that MSM states with a characteristic time longer than the duration of the nonequilibrium cooling tend to be more robust to artifacts induced by such cooling. Critically, although we observe that some states vanish in the equilibrium ensemble at 230 K, none do in our nonequilibrium cooled ensembles. To account for these perturbations, we developed a thermodynamic inference framework for recovering equilibrium populations from vitrified ensembles. These results indicate that cryo-EM has the capacity to be an accurate technique for…

items.title: Dissociation of gravity and limb dynamics in motor control
items.summary_raw: Human movements remain accurate across substantial variations in mechanical loading, yet how the nervous system anticipates and compensates for intrinsic and extrinsic forces when generating muscle commands remains unresolved. Because the forces acting on the body are complex and nonlinear, dynamical modeling provides a powerful framework for identifying the computations underlying motor control. Here, we exploited parabolic flight to dissociate gravitational loading from intrinsic limb dynamics and directly test how these mechanical components are represented in motor commands. We analyzed kinematics and shoulder muscle activity from nine participants performing visually guided pointing movements in microgravity (0g), normogravity (1g), and hypergravity (2g). Inverse dynamics revealed that the gravity-independent component of muscle torque remained invariant across gravitational conditions. In striking contrast, muscle moments estimated from muscle activation showed systematic scaling of not only static but also phasic components with gravitational load, particularly during movement deceleration. This divergence arises because activation-derived muscle moments capture cocontraction, and thus impedance-related control, that is absent from net torques obtained by inverse dynamics. Gravity-dependent regression analyses further showed that muscle activation could be reconstructed from a compact set of mechanical variables dominated by gravity-dependent torque and movement…

items.title: Epigenetic aging during the COVID-19 pandemic: A prospective longitudinal study with prepandemic baseline data in children, adolescents, and adults
items.summary_raw: Psychosocial stress is a risk factor for aging-related diseases. The COVID-19 pandemic placed a psychosocial burden on individuals, potentially increasing the risk for aging-related diseases for which epigenetic clocks are used as early biomarkers. Based on four epigenetic clocks (DunedinPACE, GrimAge2, Horvath, and PedBE), we investigated whether epigenetic aging changed during the pandemic and whether these changes were associated with objective and subjective pandemic-related stressors and preexisting individual risk factors for poorer physical and mental health. We used prospective longitudinal data (n = 1,028), including repeated salivary DNA collection from children (n = 359, MAGE = 9.5 y), adolescents (n = 385, MAGE = 15.5 y), and adults (n = 284, MAGE = 24.3 y). Saliva was collected before the first phase of containment measures in Germany in March 2020 and after the second phase in 2021. We observed significant increases in epigenetic age acceleration (PedBE: b = 0.17, P < 0.0001; GrimAge2: b = 0.08, P < 0.0001) and pace of aging (DunedinPACE: b = 0.13, P < 0.0001) across all age groups. Prepandemic physical health and parental socioeconomic status, but not objective pandemic stressors, were significantly associated with this change. In adolescents, higher perceived pandemic burden was associated with a larger increase in pace of aging (DunedinPACE: b = 0.04, P = 0.01). Together, these findings suggest that prepandemic individual risk factors for poorer physical and…

items.title: Hypothalamic lncRNA Synage prevents age-related sperm quality decline by suppressing A-type potassium currents in GnRH neurons
items.summary_raw: Age-related decline in male fertility, including diminished sperm quality, poses significant risks to offspring health and is exacerbated by modern trends toward delayed parenthood. Focusing on the hypothalamus–pituitary–testis axis, which governs hormonal control of male reproduction, we identified Synage , a long noncoding RNA expressed in the hypothalamic medial preoptic area (mPOA). We found that Synage expression in gonadotropin-releasing hormone (GnRH) neurons decreases with age, correlating with reduced sperm quality and male fertility. mPOA-targeted Synage _B (brain-specific isoform) supplementation increases serum testosterone and improves sperm count and progressive motility in 12-mo-old mice. Conversely, conditional deletion of Synage in GnRH neurons in young mice reduces GnRH neuron firing, decreases serum LH and testosterone levels, impaires sperm quality, and reduces male fertility. Mechanistically, Synage interacts with the heat shock protein HSPA8 and stabilizes the HSPA8–KCHIP4 interaction. Synage loss increases KCHIP4 abundance and its association with the Kv4.2 channel, promoting Kv4.2 membrane recruitment and enhancing A-type potassium currents ( I A ), thereby reducing GnRH neuronal excitability. Consistent with this model, GnRH neurons from 12-mo-old mice also exhibit reduced excitability. Together, these findings support a role for age-dependent Synage loss in reproductive decline, at least in part through dysregulation of the HSPA8–KCHIP4–Kv4.2…

items.title: Thermodynamic stabilization of substrate protein within the GroEL:ES chaperonin cage
items.summary_raw: The adenosine triphosphate (ATP)-regulated GroEL/ES chaperonin of Escherichia coli promotes protein folding by transiently encapsulating unfolded substrate protein in a nano-cage formed by the cylindrical GroEL and the lid-shaped GroES. How this confinement modulates the folding energy landscape, allowing accelerated protein folding unimpaired by aggregation, remains incompletely understood. Prompted by recent observations suggesting that the chaperonin cavity may favor unfolding [I. Korobko et al. , Proc. Natl. Acad. Sci. U.S.A. 119 , e2213170119 (2022)], here we reinvestigated the effect of encapsulation on protein thermodynamic stability. To allow thermal unfolding of an encapsulated substrate protein, we generated a destabilized variant of maltose-binding protein (MBP) by introducing four mutations, quadruple mutant-MBP (QM-MBP), lowering the melting temperature ( T m ) from 63.6 °C to 44.3 °C. GroEL/ES accelerated the slow spontaneous folding of QM-MBP ~20-fold. The protein reached a native-like structure while encapsulated inside GroEL:ES, as demonstrated using hydrogen/deuterium exchange and single molecule fluorescence resonance energy transfer analyses in presence and absence of the ligand maltose. Importantly, confinement in the thermally stable chaperonin shifted the cooperative unfolding transition of QM-MBP to a T m of 52.4 °C, corresponding to a stabilization by 4.6 kcal mol −1 . In-cage thermal unfolding was reversible, indicating that the environment of the…

items.title: Unpacking transatlantic income inequality
items.summary_raw: This paper uses newly harmonized survey and register data on incomes and labor market outcomes as the basis for consistent comparisons of inequalities across 17 North American and European countries over the period 1995–2021. We examine trends in disposable income inequality in the working-age population, defined as persons aged 25 to 60, as well as its component parts of market income inequality and redistribution through government tax and transfer systems. We adjust incomes to allow for changes in education, population aging, and household structure in each country. We test for convergence across countries in demographically-adjusted disposable income inequality, along with market income inequality and redistribution. There is strong evidence of convergence over time in disposable income inequality across the 17 countries, despite a divergence in the dispersion of market income inequality driven by very heterogeneous trends for hours of work and the number of workers in households across countries. Consistent with this we find a strong convergence across countries in the dispersion of our measure of redistribution. There are reductions over time in inequality-reducing redistribution in the Nordic countries and increases in some other European and North American countries, with the net effect being more similarity across countries, a lower average level of redistribution, and a higher average level of disposable income inequality. These trends are being driven by the…

items.title: Electric aviation is taking off in unexpected ways
items.summary_raw: The call came from a home in Hyde County, a rural expanse of coastal farmland and marsh in North Carolina. Paramedic Quinn Reece jumped into an electric aircraft with one seat, two wings, and eight propellers. It is called a BlackFly, and at about 14 feet long it looks like an oversized drone. Moments later it rose like a helicopter, then flew like an airplane. As she raced toward the emergency at about 60 mph, a dispatcher described the location. Reece quickly realized that the app the county uses for emergency response had given the wrong location. Because she had flown over the area before, Reece had an idea of the correct location. She zipped over in the aircraft, confirmed where the call had come from, and relayed the information to paramedics headed that way. She was on the scene and administering care 20 minutes before they arrived. That is exactly what Brook Cox, the county’s emergency medical services chief, hoped to see. She launched the six-month trial with a company called Pivotal in March to see if its BlackFly could help medics more quickly reach patients in a county that covers 1,459 square miles of land and water. The county conducted more than 300 training flights prior to using the aircraft for two 911 calls. Air taxis and flying cars have long defined the promise of electric vertical takeoff and landing aircraft, or eVTOLs. items.title: Louisiana’s accidental blueprint for restoring its coast
items.summary_raw: Arthur Matherne is used to speeding his airboat across a southeastern stretch of the Louisiana coast where lakes and bayous have widened as the Gulf of Mexico’s salty water has moved in, dissolving marshes and swamps. But in one tucked-away patch of the Barataria Basin’s 1.6 million acres, the semi-retired tour guide eases off the throttle as he tries to remember his way through channels that have grown tighter by the year. Grasses are overtaking the shallows, and oak branches are spreading overhead, dangling Spanish moss over waterways he once barreled through. “All this, it’s filling in,” Matherne said after shutting off his airboat’s roaring propeller. “Right here, it used to be three feet of water. Now it’s three inches.” What Matherne is seeing is a striking reversal of a pattern that has defined southern Louisiana for the past century. While much of the coastal zone has receded at about 11 square miles per year from erosion and other forces compounded by climate change, the wetlands here are gaining ground. The reason is just a few miles away. Near Luling in St. Charles Parish, the Davis Pond Freshwater Diversion has funneled Mississippi River water into the basin since the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers built it in 2002 to combat saltwater intrusion. But something unexpected happened. The diversion also carried the muddy river’s sediment into the wetlands, raising the bottom and helping create new land. “It’s had this unintended consequence of building land,” said Jacob…

Blackstone’s is one of several energy transition funds at private equity firms that have consistently grown over the past decade. That growth has continued even as general climate-oriented investment has fallen over the last few years. Colloquially, “energy transition” refers to the shift from fossil fuels to renewable energy that is necessary to limit the worst impacts of climate change. But on Wall Street, the term can mean something a bit different. Some transition funds — including Blackstone’s — see opportunities for profit in natural gas, data centers, and rising electricity costs. “I know a lot of the investors out there do consider gas a transition fuel,” said Ryan Loughead, a senior associate and former climate solutions analyst for BloombergNEF, an energy research firm. items.title: Between cost acceptance and opposition: On the limits of perceived costs as explanations of policy acceptability in street transformations
items.summary_raw: Street-space reallocation interventions are increasingly promoted to reduce car dependence, improve environmental quality and reclaim street space for everyday public life. Yet these measures also redistribute access, convenience and control over street space, making them politically contentious when residents anticipate personal costs. Importantly, perceived negative impacts do not necessarily coincide with opposition. Understanding why perceived losses are associated with non-acceptance for some individuals but not for others is crucial, because visible backlash can shape the political viability of urban sustainability transitions. This paper examines what distinguishes individuals who oppose street transformations while anticipating personal costs from those who remain non-oppositional despite such costs. Drawing on a survey of 2000 adults in Barcelona and its metropolitan area, we analyse four built-environment interventions: superblocks, pedestrianisations, bicycle lanes, and protected schools programmes. By crossing perceived personal impact with policy acceptability, we identify four attitudinal profiles and focus on two groups anticipating negative impacts: Self-interest opponents and Cost-accepters . Drawing on previous literature, respondents' justifications for anticipated negative impacts are grouped into four interpretative frames and analysed alongside socio-demographic, household and personal value orientations using intervention-specific binary logistic…

items.source_name: Wiley Interdisciplinary Reviews Energy and Environment
items.summary_raw: ABSTRACT Floating solar photovoltaics (FSPV) have emerged as a promising alternative to traditional ground‐mounted photovoltaic (GPV) systems. By deploying solar panels over water bodies such as lakes and reservoirs, FSPV systems mitigate land‐use constraints while enhancing energy performance and contributing to more effective water‐resource management. This paper presents a comprehensive review of FSPV technology, including its operational principles, technological developments, techno‐economic feasibility, environmental impacts, system reliability, and sustainability implications. One of the major advantages of FSPV systems is their enhanced energy generation compared with GPV installations. The presence of water beneath the modules provides a natural cooling effect that lowers the operating temperature of the panels and improves their efficiency. However, the level of performance improvement depends on climatic conditions, installation configuration, and system design. Beyond electricity generation, FSPV systems also provide several ancillary benefits related to water‐resource conservation and management. The coverage of water surfaces reduces evaporation losses and can support water conservation. Despite these benefits, FSPV deployment may also affect aquatic ecosystems and water quality. Therefore, proper site selection and environmental impact assessments are essential to minimize ecological disturbances. From an economic perspective, the initial capital cost of FSPV…

items.title: Energy Subsidies and the Climate Dilemma in Middle Eastern Petro-States: An Empirical Analysis
items.source_name: International Journal of Energy Economics and Policy
items.summary_raw: This study examines the link between fossil fuel subsidies and greenhouse gas emissions in five major Middle Eastern petro-states: Iran, Iraq, Kuwait, Saudi Arabia, and the UAE, which face a severe dilemma as they weigh the imperative of addressing climate change against their economic reliance on fossil fuels. Covering the period 2010–2023, the analysis estimates the elasticity of emissions with respect to total and fuel-specific subsidies. The results indicate a robust and statistically significant positive association between subsidies and emissions, with a 10 percent reduction in total subsidies corresponding to a 1.2 percent decline in emissions. Among fuel types, gas subsidies show the strongest and most consistent correlation with emissions, while oil and electricity subsidies exhibit weaker or statistically insignificant patterns. The findings highlight the environmental relevance of fuel-specific subsidy reforms and provide an empirical foundation for evaluating policy pathways that balance fiscal sustainability, social welfare, and emission-reduction objectives in the region.

items.title: A scoping review of psychosocial factors of climate change inaction: Implications for climate change communication and education
items.summary_raw: Abstract Climate change communication and education efforts often focus on the cognitive aspects of addressing climate change, emphasizing that a key path to solving climate change-related challenges may be achieved through an educated public that better understands the science of this issue. However, despite decades of information-heavy communication and education efforts, designed with knowledge-related outcomes in mind, meaningful and sustained action to address climate change has yet to occur at a broad scale. This lack of effective, sustained action has motivated researchers from a range of fields to examine other factors that prevent climate change action. We undertook a systematic scoping review of peer-reviewed, empirical studies (n = 92) focusing on psychological and sociological (psychosocial) factors associated with climate change inaction. Through thematic analysis, we identified trends and patterns across the studies, but also noted that no obvious list of discrete psychosocial factors leading to climate inaction emerged. Political ideology and emotions were the most common factors discussed as influencing climate change inaction. Other psychosocial factors receiving notable attention included climate change perceptions, trust in institutions and leaders, values, and efficacy beliefs. The most-recommended strategies for improving effectiveness of climate change communication and education were attending to climate-related emotions; addressing issues of ideology…

While individual bio-CCUS technologies are increasingly well understood, the actor-level dynamics and governance conditions determining value chain formation are less studied. We address that gap through semi-structured interviews with representatives of 13 companies across bio-CCUS value chains and four forerunner municipalities in Finland, characterizing the decision-making environment facing both groups, complemented by an analysis of EU-level and national regulation. The findings reveal that investment in bio-CCUS is primarily constrained by system-level coordination failures: a chicken-and-egg dynamic persists between CO₂ producers waiting for stable demand and users waiting for reliable supply, while missing logistics infrastructure, spatial dependencies, and regulatory fragmentation across legal domains compound the challenge. Biogenic CO₂ is currently largely excluded from EU ETS compliance incentives, and strong policy support for RFNBOs contrasts with the near-absence of comparable incentives for other CCU applications. National policy instruments translate EU frameworks into concrete incentives, but their design may reinforce a focus on fuel-based pathways and limit participation of smaller actors. items.title: Responsible tourism in protected areas: ecolodge operators’ perceptions of carbon emission sources and mitigation needs in Zimbabwe
items.summary_raw: Ecolodges are increasingly important components within Southern African nature-based tourism destinations. Ecolodges aim to provide tourists with experiences that are socio-economically and environmentally responsible. Due to growing concerns about climate change, ecolodges are expected to play a responsible role in mitigation efforts. One of the existing mitigation tools for tourism operators is based on carbon footprint assessment. This study analyses ecolodge managers’ perceptions of key sources of carbon emissions, needed mitigation strategies, and related challenges in Hwange National Park, Zimbabwe. Semi-structured interviews were conducted with 23 lodge managers. The results indicate that the dominant sources of carbon emissions are transportation, energy, and waste disposal by operators. The ecolodges investigated have employed various mitigation strategies, which were mainly based on saving costs. This is a good motive for a business, but it may guide mitigation to only those processes that do not create costs for them. Overall, crucial issues and challenges affect the adoption of mitigation strategies, such as financial constraints, knowledge and skills gaps, and technical limitations.

items.title: Digital innovation and public acceptance of nuclear energy in the green transition
items.summary_raw: Abstract Public acceptance is widely regarded as a binding constraint on the contribution of nuclear energy to the green transition, yet claims that digital innovation will ease this constraint have rarely been examined against social science evidence. This topical review asks under what conditions digital innovation in nuclear energy systems, in particular digital twins, artificial intelligence (AI)-based predictive maintenance and the digitally supported design, manufacture and operation of Small Modular Reactors (SMRs), can contribute to public acceptance of nuclear energy. The analysis draws on five strands of scholarship that are seldom brought into contact with the technical literature: risk perception research, cultural theory of risk, the deficit and engagement models of science communication, the social licence to operate, and socio-technical transitions theory, which serves as the integrating framework. Reading techno-optimistic claims through these lenses, the review identifies three structural barriers: a cybersecurity paradox, whereby the connectivity that enables digital safety functions simultaneously expands the attack surface; an economic gap, specific to SMRs, whereby projected cost reductions rest on serial-production assumptions that recent project experience has not supported; and a transparency fallacy, whereby information disclosure is expected to build trust although meta-analytic evidence links the benefit and risk perceptions associated with…

items.title: State Aid Compatibility Beyond State Aid Law? Public Procurement and the Inextricable Link Doctrine After Paks II
items.source_name: JCMS Journal of Common Market Studies
items.summary_raw: Abstract The Court of Justice's annulment of the Commission's approval of state aid for Hungary's Paks II nuclear project carries significance far beyond the resolution of a single dispute. Following the Russian invasion of Ukraine, many EU Member States began prioritising policy objectives such as energy security and decarbonisation over common market rules. In the nuclear sector, this has manifested itself in government efforts to select technology suppliers directly and provide state aid without a public procurement procedure. However, the Court of Justice of the European Union, in its 2025 judgment regarding the Paks II nuclear power plant, holds that broader policy objectives cannot displace existing energy market rules, including those governing state aid. Not every procurement issue needs to be automatically examined as part of a state aid review. However, where the procurement dimension is inseparably linked to the aid measure and has been raised during the administrative procedure, the Commission must address it in a reasoned and self‐contained manner. The ruling thus underscores the importance of EU internal market rules and instruments when granting state aid and could have a significant impact on the development of energy infrastructure in the EU.

items.title: Farmers’ beliefs about the impacts of a CO2e tax on agriculture and their acceptance of the tax: A randomized survey experiment
items.summary_raw: Agriculture is a major source of greenhouse gas emissions but has largely been exempt from stringent climate change mitigation policies, often due to concerns about resistance from the sector. With Denmark introducing the world’s first CO 2 -equivalent (CO 2 e) tax on agricultural emissions, this paper provides representative evidence of farmers’ beliefs about its impacts and examines whether providing expert-predicted impacts can causally influence these beliefs and acceptance of the tax. Using a randomized survey experiment with 981 Danish farmers, we find a widespread overestimation of the tax’s impacts on production, employment, and land value, with 94–97 % of farmers expecting the impacts to be up to three times larger than expert-predicted estimates. Providing an expert-predicted impact reduces these perception gaps, with effects varying according to the tax’s stringency, size of belief gaps, and farm characteristics such as size and type. However, our results also indicate that, in some cases, belief updating may be muted or even contrary to the information provided, consistent with behavioral theories beyond the Bayesian framework. We also find that the belief revisions can translate into greater acceptance of the tax, although these effects vary with tax stringency, initial belief gaps, and farm characteristics. Our findings suggest that designing acceptable climate policies for agriculture may require not only expert information but also targeted communication and…

items.title: Zero emissions commitment depends on warming level
items.summary_raw: Abstract When anthropogenic CO 2 emissions cease, global temperature does not stabilize immediately. The resulting global temperature change, the zero emissions commitment, is central to carbon budget assessments and understanding reversibility of global warming, yet its dependence on prior warming levels remains unclear. Here we show, using zero-emission simulations with the UK Earth System Model (UKESM1.2) across global warming levels of 1.5–5 K, that the zero emissions commitment stays near zero up to 2 K but becomes positive at higher warming levels, reaching 0.4–0.6 K after ~ 150 years. This dependence indicates that stabilizing or reversing warming becomes progressively more difficult as peak temperature rises. We identify the mechanism behind this behaviour: stronger warming from higher radiative disequilibrium and weakening carbon sinks, driven by saturated land carbon uptake and the reduced radiative impact of CO 2 drawdown at higher background CO 2 concentrations. Higher peak warming therefore commits the planet to additional warming, limiting temperature-overshoot reversibility.

items.title: A socio-technical transition framework for biomass torrefaction at the nexus of energy security and energy justice
items.summary_raw: The global energy transition necessitates a critical re-evaluation of bioenergy’s role and moving beyond its conventional perception as a mere renewable source, aligning with the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), particularly SDG 7 (Affordable and Clean Energy) and SDG 13 (Climate Action). Biomass torrefaction, a mild thermochemical pretreatment, emerges as a pivotal technology that can fundamentally upgrade biomass into a high-quality solid biofuel. This review examines torrefaction as a socio-technical pathway that may contribute to multidimensional energy security while identifying potential energy justice implications across distributive, procedural, recognitional, and restorative dimensions within the bioenergy sector. This review systematically synthesizes recent advancements in torrefaction science, reactor design, and sustainability assessment. A novel analytical framework is developed to evaluate its role in enhancing energy security across the dimensions of availability, accessibility, affordability, and acceptability. Crucially, this review offers a systematic energy justice-oriented assessment of the torrefaction pathway, critically evaluating its implications across the distributive, procedural, recognitional, and restorative justice dimensions. The analysis reveals that the techno-economic promise of torrefaction is necessary but insufficient for its sustainable integration. items.title: Attitude-Based Performance Assessment Instrument
items.source_name: Majapahit Journal of Islamic Finance and Management
items.summary_raw: Performance assessment based on attitude in this study is one way to assess how a lecturer behaves in interacting with students. Questionnaires were distributed to 17 students to assess a lecturer A. Descriptive analysis was carried out on the collected data. The results of the performance assessment of Lecturer A were in the "very good" category with an average score of 4.68 on a scale of 5. Based on the recapitulation, the grand mean was obtained = 4.68 which indicated a very good general category. Students assessed that Lecturer A's main strengths were in the indicators "arrives on time during lectures" (highest score = 4.94), "speaks clearly when teaching" (score = 4.88), "provides examples of good professional attitudes" (score = 4.82), "is open to discussions with students" (score = 4.82), "respects students' questions" (score = 4.76), "has a high level of commitment" (score = 4.76), "is able to control the class" (score = 4.76), "is able to inspire students" (score = 4.76). Meanwhile, students assessed that Lecturer A's areas of improvement were "openness to criticism and input from students" (score = 4.47), "responsiveness to problems faced by students" (score = 4.47), "creative in solving problems that occur" (score = 4.41), and "ability to adapt to student conditions" (score = 4.41). Although still in the good category, these two indicators should be improved to achieve the maximum score.

items.title: Strategi Adaptasi Petani Padi dalam Pengeringan Gabah pada Kondisi Ketidakpastian Cuaca: Studi Fenomenologis
items.summary_raw: Climate change and weather unpredictability present major challenges to the post-harvest grain drying process. This study aims to analyze farmers' adaptation strategies and the utilization of technology in grain drying. A qualitative method with a phenomenological approach was employed through observations and interviews with two rice farmers in Malang. The results show that farmers are still heavily reliant on conventional sun-drying methods. Rainfall fluctuations and high humidity prolong the drying duration and pose a risk of degrading harvest quality. Adaptations remain intuitive and experience-based, while access to modern drying technology and weather information systems is severely limited. Therefore, strengthening adaptive capacity through structured extension services, expanding access to post-harvest technology, and delivering strategic policy support are crucial to enhancing farmers' resilience against climate uncertainty.

items.title: How to foster a resilient, efficient and clean hydrogen ramp-up – A comparative assessment of EU and US support systems
items.summary_raw: Achieving climate targets in hard-to-electrify sectors such as energy-intensive industries, aviation and maritime requires rapid uptake of renewable and low-carbon hydrogen despite market uncertainties. However, hydrogen will contribute to decarbonization only when its production comes with zero or very limited greenhouse gas emissions. Moreover, limited public funding calls for an efficient allocation of support. Public support systems for hydrogen need to address this conundrum of greenhouse gas effectiveness, economic efficiency and resilient market uptake with a suitably designed instrument mix. A key question is how to identify ex-ante gaps and deficiencies in the instrument mix. This paper develops assessment criteria for such support systems, expanding existing assessments beyond supply-side policies and electrolytic hydrogen. The criteria are then applied to the most relevant deployment policies in the European Union, including but not limited to the Hydrogen Bank, and the United States, namely the Inflation Reduction Act and the Bipartisan Infrastructure Law. The findings indicate that the EU support system is more stringent regarding greenhouse gas effectiveness and economic efficiency than the US support system but poses greater risks to rapid market uptake due to its complexity and limited focus on domestic supply chains. The results are partially validated by recent market developments based on the IEA Hydrogen Projects Database, while the infancy of the market…

items.title: Cultivating proactive sustainability mindsets in higher education? Unmasking climate education in business schools
items.source_name: International Journal of Sustainability in Higher Education
items.summary_raw: Purpose This study aims to examine how Sustainable Development Goal (SDG) 13 (Climate Action) is integrated into business education in higher education (HE) by exploring student perceptions to comprehend whether climate education is substantively implemented or symbolically presented. Design/methodology/approach Using Q-methodology, 137 business students ranked 29 statements covering curriculum content, skills development, and attitudes toward climate action. Principal component analysis identified shared viewpoints, while qualitative feedback provided depth and context. Findings Tensions between sustainability objectives and disciplinary silos are highlighted by the emergence of two student archetypes: Engaged Advocates, who demand experiential pedagogies, and Pragmatic Observers, who prioritize economic outcomes. Results highlight a legitimacy gap between institutional rhetoric and meaningful curriculum integration. Research limitations/implications Findings are drawn from a single HE institution and focus solely on students, limiting generalizability. Future research should examine faculty perspectives, policy implementation and multi-institutional comparisons. Practical implications HE must integrate sustainability into research, curricula and community engagement, following 1) Systemic curriculum integration; 2) Scaling experiential/place-based learning and systemic/anticipatory skills; 3) Faculty training for climate-aligned pedagogies to prepare students to be…

items.title: The critical role of political trust in the energy transition
items.summary_raw: Abstract Achieving net‐zero CO 2 emissions requires sustained collaboration between civil society and the private and public sectors across time and geographies, but low trust in and among these actors impedes coordinated action. This multidisciplinary review examines how different forms of trust, in particular political trust (i.e., trust between actors with differential power), shape the energy transition, addressing four core questions: How does trust impact energy project development and outcomes? How do the processes of building, maintaining, eroding, and repairing trust differ? What are the asymmetries in trust gain and loss? How does a project's history and stage determine which process is at play and whether trust repair is possible? A narrative literature review and analysis of fifteen case studies spanning diverse energy contexts identifies key trust dyads: government‐community, developer‐community, regulator‐developer. Mapping these trust dyads on project outcomes reveals when trust functions as either a barrier or a pathway to success. We complement our literature review and case analysis with primary data from stakeholder surveys and expert workshops that validate the real‐world relevance of trust research insights and identify the largest trust deficits and effective trust‐building strategies perceived by expert practitioners. Our findings across sources of evidence converge to show that political trust operates through distinct mechanisms across different…

items.title: Soil, Society, and Supply Chains
items.source_name: International Journal of Agriculture Innovations and Cutting-Edge Research (HEC Recognised)
items.summary_raw: Organic farming is widely promoted to improve environmental protection and rural sustainability. In Europe, Bio-Districts connect organic agriculture with territorial governance, cultural heritage, and local development. This review assesses how organic farming contributes to environmental, economic, social, and territorial sustainability in the Cilento Bio-District in southern Italy. We used a structured, literature-based approach to examine peer-reviewed studies, academic books, institutional reports, and policy-oriented publications identified through academic databases and relevant institutional resources. The literature published between 2005 and 2024, supplemented by selected 2025–2026 studies on Bio-District governance and rural vitality, was synthesized thematically across four dimensions: environmental integrity, economic viability, social and territorial sustainability, and institutional governance. The reviewed literature associates organic farming with soil conservation, biodiversity protection, reduced reliance on synthetic inputs, local market development, farmer cooperation, and the preservation of traditional agricultural practices. It also indicates that these outcomes depend on enabling conditions, including territorial coordination, market access, institutional collaboration, and policy support. Challenges reported in the literature include certification and compliance costs, administrative burdens, climate variability, and limitations in market access…

items.title: Knowledge, attitudes and practices of smallholder banana farmers and their socio-economic correlates
items.source_name: Saudi Journal of Food Security and Environmental Sustainability
items.summary_raw: Banana production is an important source of food and income for smallholder farming households in Tanzania. However, farmers perceived knowledge, attitudes and practices (KAP) may vary across banana value-chain activities and according to their socio-economic and institutional circumstances. This study assessed and compared the perceived knowledge, attitudes and practices of smallholder banana farmers’ across selected value-chain activities and examined the socio-economic factors associated with these KAP dimensions in Meru District Council and Moshi Rural District, Tanzania. A quantitative cross-sectional survey was conducted among 352 smallholder banana farmers, comprising 149 (42.3%) from Meru District Council and 203 (57.7%) from Moshi Rural District. Data were collected using a structured questionnaire administered through Kobo Toolbox. Descriptive statistics, Pearson’s chi-square tests and multiple linear regression were used for analysis. The findings showed variation in perceived knowledge, attitudes and practices across the different banana value-chain activities. Overall, 50.3% of farmers in Meru and 49.3% in Moshi Rural had low perceived knowledge, while 40.9% and 39.9%, respectively, had high perceived knowledge. Regarding attitudes, 51.0% of farmers in Meru and 52.2% in Moshi Rural reported negative attitudes, whereas 41.6% and 42.9%, respectively, reported positive attitudes. For practices, 47.7% of Meru farmers and 43.8% of Moshi Rural farmers reported poor…

items.title: Testing protection motivation theory in climate–hunger nexus: food insecurity, climate perceptions, and environmental policy support in Ghana with urban–rural inequalities
items.summary_raw: This study examines the climate–hunger nexus by evaluating how climate change perceptions influence environmental policy support through food insecurity, accounting for urban–rural and income inequalities in Ghana. The paper advances Protection Motivation Theory (PMT) by integrating material hardship, framing food insecurity as a key mediator between cognitive threat appraisal and public policy support. Utilizing nationally representative data from the Afrobarometer Round 10 (2024) survey with a sample size of 2 , 400 adult respondents, the analytical framework employs Structural Equation Modelling (SEM) with bootstrapped mediation, multi-group analysis, and interaction structural models. The results indicate that climate threat perceptions positively impact food insecurity, which in turn significantly increases support for environmental policies. Food insecurity mediates the relationship between climate perceptions and policy support. Multi-group and interaction analyses further reveal that this indirect pathway is significantly stronger among rural ( β = 0.17 , p < 0.001 ) and low-income ( β = 0.19 , p < 0.001 ) households. In conclusion, cognitive recognition of climate risk translates into policy support primarily when mediated by real material vulnerability. Consequently, climate risk communication and adaptation policies must explicitly integrate household food security mechanisms, targeting rural and low-income communities with climate-smart agricultural support and…

items.title: CLIMATE CHANGE AND ACADEMIC PERFORMANCE AMONG GRADE 9 STUDENTS: EVIDENCE FROM A RURAL PHILIPPINE PUBLIC SCHOOL
items.source_name: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
items.summary_raw: Climate change increasingly poses challenges to educational continuity, student well-being, and academic performance, particularly in climate-vulnerable communities. This study examined the relationship between climate change hazards and the academic performance of Grade 9 students in MAPEH at Sagbayan National High School, San Miguel District 2, Surigao del Sur, Philippines during the School Year 2025-2026. A mixed-methods research design integrating quantitative descriptive and qualitative phenomenological approaches was employed. The study involved 121 respondents, comprising 113 Grade 9 learners and 8 Grade 9 teachers. Quantitative data were gathered through a structured questionnaire and academic performance records, while qualitative data were obtained from participants’ lived experiences of climate-related disruptions. Findings showed that students strongly perceived climate change hazards across eight dimensions, with an overall weighted mean of 4.69. Environmental protection received the highest rating (M = 4.80), followed by students’ attitude (M = 4.76), well-being (M = 4.74), psychological concerns (M = 4.73), and socio-economic developmental concerns (M = 4.72). School infrastructure received the lowest, although still strong, perception rating (M = 4.46). Despite high climate-change perceptions, students’ MAPEH performance remained at a low proficiency level, with a mean score of 31.77 out of 50 and a mean percentage score of 53.62. Pearson correlation analysis…

items.summary_raw: Vážení priatelia, prežije Európa francúzsku krízu? V novom podcaste Na Vŕšku práve túto otázku otvárajú Dominik Stroukal, Juraj Karpiš a Martin Vlachynský.
