A od otázky, čo nás koľko stojí, sa dostaneme aj […] Článok Týždeň s INESS 26 – Bonjour, kríza! je zobrazený ako prvý na INESS - Institute of Economic and Social Studies .

items.title: Rapid soil degradation of a cross-linked, semicrystalline polyethylene-like polyester produced by Colletes bees
items.summary_raw: Polyethylene (PE)-like polyesters have long been investigated as biodegradable alternatives to conventional polyolefins but degrade poorly despite possessing hydrolyzable esters due to high crystallinity and hydrophobicity. Bees of the genus Colletes line their nests with a PE-like polyester that shows no environmental accumulation despite decades of nesting in dense aggregations, suggesting rapid biodegradability. This work provides a comprehensive characterization of Colletes inaequalis polyester and demonstrates its rapid degradation under ambient environmental conditions. Colletes polyester is completely insoluble in trichlorobenzene or toluene at elevated temperatures, indicating cross-linking despite originating from macrocyclic lactones that lack obvious cross-linkable functionality. Small molecules extracted from the network match the Dufour’s gland secretion but lack macrolactone, indicating complete monomer conversion. Although its repeat unit resembles amorphous, network-like plant cutin, Colletes polyester is highly crystalline ( X c = 60%), with PE-like orthorhombic packing and T m = 75 °C, indicating a much lower cross-link density. Composition analysis of nest linings collected 0 to 11 mo after construction reveals significant degradation, with polyester content falling from 73 to 40 wt% within 4 mo in ambient soil. Esterase activity against the model substrate p-nitrophenylbutyrate is observed in both newly constructed and 4-mo aged linings, which may…

items.title: Heme signatures in mineralized red blood cells within vascular canals of a 115-million-year-old dinosaur bone
items.summary_raw: Detection of endogenous biomolecules in vertebrate fossils remains controversial because labile compounds degrade quickly and are highly susceptible to contamination. Here, we present data on the preservation of heme-derived tetrapyrroles, and vascular canal-constrained ellipsoidal microstructures, inferred to be red blood cells, in limb bones of Aratasaurus museunacionali , a 115-million-year-old theropod dinosaur. High-performance liquid chromatography–mass spectrometry identified parent and diagenetically altered heme B as the principal tetrapyrroles of bone extract, contrasting the chlorophyll and bacteriochlorophyll porphyrin signatures of the surrounding matrix supporting an endogenous origin. Separate spatially resolved analyses by Raman spectroscopy and transmission electron microscopy confirmed the ellipsoid microstructure localization of i) porphyrin signals of heme and ii) key elements of heme (Fe, N, and C) and mineral stabilizing hausmannite (Mn 3 O 4 ), respectively. These results demonstrate blood-derived biomolecules in mineralized red blood cells of a dinosaur.

items.title: Ancient genomes from Mendoza, Argentina, trace the dynamics of colonial urban formation in the Southern Cone of the Americas
items.summary_raw: European colonization introduced abrupt changes into the Americas. These included the introduction of infectious diseases, forced labor and displacement of Indigenous and African individuals, European settlement, and the imposition of caste regimes. However, the role of these forces in reshaping communities across different regions remains debated. This is especially true in the Virreinato del Río de la Plata (the territories of present-day Argentina, Bolivia, Uruguay, Paraguay, and Brazil), which is less studied than other regions such as the United States, the Caribbean, and Mexico. We investigated how these forces shaped the colonial societies of Mendoza in the Cuyo region (Central-Western Argentina) by sequencing ancient DNA of 28 individuals (17th to 19th centuries) excavated from churches associated with different social strata, recovering 22 mitochondrial genomes, and genome-wide data of 15 individuals. By performing paleogenomic analyses contextualized by burial site, we detected admixture among Indigenous, European, and African populations, with ancestry partially structured by church and burial location. Exceptions to this pattern indicate social mobility and flexible social classifications beyond genetic ancestry. The European-related ancestry aligns with Southern European migration, while African-related ancestry shows affinities to Western-Central Africa. The Indigenous-related ancestry shows highest affinity to precontact populations from Cuyo, supporting local…

items.title: Active immunotherapy against IL-1β restores tissue repair under chronic inflammation
items.summary_raw: Chronic inflammation driven by sustained interleukin-1 beta (IL-1β) signaling disrupts the resolution phase of tissue repair by orchestrating dysregulated immune activity. As a key upstream mediator, IL-1β prolongs the activation of pro-inflammatory myeloid cells and establishes an environment that prevents the transition to tissue repair. Here, we developed an active immunotherapy against IL-1β using the self-assembling peptide nanofiber Coil29, which elicits robust and specific IL-1β-targeted immune responses in both wild-type and diabetic mice, without inducing systemic immunosuppression. In a chronic wound model, the therapy accelerated re-epithelialization and enhanced overall tissue regeneration, outperforming anti-IL-1β monoclonal antibodies. This therapy suppressed macrophage activity, promoted their M2-like polarization, enhanced pro-healing cytokine secretion and enriched the injury site with anti-IL-1β antibodies. In vitro, we found that antibodies from immunized mice reprogrammed M1 macrophages toward an M2-like phenotype, suggesting that antibody-mediated modulation of IL-1β activity may drive the enhanced wound re-epithelization seen in immunized animals. Altogether, these findings highlight a targeted, regenerative therapy for the healing of chronic wounds.

items.title: Intratumoral cDC1–T cell clusters serve as sites of local costimulation to enhance CTL-mediated tumor rejection
items.summary_raw: T cells are essential for antitumor immunity, but their ability to eliminate tumors depends on interactions with type 1 conventional dendritic cells (cDC1s). cDC1s are known for cross-presenting tumor-derived antigens in lymph nodes to prime T cells, but their role within tumors remains less well understood. Here, we use a tumor array model to investigate how cDC1–T cell interactions influence immune responses and tumor fate. We show that the spatial distribution of both cDC1s and T cells determines whether a tumor can be rejected. We defined three immunotypes based on the spatial distribution of T cells and cDC1s: T cell–inflamed/dendritic cell-inflamed (TC-In/DC-In) tumors, where T cells and cDC1s coinfiltrate the tumor; T cell–inflamed/dendritic cell-excluded (TC-In/DC-Ex) tumors, where T cells infiltrate but cDC1s remain at the periphery; and T cell–excluded/dendritic cell-excluded (TC-Ex/DC-Ex) tumors, which lack both cDC1 and T cell infiltration. TC-In/DC-In tumors are most likely to undergo rejection, whereas TC-In/DC-Ex tumors persist despite T cell infiltration. Within TC-In/DC-In tumors, cDC1s interact directly with T cells, upregulate costimulatory molecules, and sustain effector T cell responses, while cDC1s in TC-In/DC-Ex tumors express higher migration-associated genes, suggesting they may exit the tumor. We further show that chemokine modulation, particularly through CXCL9, CCL5, and XCL1, can reshape immune infiltration patterns to promote intratumoral cDC1–T…

items.title: At long last, BchE gets its day in the sun
Transcranial magnetic stimulation to the dorsolateral prefrontal cortex modulates single-neuron activity in humans
items.summary_raw: Transcranial magnetic stimulation (TMS) to the dorsolateral prefrontal cortex (dlPFC) is an established treatment for depression, yet the fundamental question of how cortical stimulation influences single neurons in deep brain circuits critical for mood regulation remains unanswered. Using a rare opportunity to record from intracranial microelectrodes while TMS was delivered in four neurosurgical patients, we evaluated the responses of 185 single neurons. Artifact cleaning enabled single-neuron spikes to be resolved as early as 8 ms after stimulation. We found that single-pulse TMS to the left dlPFC elicited time-locked firing responses in 46% of neurons (26% facilitated only, 19% suppressed only, 1% both). These responses occurred within deep bilateral cortical and subcortical structures, including the putamen and thalamus. Single-pulse TMS tended to facilitate spiking in striato-thalamic putative inhibitory neurons from ~8 ms, peaking at ~80 to 100 ms, and decaying until ~600 ms. In contrast, putative excitatory neurons and limbic areas were suppressed with a slower time course lasting to ~1,000 ms. TMS-evoked potentials recorded from intracranial depth macroelectrodes to quantify network activity revealed that the modulation of responsive neurons was positively correlated with cortico-striato-thalamic network activity and anticorrelated with limbic network activity in one participant with sufficient network and unit sampling. These results suggest that dlPFC TMS recruits…

items.title: 3D confinement reshapes RNA folding and enhances circularization in the Zika virus
items.summary_raw: Many RNA molecules function within confined environments, but the effect of confinement on RNA folding remains poorly understood. Proximity ligation experiments reveal altered long-range contacts in confined vs. unconfined states, yet they do not explain how spatial constraints give rise to these differences. Here, we develop a physical modeling approach that incorporates proximity ligation data into coarse-grained molecular dynamics simulations to reconstruct RNA 3D structures under confinement. We test our model on the ∼ 11 kb genome of the Zika virus, comparing the folding in virions (confined) and in cells (unconfined). We observe that the probability of contact between two regions of the genome vs. linear distance follows different scaling laws in the confined and unconfined cases, in agreement with proximity ligation experiments. We find that genome circularization—an interaction that regulates replication in Zika—occurs more frequently under confinement in both experiments and simulations. Our model reveals that the formation of long double-stranded stems through stacking confers local nematic liquid crystalline order to the RNA, and predicts pseudoknot topologies consistent with those seen in crystallographic structures of shorter RNAs. These results provide insight into the mechanism through which confinement alters the ensemble of 3D structures accessible to a long RNA molecule.

items.title: Correction for Fahy et al., Hydroxyl radical oxidation of chemical contaminants on indoor surfaces and dust
CD8 + regulatory T cells limit immunopathology but impair viral clearance in Hantaan virus infection
items.summary_raw: In hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome (HFRS) caused by Hantaan virus (HTNV), virus-specific CD8 + T cells mediate both viral clearance and immunopathology. Here, we characterized a CD8 + regulatory T cell (Treg) subset restricted by HLA-E (and its murine ortholog Qa-1) in HFRS patients and in a murine HTNV infection model. CD8 + Tregs (CD122 + Eomes + CD49d lo KIR + ), a subset substantially enriched for HLA-E-restricted T cells, were significantly reduced in peripheral blood of HFRS patients and displayed a terminally differentiated profile with elevated expression of KLRG-1, NKG2A, CTLA-4, and Fas-L, correlating with disease severity. Two HTNV glycoprotein-derived nonapeptides that bound Qa-1 were identified. Following immunization with the identified HTNV peptides and subsequent HTNV challenge, wild-type (WT) mice showed attenuated renal immunopathology, whereas D227K knock-in mice (with disrupted Qa-1-CD8/TCR interaction) showed enhanced viral clearance in the spleen and kidney but exacerbated renal immunopathology. Mechanistically, Qa-1-restricted CD8 + Tregs from WT mice suppressed effector CD8 + T cell proliferation in a peptide-specific, CD8/TCR-dependent manner via enhanced TGF-β secretion. Strikingly, D227K mutation dichotomously reshaped Treg phenotype: bulk polyclonal CD8 + Tregs displayed compensatory upregulation of inhibitory receptors (NKG2A, CTLA-4, PD-1) and TGF-β, whereas epitope-specific CD8 + Tregs showed impaired antigen-specific suppressive function…

items.title: Correction for LaFoya et al., Midbody formation triggers asymmetric fate specification in neural stem cells
A causal account of the neural origins of mental fatigue
items.summary_raw: Successful goal-directed behavior often requires the exertion of effortful cognitive control processes, but it remains unclear why engaging in cognitive control is experienced as effortful and induces fatigue. Here, we tested the hypothesis that sustained activation in the dorsolateral prefrontal cortex (DLPFC)—a neural substrate of cognitive control—causally induces motivational fatigue via the accumulation of prefrontal glutamate metabolites. For this purpose, we combined brain stimulation with spectroscopy imaging to assess how increasing DLPFC excitability during an effortful mental task changes the motivation for mental effort and glutamate concentrations. We found that stimulating the DLPFC during mental effort exertion improved mental performance at the cost of increased posteffort motivational fatigue, suggesting a causal role of DLPFC activation for inducing fatigue. On the neural level, DLPFC activation during effortful cognition also increased prefrontal concentrations of glutamate, which statistically explained the fatigue-induced lower motivation for mental effort. A corresponding analysis of combined glutamate–glutamine (Glx) concentrations revealed converging effects. Together, these findings provide causal evidence that enhanced DLPFC activation contributes to fatigue via neurochemical changes, supporting neuro-metabolic accounts of fatigue and offering new insights into why demanding cognitive tasks are perceived as effortful.

items.title: Designing school choice for diversity in the San Francisco Unified School District
items.summary_raw: More than 65 years after the Brown v. Board of Education ruling that school segregation is unconstitutional, public schools across the United States are again experiencing rising segregation. In districts like San Francisco, efforts to implement district-wide choice policies have largely failed to reverse these trends. Since 2019, we have collaborated with the San Francisco Unified School District to design a student assignment policy meeting the district’s goals of diversity, predictability, and proximity. We use optimization techniques to develop policies restricting choice to zones. We compare these to district-wide choice policies by estimating a choice model using historical application data and simulating assignment. Our results show multiple policies can reduce school segregation while preserving varying degrees of proximity, choice, and predictability. Zone-based policies with reserves reduce the concentration of racial minority students in high-poverty schools and maintain proximity, but reduce choice. District-wide choice with reserves and distance-based priority can further reduce segregation, but at the cost of predictability. Tradeoffs are necessary as no policy dominates another policy. In addition, we show that spatial segregation indices capture average patterns in these tradeoffs but miss important variation revealed by our simulation framework. Our work informed the design and approval of a zone-based policy in San Francisco in 2020, and supports ongoing…

items.title: Environmental forcing, individual repeatability, and mother–daughter resemblance shape the phenology of a long-lived seabird
items.summary_raw: Climate change and variability push species to shift their distributions and phenology to track their climatic niche. Predicting population responses requires identifying the environmental cues that trigger reproduction, their fitness consequences, and the intrinsic factors that shape individual breeding decisions. In long-lived species with deferred breeding, extrinsic (environmental) and intrinsic (individual/maternal) factors may interact in shaping responses to environmental change, but direct empirical evidence remains scarce. We use 2065 breeding events collected over 22 y on a wide-ranging seabird, the Scopoli’s Shearwater. We quantify the effects on population mean laying date of a large-scale climatic index (wNAO) associated with oceanographic conditions. We assess how individual breeding experience and mother–daughter resemblance contribute to among-female differences in reproductive timing, and evaluate the consequences for breeding success (BS) and adult survival. Average laying date was earlier under negative phases of wNAO, indicating a plastic response at the population level. Individual repeatability in the relative laying date (RLD) was high ( R = 0.50) irrespective of experience, indicating consistency among females. Using 142 mother–daughter cases, daughters’ RLD resembled those of their mothers, a covariance that may reflect genetic inheritance, maternal effects, or shared environment. Early laying was associated with higher BS and survival, translating…

items.title: The limits of scaling in aggregation-driven patterning of cell collectives
items.summary_raw: Robust development requires maintaining correct proportions as overall size varies. What controls and limits this scaling remains poorly understood due to the complex interplay of mechanical and biochemical embryonic factors. Combining confinement of dissociated embryonic presomitic mesoderm cells with imaging and chemical perturbations, we identified cell aggregation as the initial event in de novo posterior pole formation. Using a continuum model based solely on cell–cell attraction, we quantitatively map how the time available for aggregation-driven patterning limits the maximum scalable system size. Small systems allow rapid, robust pattern scaling, whereas coarsening dynamics substantially delay scaled patterns in large systems. Our experiments quantitatively confirm these predicted scaling regimes. Together, our results reveal a developmental time–size tradeoff governing the scaling of aggregation-driven patterns.

items.title: Correction for Iwawaki et al., Function of IRE1 alpha in the placenta is essential for placental development and embryonic viability
Molecular basis of quorum-sensing signal transduction by CqsS and its inhibition by CqsA, the autoinducer synthase
items.summary_raw: Vibrio bacteria possess multiple quorum-sensing systems, each of which conveys information into the cell concerning the cell density and species composition of the vicinal community. Germane to the present work is the CqsA-CqsS quorum-sensing pathway that vibrios use for intragenus communication. CqsA is the synthase for the autoinducer ( S )-3-hydroxytridecan-4-one (CAI-1), and CqsS, a bifunctional two-component kinase-phosphatase, is the CAI-1 receptor. Here, we determine the cryo-EM structures of the full-length Vibrio harveyi CqsS dimer in the apo- and ATPγS-bound states. Our structures reveal the molecular basis for the initiation of the phosphorylation cascade, which we support through biochemical and genetic analyses. Autophosphorylation of CqsS occurs in cis at the conserved histidine residue (H1), whereas phospho-transfer to the conserved aspartate residue (D1) in the C-terminal receiver domain occurs in trans . By coexpressing CqsS and CqsA to capture CqsS bound to CAI-1, we unexpectedly find a tight interaction between the CqsS intracellular domain and CqsA. In the complex, the CqsS H1 residues are positioned away from the catalytic cavity, and CqsS kinase activity is inhibited. Cryo-EM analysis, focused on the transmembrane domain of CqsS in this complex, reveals the presence of two CAI-1 molecules. CAI-1 binding induces an obvious movement of transmembrane helix 6, disrupting its extension into the cytosol, providing a structural basis for how CAI-1 binding in…

items.title: Pericyte contraction generates angiostatic effect via cell force–dependent activation of TGFβ
items.summary_raw: Pericytes are phenotypically plastic and capable of switching between contractile and proliferative phenotypes, similar to vascular smooth muscle cells. The intimate interaction of contractile pericytes with endothelial cells (ECs) is essential to the maturation, quiescence, and stability of the capillary and microvascular endothelium. However, the mechanistic link between pericyte contraction and vascular stability is unknown. It is known that TGFβ has dual pro- and antiangiogenic effects depending on the downstream Smad signaling. Here, we show that R-Ras-mediated contractility in pericytes activates TGFβ by integrin-dependent, actomyosin-generated cell traction force. This TGFβ activation, in turn, promotes the quiescence of ECs via the ALK5-Smad2/3 axis of the TGFβ pathway in ECs, but not the Smad1/5 axis of the TGFβ pathway. Furthermore, pericyte-targeted deletion of Rras in mice resulted in impaired pericyte contractility and a significant reduction of Smad2/3 phosphorylation in ECs, accompanied by increased tumor angiogenesis and vessel deformation in the skeletal muscle. These observations suggest that pericytes use the cell force to maintain the quiescence of the endothelium by elevating the local bioavailability of active TGFβ. Our findings provide a mechanism by which pericytes stabilize blood vessels.

items.title: On-site, subannual climate records decouple Neolithic expansion from climate instability
items.summary_raw: How the life of prehistoric people was influenced by climate change and extreme events often remains elusive. Finding appropriate spatiotemporal scales is the major challenge for studies with socioenvironmental questions. This challenge can be overcome by sourcing climatic information from archaeological sites, alongside traces of human agency. For instance, extreme cold-events have been proposed as causing a standstill in early farming expansion across the Mediterranean 8600-8000 years ago. However, there is no immediate (local/short-term) evidence of such events and how they might have influenced people’s lives, nor have previous records been sufficiently resolved to test this robustly. Here we statistically assess the influence of on-site and short-term extremes on human decision-making hypothesized by long-term climate records. Using the largest dataset yet of high-resolution temperature archives in mollusks, we test whether early farmers would have been exposed to extreme cold-events, compromising their subsistence by reducing harvest yields. This immediate agricultural risk is argued to have prevented the spread of new settlements and thus delayed the vigorous expansion that followed, one of prehistory’s fastest known dispersals. Direct comparison of paleotemperature and subsistence data from the same archaeological contexts shows no winter cooling of the magnitude proposed for this period, and no strong relationship between climate and subsistence. Our study reveals…

items.title: Thermal ecology drives alternate responses to rising temperatures in Caribbean anoles
items.summary_raw: Rapidly rising temperatures threaten populations of ectothermic animals worldwide, with the greatest impacts predicted in the tropics—hotspots for biodiversity. Ectotherms can respond to warming through two primary compensatory responses: behavioral thermoregulation, which buffers exposure to extreme temperatures; and heat tolerance increases via plasticity, adaptation, or both. The relative contribution of these responses is predicted to depend on ecological context, but whether these principles can anticipate organismal responses to contemporary warming remains largely untested. Here, using a decadal resurvey of anole lizards from Hispaniola, Jamaica, and Puerto Rico, we show that simple principles of thermal ecology can reliably anticipate organismal responses to rising temperatures. Species occupying thermally heterogeneous open/edge habitats, such as dry forests, behaviorally thermoregulate and have shown little to no increase in heat tolerance over the past decade. By contrast, species from thermally homogeneous closed-canopy environments are poor thermoregulators and have increased their heat tolerance by 2 °C, on average, over the same period. Seasonal comparisons, acclimation experiments, and laboratory-rearing experiments indicate that contemporary increases in heat tolerance likely reflect contributions from rapid evolutionary change and physiological plasticity. Thermal ecology, not phylogenetic or spatial proximity, is the key factor driving responses to rising…

items.title: Rising temperatures, shifting population: Changes in children’s ambient heat exposure in China
items.summary_raw: The frequency and intensity of heat waves are increasing, but how these trends translate to changes in the ambient heat to which children are potentially exposed (hereafter, exposures) is not well established. One complicating factor is that it is not only extreme temperatures that change over time, but also the geospatial distribution of children. Another limitation in our understanding is that existing studies often summarize exposure as person-time accumulated above a temperature cutoff, a quantity that confounds the choice of cutoff, the duration of individual exposure, and the share of the population affected. Our study addresses these gaps by developing a double-dual-distributional framework that jointly considers two types of geospatial and temporal distributions (ambient temperatures and child populations) and two types of heat exposure thresholds, namely intensity (heat levels) and duration (hourly exceedance). To illustrate, we assessed potential exposures—the ambient heat conditions experienced—among 250 million children in China, comparing the 1989–1991 and 2019–2021 periods. We found that children’s average annual exposure to moderate or stronger heat increased by 385 h, and the share exposed to strong heat for at least 12% of hours rose from 8.1% (24.9 million) to 23.7% (59.1 million). Both rising temperatures and shifts in child population distributions contribute materially to increased heat exposures in China, a finding that suggests the need for forecasts…

items.title: Correction for Tsang et al., Cyclin D1 overexpression supports stable EBV infection in nasopharyngeal epithelial cells
Binding sites as dynamic hubs of coevolution encoded information flow
items.summary_raw: The relationship between evolution and allostery is inherently intertwined. While structural studies have elucidated allosteric mechanisms, the extent to which evolutionary sequence information encodes these dynamic networks remains underexplored. Here, we introduce Sequence-based GNM-TE, a framework that integrates coevolutionary information with Gaussian Network Model (GNM) based Transfer Entropy (TE) calculations. This approach translates evolutionary constraints, shaped by both structural and functional requirements, into functionally meaningful allosteric dynamic information. Across 29 cases, we identify binding sites as dynamic hubs of collective information transfer and reveal mode-dependent, directional information flows between these sites. These findings overall indicate that evolutionary constraints embed the architecture of allosteric regulation within protein sequences, preserving binding site communication within layered dynamic ensembles that enable robust functional control and adaptation.

items.title: Afforestation reshapes wildfire activity across global temperate biomes
items.summary_raw: In temperate ecosystems, afforestation is rapidly expanding as a flagship climate mitigation strategy. Yet its impact on wildfires remains poorly understood, raising concerns that establishing planted forests over nonforest areas may intensify wildfire activity under increasingly fire-prone climatic conditions. Here, we combine land-use change data, fire activity records, climatic and anthropogenic covariates to quantify how afforestation alters fire occurrence and burned area across 67,248 patches distributed throughout global temperate biomes using satellite records starting in 2001. We found that, on average, afforestation increased fire occurrence by 26% and burned area by 23% in global temperate regions. However, these effects differed markedly among biomes. Wildfire responses ranged from a near-threefold increase in fire occurrence in Temperate Conifer Forests and a 38% increase in Mediterranean Woodlands biomes to an 18% reduction in the Temperate Grasslands, Savannas, and Shrublands biome. In Temperate Broadleaf and Mixed Forests, afforestation reduced fire occurrence but increased burned area, indicating a shift toward less frequent but larger wildfires following the conversion to planted forest. These contrasting, biome-specific responses show that the consequences of afforestation on wildfire activity may depend strongly on ecological and regional context. The strong variability at biome-scale questions the premise that tree planting provides consistent climate…

items.title: TLR7-independent control of retroviral infection
items.summary_raw: Development of effective immune responses against any pathogen requires efficient activation of the innate immune system followed by induction of an appropriate adaptive immune response using specific signaling pathways tailored to each infection. The sole innate immune receptor implicated in the induction of adaptive immunity to retroviral infection is Toll-like receptor 7 (TLR7). We have found that germinal center responses, neutralizing antibody production, and clearance of murine leukemia virus (MLV) infection in BALB.J and C57BL/6N (B6N) mice occurs in the absence of TLR7 signaling. This suggests that a previously unknown alternative sensing pathway exists for the activation of protective immune responses upon retroviral infection. Genetic crosses indicate that the ability to control retroviral infection in the absence of TLR7 signaling is determined by the same recessive mechanism in both B6N and BALB.J mice, suggesting that TLR7-independent responses do not result from a gain-of-function of an alternative pattern recognition receptor. Additionally, we observed that TLR7-deficient BALB.J mice produce neutralizing antibodies against mouse mammary tumor virus (MMTV) infection, indicating that this alternative sensing pathway is active against retroviruses of multiple genera. Finally, we determined that the alternative sensing pathway is also independent of both MyD88 and STING signaling. The ability of mice of two genetic backgrounds to control retroviral infection in…

items.title: Lifetime stressor exposure is associated with altered trust formation and social learning in dynamic interactions
items.summary_raw: Although trust is fundamental to social interactions, how lifetime stressor exposure relates to the cognitive processes underlying trust remains poorly understood. Using the Stress and Adversity Inventory (STRAIN) to assess cumulative lifetime stressor exposure, combined with an adaptation of the repeated trust game and computational modeling (Hierarchical Gaussian Filtering), we investigated how stressors experienced over the life course relate to three core aspects of trust dynamics—initial trust formation, learning about others’ intentions, and adaptation to changes in trustworthiness—in 168 adults. Greater lifetime stress was associated with stronger negativity biases, lower initial trust, and heightened uncertainty about others’ intentions, increases that were general rather than specific to partner type. These more pessimistic priors were not accompanied by poorer reading of partners: Higher lifetime stress was associated with greater differentiation between prosocial and selfish trustees, driven by reduced investment in the selfish trustee alone. Computational analyses further indicated greater belief volatility, consistent with faster model-implied updating of perceived trustworthiness. These findings provide novel evidence that lifetime stress is associated with a profile consistent with recalibration, rather than a degradation, of the cognitive mechanisms underlying trust, with potential consequences for relationship formation and social functioning. items.title: Using high-frequency data to quantify how urban nature affects air temperature and energy consumption
items.summary_raw: Globally, cities account for 78% of energy consumption and 70~75% of greenhouse gas emissions. Using spatially explicit data on urban vegetation, water bodies, and buildings, combined with extensive daily observations of air temperature and electricity consumption for the subtropical megacity of Shenzhen, China, this study shows that urban nature contributes to urban cooling, reducing energy consumption and associated greenhouse gas emissions. We found that green and blue spaces in the city’s built-up area had a pronounced influence on air temperature, ranging from a cooling effect of 1.27 °C to a warming effect of 0.29 °C, with the cooling effect being dominant over the course of a year. The cooling effect was greatest at moderate temperatures (~20 °C) and was lower on hotter days. We identified a temperature threshold of 16 to 18 °C above which urban nature produces measurable reductions in cooling energy demand. We found that residential electricity consumption was more temperature-sensitive than nonresidential electricity consumption. For the study year of 2021, the net electricity savings from urban nature was 1.5 billion kWh. This reduction in energy consumption translated to almost one million tons of avoided CO 2 emissions, which was 4.65-times the sequestration capacity of the city’s terrestrial vegetation and equivalent to the annual emissions of over 223 thousand people using global average annual per capita carbon emissions.

Kinome profiling enabled development of a LATS1/2 inhibitor with wound healing potential
items.summary_raw: System-level mapping of kinase inhibitors’ polypharmacology can uncover opportunities for drug repurposing and identify starting points for medicinal chemistry campaigns aimed at novel targets. Here, we describe a large-scale profiling of 257 kinase inhibitors that revealed domains of promiscuity, a broad region of uninhibited targets and discrete pockets of selectivity. Focusing on a subcluster enriched for AGC group kinases and using the AKT inhibitor AT-7867 (an antiproliferative agent) as a starting point, we employed scaffold hopping and property-based optimization to discover NCGC-6782, a LATS1/2 inhibitor with robust proproliferative activity. In biochemical and cell-based assays, NCGC-6782 inhibited LATS1/2 activity, reduced YAP phosphorylation, and promoted rapid YAP nuclear translocation and transactivation of YAP-target genes. Kinome-wide profilings demonstrated good in vitro selectivity and exquisite chemoproteomic and kinetic selectivity. In vivo, NCGC-6782 exhibited favorable pharmacokinetic (PK) profiles following intraperitoneal (IP), intravenous (IV), or oral (PO) dosing, leading to rapid inhibition of YAP-phosphorylation in murine liver samples. Transcriptomics and proteomics following NCGC-6782 revealed upregulation of YAP-dependent genes (4 h) followed by activation of cell cycle programs (24 h). Consistently, NCGC-6782 accelerated proliferative regeneration in both cell-based and in vivo wound healing models of full-thickness excisional skin injury…

items.title: Nonadiabatic dynamics of the ferroelectric soft mode
items.summary_raw: Most microscopic descriptions of structural dynamics assume the Born–Oppenheimer separation, where electrons adjust adiabatically to ionic motion. When this separation breaks down, electronic and lattice degrees of freedom can evolve on different timescales, giving rise to new physical phenomena beyond the adiabatic limit. Here, we use time-resolved, phase-sensitive second-harmonic generation and pump–probe reflectivity to reshape the ferroelectric free-energy landscape of SnTe while separately tracking polar order and coherent lattice motion. When photoexcitation transiently suppresses the double-well barrier, polarization dynamics become strongly nonlinear, while the coherent phonon dynamics remain harmonic. This decoupling cannot be described by a single adiabatic coordinate for the electronic polarization and ionic positions. We provide a unifying physical description for the nonadiabatic dynamics of the ferroelectric mode and the mixed displacive/order–disorder nature of SnTe based on a separation of scales for the renormalization of the ferroelectric stiffness.

items.title: Paradoxical effects of opioids in suppression of colonic motility
items.summary_raw: Opiates slow colonic transit and cause constipation, effects traditionally attributed to suppression of excitatory cholinergic neurons through μ (MOR), δ (DOR), or κ (KOR) opioid receptors on myenteric neurons. However, the cellular mechanisms mediating opioid-induced constipation remain incompletely defined. We found that spontaneous enteric nitrergic motor inputs to mouse colon were reduced by opioid receptor agonists, leading to increased phasic contractions of colonic muscles, an effect abolished by pretreatment with tetrodotoxin, L-NNA, or apamin (in distal colon). Increased contractions in response to opioids are not easily explained by suppression of excitatory neural inputs, and spontaneous cholinergic motor inputs to colon were not suppressed by the MOR agonist Endomorphin-1 (EM-1). Consistent with these effects, MOR were expressed by many nitrergic neurons, and EM-1 reduced the asynchronous activity of nitrergic myenteric neurons during the period of tonic inhibition and the synchronized activity occurring normally just before neurogenic contractions. In addition to increasing phasic contractions, EM-1 enhanced Ca 2+ transients in interstitial cells of Cajal, depolarized membrane potentials of circular muscle cells, effects equivalent to the effects of tetrodotoxin. These are effects consistent with suppression of tonic inhibition. items.title: The American Dream wasn’t built for climate change
items.summary_raw: To Sierra Isley, the American Dream brings to mind a home ringed by a white picket fence. “The house in the suburbs is just what you’re taught growing up,” the 26-year-old said. “You know, that’s what you see on TV.” What she wanted for her life was a bit different from that picket-fence ideal, but she still saw the prospect of buying her first house two years ago as a chance to live out what she called “that big dream that everybody has as a kid.” Isley and her girlfriend, Jamie, were moving from Philadelphia to Asheville, North Carolina, and found a home they liked, a three-bedroom brick house with lots of natural light and a big tree out front. With some help from their parents, they put down a deposit and got their offer accepted. But when they went to sign the closing papers, a complication got in the way: The house had a huge lien on it. After consulting with lawyers, they decided to break the contract and hunt for an apartment to rent in Asheville. It was a blessing in disguise. One month later, while Sierra and Jamie were still unpacking boxes and building furniture, the remnants of Hurricane Helene turned Asheville into a disaster zone. The basement of their apartment flooded, but they were luckier than some of their neighbors, whose homes had been destroyed. items.title: Exclusive: Most voters believe climate change threatens the American Dream
items.summary_raw: In his inaugural address in January 2025, President Donald Trump promised that “the American Dream will soon be back and thriving like never before.” Apparently, that required undoing policies to tackle climate change: The Trump administration has invoked “the American Dream” as a justification to propose ending mandatory reporting of greenhouse gas emissions , reverse rules to cut emissions from cars , and deregulate coal . Voters, on the other hand, view climate change itself as a problem for their aspirations. Exclusive polling for Grist from the think tank Data for Progress shows that 58 percent of likely U.S. voters believe that the warming climate will hinder their ability to achieve or maintain the American Dream over the next 20 years — including 42 percent of Republicans. “We identify a strong concern about climate change as a threat to achieving the American Dream,” said Grace Adcox, a senior climate strategist at the progressive think tank. It sits on a gravel spit that juts into Kotzebue Sound just north of the Arctic Circle, and is accessible only by air and sea. Ice keeps freight barges from reaching it for most of the year. The community relies on diesel for 75 percent of its power, and residents put about 20 percent of their income toward buying it. That’s more than three times the average energy burden for low-income households nationwide. “We’re pretty much at the mercy of world markets,” Chad Nordlum, who is the energy project manager for the Native Village of Kotzebue, told Grist. “Right now, with the Iran war going on, the diesel prices are very high and we’re locked in to much higher prices than we’ve had in the past. There’s really nothing the community can do about diesel prices, but what we can do is produce our own energy.” That’s why Nordlum was so excited about a $20 million grant from the Environmental Protection Agency to support a wind energy project. The funding, announced in 2024, was part of a larger $150 million allocation for tribal infrastructure in Alaska. Nordlum says it would have lowered the community’s reliance on diesel to about 40 percent to 50 percent and given the tribe more control over energy and economic decisions. items.title: Corrigendum to “Clean energy for all? Mapping inequity potential in the clean energy transition in the United States” [Energy Res. Soc. Sci. 108, 103400, 2024]
Countering innocence: Teaching the justice in climate justice education with young learners
items.summary_raw: Early childhood education often frames climate change as too complex, political, or emotionally charged for young children, positioning them as “innocent” or incapable of engaging with environmental and social justice issues. Drawing on Critical Race Theory, this study examines climate justice education in early childhood, with particular attention to how dominant constructions of childhood innocence and race shape opportunities to engage young children in critical conversations about climate and environmental justice. We analyze one outdoor preschool teacher’s reflections on child-led discussions around environmental stewardship, care, and human impact with young children. Our findings reveal that there are many opportunities to discuss issues of power, harm, and justice within climate education that remain mostly missed. The analysis also illuminates how dominant discourses of innocence and apolitical pedagogy, alongside educator uncertainty and institutional conditions that shape their willingness and ability to navigate unfamiliar and uncomfortable topics. Implications include strengthening early childhood teacher education, supporting educators’ ethical reflection, and engaging families in developing approaches to environmental awareness and social responsibility in early childhood.

items.title: Climate Change or Mismanagement? Partisan Attribution and Public Support for Urban Wildfire Policy
items.summary_raw: Abstract This paper examines how Americans assign responsibility for the rising urban wildfire risk and how those judgments influence their support for pre- or post-disaster planning and policy. Urban wildfires are becoming more destructive because of a combination of factors including climate change, expansion of settlement into the wildland–urban interface, fuel accumulation from fire suppression policies, and the failure of older infrastructure. Using two surveys conducted in summer 2025, a national U.S. sample and a California-focused sample, the study investigates public perceptions of wildfire trends, attribution of causation to climate change versus government mismanagement, and support for related mitigation and adaptation policies. The results show broad agreement across partisan groups that urban wildfires are increasing in frequency and severity. However, much like the messaging from the media and partisan elites, Democrats were significantly more likely to attribute the increase primarily to climate change, while Republicans were more likely to emphasize poor government management of forests. Californians were more likely than national respondents to view both climate change and government mismanagement as contributing causes, suggesting that proximity to wildfire risk and prolonged media exposure may encourage more multifaceted understandings of wildfire causation. Beliefs about causation were strongly associated with policy preferences: attribution to climate…

items.title: Can digital infrastructure construction promote the synergy between pollution and carbon reduction? A quasi-natural experiment based on the “Broadband China” pilot policy
items.summary_raw: Abstract Digital infrastructure (DI) presents a critical opportunity for China to address the dual challenges of climate change and environmental pollution. In this study, we empirically investigate the effects and mechanisms of DI on the synergy between pollution and carbon reduction (SPCR) using balanced panel data from 273 Chinese cities during 2011–2023. The results reveal that DI significantly reduces CO 2 and SO 2 emissions, thereby promoting SPCR. The mechanism analysis shows that DI facilitates synergistic governance by limiting the entry of heavily polluting enterprises and increasing government expenditure on environmental protection. Heterogeneity analysis suggests that the synergistic effects of DI are more pronounced in cities with small and medium size, high digital innovation capacity, advanced economic development, and greater government digital attention. This study clarifies the micro- and macro-mechanisms through which DI empowers cities to achieve SPCR, and provides empirical evidence and policy implications for improving DI construction and promoting urban green transformation.

items.title: A place-based perspective on local wind energy acceptance: the role of place attachment, motivations, and social norms
items.summary_raw: Wind energy is widely supported, yet specific projects encounter local contestation. Moving beyond NIMBY-based interpretations, this research examined social acceptance of wind energy as a place-based and socially situated judgment. Across two Italian experimental studies, we tested whether making place attachment salient reduces acceptance of a proposed wind farm and whether environmental, economic, and social motivations relate to acceptance under different place and normative conditions. In Study 1 ( N = 491), participants evaluated a wind farm near either a personally meaningful natural place or a non-meaningful place. Place attachment salience reduced local acceptability and support, whereas general support for wind energy did not differ between conditions. Economic motivation was positively associated with acceptance in the low-salience condition, whereas the association between social motivation and acceptance did not differ significantly between conditions. In Study 2 ( N = 509), all participants evaluated a project in a high place-attachment context and received local descriptive norm information indicating low or high local support. The manipulation changed perceived local support but did not increase acceptance. More importantly, social motivation interacted with the local descriptive norm: it predicted acceptance when local support was low, but not when support was high, suggesting that community-oriented reasons may sustain acceptance when local consensus is…

items.title: Early childhood students perspective on climate change education and sustainability through the lens of critical and sustainability pedagogies
items.summary_raw: Climate change is recognised as a pressing global environmental challenge, disproportionately affecting children’s development, wellbeing, and rights. This study investigates final-year early childhood studies students’ perspectives on climate change education and sustainability in two national contexts, the United Kingdom and Hungary, which differ in the extent to which environmental and sustainability education is explicitly reflected in early childhood curriculum guidance. In England, while the Department for Education’s sustainability and climate change strategy recognises the importance of developing children’s understanding of nature, sustainability, and climate change, these themes are not explicitly identified as areas of learning within the Early Years Foundation Stage statutory framework. In contrast, Hungarian early years teacher education systematically integrates environmental pedagogy into professional training. Therefore, the aims of the study were to explore how early childhood studies students interpret their role in addressing climate change education and sustainability when working with children, how they perceive the curriculum, and develop pedagogical practices in climate change education they consider age-appropriate and meaningful. Across both contexts, students valued early engagement with climate awareness but highlighted challenges including lack of explicit awareness of the early childhood education workforce how to address children’s emotional…

items.title: Integrating solar photovoltaics in river basins: advancing water–energy–climate synergies for sustainable development goals
items.summary_raw: ABSTRACT The graph describes the framework for USPV siting in river basins, including site suitability analysis, scenario design for USPV plant selection, and economic and ecological outcomes assessment. Utility-scale solar photovoltaic (USPV) deployment in river basins involves critical trade-offs among technological feasibility, economic performance, and ecological conservation. This study proposes an integrated decision-making framework for USPV siting in the upper Jinsha River by incorporating multiple criteria under different priorities. Results show that economic-priority scenarios allocate more than two-thirds of the suitable development areas east of the river, with median economic costs of 0.33–0.34 CNY/kWh and ecological costs of 0.013 CNY/kWh. Conservation-priority scenarios shift 60% of the suitable development areas westward, increasing economic costs to 0.36 CNY/kWh while reducing ecological costs to 0.006–0.007 CNY/kWh. Although total land conversion areas remain comparable across scenarios, differences in land conversion types result in carbon emissions of 1.04–1.13 Mt CO2 under economic priorities and 0.46–0.53 Mt CO2 under conservation priorities. These findings support spatially differentiated USPV planning that contributes to sustainable development goals (SDGs), particularly SDG 7 (Affordable and Clean Energy), SDG 13 (Climate Action), and SDG 15 (Life on Land), while strengthening water–energy–climate synergies in river basins.

items.title: Climate Anxiety and Climate Change Perceptions in Malaysian Higher Education: Impacts on Emotion, Cognition, and Function

items.summary_raw: Objective: To assess the level of climate anxiety among International Islamic University Malaysia (IIUM) undergraduate students, describe associated negative thoughts and functional impacts, and examine differences by gender and faculty, as well as correlations among emotional, cognitive, and functional domains.Material and Methods: A cross-sectional online survey was conducted among IIUM undergraduate students (n=222) using an adapted version of the Climate Anxiety Questionnaire, with government-response items removed. The instrument assessed emotional responses, negative beliefs, and functional impacts. Data were analysed using descriptive and non-parametric statistics. Mann–Whitney U tests compared median domain scores by gender and faculty (health vs non-health), while Spearman correlation assessed associations among domains. Statistical significance was set at p-value<0.05.Results: Participants were predominantly female (77.9%) and from health-related faculties (64.9%). Emotional concern about climate change was high, with most respondents reporting moderate to extreme worry regarding its threat to people and the planet. Negative beliefs were common, particularly perceptions of a frightening future and collective failure to protect the environment. Functional impacts on daily activities were generally low to moderate. items.title: Navigating the science-policy interface: climate scientists' role conceptions and engagement practices
items.summary_raw: Effective climate change response requires constructive science-policy engagement, yet what role interpretations climate scientists hold at the science-policy interface, which factors shape these interpretations, and how they relate to actual communication behaviour remain empirically underexplored. We surveyed German climate scientists (N = 249) and identified five distinct profiles: Advocating Brokers, Engaged Advocates, Reserved Academics, Policy Advisors, and Traditional Academics. Notably, the latter group --- preferring detachment from societal and policy engagement --- represents only a small minority. These findings provide insights into the ways scientists navigate their engagement at the science-policy boundary, contributing to the ongoing discourse on scientific advocacy in post-normal science contexts.

items.title: Does the carbon emission trading scheme enhance enterprises’ green total factor productivity? Evidence from China
items.summary_raw: With growing global attention to climate change and sustainable development, the green and low-carbon transition has become a key pathway to advancing high-quality economic development. However, whether the carbon emission trading scheme can enhance enterprises’ green total factor productivity while simultaneously achieving emission reductions still requires further investigation. Utilizing relevant data of Chinese A-share listed companies spanning from 2011 to 2023, the present study conceptualizes the carbon emission trading scheme as a quasi-natural experiment and establishes a Difference-in-Differences (DID) model to scrutinize its impact on enterprises’ green total factor productivity (GTFP). The findings reveal that the carbon emission trading scheme notably elevates enterprises’ GTFP, with the outcomes retaining robustness even after addressing endogeneity concerns and conducting rigorous robustness checks. Mechanism tests elucidate that the carbon emission trading scheme primarily propels enterprises’ GTFP by alleviating financing constraints, curtailing agency costs, and promoting digital transformation. Moderating effect tests demonstrate that market competition plays a pivotal role in amplifying the positive influence of the carbon emission trading scheme on enterprises’ GTFP. Heterogeneity analysis suggests that the policy effects of the trading scheme are more noticeable among non-state-owned enterprises, pollution-intensive enterprises, and enterprises situated…

items.title: Coupled Geophysical and Technoeconomic Industrial Growth Constraints on Geological Carbon Storage Scale-Up: Application to UK Offshore Resources
items.summary_raw: Abstract Geological carbon dioxide storage is central to meeting many national climate change commitments, but large-scale deployment may be limited by both techno-economic rates of growth and physics-based processes imposed by subsurface geology. We develop a modeling framework for the assessment of feasible CO2 storage scale-up trajectories that unifies constraints arising from industrial rates of growth, dynamic injection rate limits from reservoir pressurization, and static maximum cumulative storage resource. We employ logistic and Gompertz models to represent policy-compliant deployment trajectories, parametrized by the total cumulative storage resource. We then use a simplified physics model to estimate the resulting regional subsurface pressurization along these trajectories. Growth curves where reservoir pressurization exceeds safe limits are updated by reducing the static storage resource until residing in the safe deployment range. The result is both a growth trajectory and static storage resource achievable subject to injectivity limits. Applying the framework to the United Kingdom (UK), we find that offshore storage resources are sufficient to accommodate all government midcentury deployment rate scenarios up to 175 Mt yr–1. Cumulative storage of up to 78 Gt, representing a reference estimate of the UK storage resource base used in national planning, can be achieved under Gompertz growth trajectories. The more aggressive logistic trajectories are constrained by…

items.title: Towards a green China: energy policy, technological innovation, and green investment as drivers of environmental sustainability
items.summary_raw: China’s pursuit of environmental sustainability has become one of the defining policy experiments of the twenty-first century, combining an ambitious dual-carbon pledge with the world’s largest deployment of clean-energy technology and green capital. This review synthesizes recent scholarship to examine how three interlocking levers, energy and climate policy, technological innovation, and green investment, jointly shape China’s transition toward a lower-carbon and more resilient development path. Drawing on a structured reading of peer-reviewed research published predominantly between 2019 and 2025, the article develops an integrated framework in which policy sets direction and incentives, innovation lowers the cost and expands the frontier of abatement, and investment mobilizes the capital required to translate intent into installed capacity. The evidence indicates that target-based governance, embodied in successive Five-Year Plans and the 2030/2060 carbon commitments, has been reinforced by market-based instruments such as the national emissions trading system, and by an expanding architecture of green credit and green bonds. Technological progress in solar photovoltaics, wind power, batteries, and electric mobility has driven steep learning curves, allowing renewable additions to exceed fossil capacity additions by wide margins in recent years. Feeding the future with clean energy: poultry farmers’ adoption of renewables
items.summary_raw: Renewable energy is essential for mitigating climate change, reducing greenhouse gas emissions, and strengthening energy security and promoting sustainable development. As an energy-intensive sector, poultry farming must shift from fossil fuels to renewable energy to meet current and future energy demands. This study employed a quantitative, cross-sectional survey to examine factors influencing poultry farmers’ intentions to adopt renewable energy in Bushehr Province, Iran. This study integrates the Technology Acceptance Model (TAM) and the Theory of Planned Behavior (TPB), with TAM explaining attitudes through perceived usefulness and perceived ease of use, and TPB explains intention through attitude, subjective norms, and Perceived behavioral control. Structural equation modeling using maximum likelihood estimation in AMOS showed that perceived usefulness, attitude, and perceived behavioral control significantly and positively influence farmers’ adoption intentions. Perceived ease of use also positively affects perceived usefulness, which in turn shapes attitudes toward renewable energy. These findings highlight the need to increase awareness of the benefits and efficiency of renewable technologies in poultry farming, provide financial support for high-cost technologies through national and international funding schemes, and encourage future research that incorporating value-based theoretical models.

items.title: Impact of Policies on the Development of Geothermal Industry in China: An Empirical Analysis of Panel Data
items.summary_raw: ABSTRACT Geothermal energy is a clean, low‐carbon, widely distributed, abundant, safe and high‐quality renewable energy. According to a survey of China's geothermal resources, China's annual recoverable geothermal energy resources are equivalent to 2.6 billion tons of standard coal and thus have great development and utilization potential. Using geothermal energy to realize clean heating is highly important for achieving the goals of peak carbon and carbon neutrality. Financial subsidies and tax incentives support the geothermal industry, increase additional income for geothermal enterprises, encourage enterprises to invest more in scientific and technological research and development of the geothermal industry and expand the scale of reproduction to promote the large‐scale sustainable development of the geothermal industry. However, existing policies have difficulty meeting the larger, more efficient and high‐quality development needs of geothermal energy. This paper selects geothermal industry enterprises listed on domestic stock exchanges from 2004 to 2021 as research samples, and it uses panel data to evaluate the implementation effect of geothermal fiscal and tax policies. This research reveals that direct government subsidies significantly enhance the technological capabilities of these enterprises by fostering patent output and driving technological innovation, positively affecting the sector's advancement. In contrast, both corporate income tax and value‐added tax…

items.title: Towards Digital Transformation: The Role of Digital Literacy and Behavioral Drivers in Embracing E-Business Solutions among Microfinance Institutions
items.summary_raw: Digital literacy (DL) is a critical determinant of individual intentions toward adoption of technology in the digital era. However, scholarly research on the role of DL in shaping individual behavior toward the intention to embrace Electronic Business Solutions (EBS) within microfinance institutions (MFIs) remains limited. This study seeks to extend the Theory of Planned Behavior (TPB) by integrating the Diffusion of Innovation (DOI) Theory to develop a novel framework (DOI-TPB) for understanding the role of DL in shaping individual behavior regarding the intention to adopt EBS. The study examines this relationship among 229 respondents from MFIs in Mwanza, Tanzania, with data collected via self-administered questionnaires distributed through Google Forms. Employing structural equation modeling (SEM), the empirical findings indicate that DL positively and significantly strengthens therelationships between the three core TPB components: attitude, subjective norms, perceived behavioral control, and the intention to embrace EBS. The extended DOI-TPB model demonstrates that DL not only influences these TPB constructs but also enhances the model’s overall explanatory power. The study concludes by offering practical recommendations for strategically promoting DL within the financial sector to facilitate more effective adoption of EBS.Keywords: Digital Transformation, Digital Literacy, Behavior Drivers, Microfinance Institutions, E-business Solutions

items.title: Bridging the Attitude-Behaviour Gap in Biobased Product Consumption: A Comprehensive Behavioural Decision Model
items.summary_raw: Market acceptance of biobased products is essential for advancing a sustainable bioeconomy, yet consumer decision-making remains complex and insufficiently understood. This study introduces and validates the Comprehensive Behavioural Decision Model for Biobased Products (CBDM-BBP), designed to bridge the gap between consumer attitudes and actual use behaviour. The model integrates cognitive, affective, and conative dimensions while accounting for internal and external influences such as self-interest, altruism, and contextual factors. Using survey data from 525 consumers in the Republic of Ireland, a country with strong bioeconomy ambitions and policy support for biobased innovation, we applied Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modelling (PLS-SEM) to evaluate the framework. Results demonstrate that CBDM-BBP outperforms individual theoretical models in explaining use behaviour, offering strong predictive capability. These findings suggest that consumer use behaviour of biobased products cannot be adequately explained through isolated behavioural mechanisms but instead arises from the interaction of multiple psychological and contextual influences. The CBDM-BBP provides an empirically validated framework for capturing this complexity, offering a more comprehensive basis for understanding consumer behaviour in the bioeconomy.

Wind energy acceptance and forest owners’ land-leasing intentions: The role of beliefs and attitudes
items.summary_raw: The expansion of wind power plays a crucial role in the European Union's decarbonization strategy. However, the social acceptance of wind power projects, particularly among landowners and non-landowners, remains a significant concern. Drawing on behavioural insights of the social acceptance literature, this study examines the beliefs, attitudes, and behavioural intentions of these groups towards wind power. We focus on the national context of Finland, where wind energy development has accelerated in recent years. Utilizing survey data from 2,103 respondents, including forest owners and non-forest owners, the study employs Structural Equation Modelling (SEM) and regression models to explore how beliefs shape attitudes, policy support and forest owners' behavioural intentions. The acceptance measures indicate that non-forest owners held more favourable attitudes towards wind power, associating it with environmental benefits and economic opportunities, while forest owners expressed greater concerns about landscape changes, land ownership, and economic impacts. The SEM model reveals that attitudes toward wind power were strongly influenced by beliefs about energy production and local impacts, which, in turn, shaped policy support. Additionally, forest owners’ willingness to lease land for wind turbines was associated with higher income level, owned land area size, and positive attitudes towards wind power. items.title: Nationalist frames erode opposition to violent hate crimes
items.summary_raw: Abstract Public opinion of hate crimes may be malleable because these acts are understood through victims' varying social identities. We investigate whether violent attacks provoke different reactions when framed around victims' national rather than religious identities. We first document media coverage of hate crimes, showing that more than 20% of headlines about anti-Jewish hate crimes use nationalist frames, invoking Israel. We then analyze discourse surrounding a high-profile anti-Jewish attack and demonstrate the prominence of nationalist framing. In two survey experiments with U.S. adults, we show widespread aversion to religiously motivated violence, but greater ambivalence toward attacks motivated by nationalism. Specifically, opposition to physically violent attacks against Jews weakens when framed through the victim's support for Israel rather than their religious identification. Similarly, opposition to attacks on Muslims and Hindus declines when linked to Palestinian and Indian nationalism, respectively. While Americans display near-universal opposition to religious bigotry, nationalist frames erode public condemnation of identity-based violence.

items.title: Bibliometric and bibliographic review of sewage sludge by pyrolysis
items.summary_raw: The growing global generation of sewage sludge, estimated at approximately 200 million tons per year, has intensified the need for sustainable and efficient management strategies. In this context, emerging trends point to a transition from conventional waste treatment to integrated resource recovery systems. Accordingly, pyrolysis has emerged as a promising thermochemical route for converting sewage sludge into value-added products while minimizing environmental impacts. Recent advances demonstrate that pyrolysis enables the recovery of key resources in the form of biochar, bio-oil, and non-condensable gases, depending on operating conditions, particularly temperature (400–700 °C). Biochar, typically containing more than 50 wt.% carbon and exhibiting high surface area, has gained attention for applications in soil amendment, carbon sequestration, and as a functional material for adsorption and catalysis. Bio-oil, with a calorific value ranging from 15 to 25 MJ·kg −1 , is being explored as a renewable energy carrier and chemical feedstock, while non-condensable gases (e.g., CO, CO 2 , CH 4 , H 2 ) enable partial energy self-sufficiency of the process. However, challenges remain regarding contaminant management (e.g., heavy metals), product standardization, and process scale-up.
